attorneys.name: Emily Temple Abels
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning and Estate Administration Lawyers in Kennett Square, PA
attorneys.bio:
Founded in 1946, Larmore Scarlett is the oldest, continuously operating law firm in Kennett Square, Pennsylvania.

Emily joined Larmore Scarlett in 2019 after nearly four years in Philadelphia as a child advocate attorney. Born and raised in Chester County, Emily was eager to join a small firm to be able to live, work, and contribute to the vibrant community in Chester County. She became a lawyer to help families and individuals solve problems, and to advocate for them. Her practice at Larmore Scarlett focuses on estate planning, including wills, trusts, powers of attorney for financial and health care, and advance directives. Larmore Scarlett approaches estate planning on a client-by-client basis, with each client having the opportunity to create an estate plan tailored to their specific goals, financial needs, and family structure. While estate planning is a significant focus of Emily's practice area, she also works in business formation and commercial law, business contracts, real estate, land use, and Orphans' Court or probate court litigation focused on estate and guardianship matters.

attorneys.name: Michael J. Alivernini
attorneys.practice_type: Casual & Premises Liability Defense Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Michael J. Alivernini is a Partner in Chartwell's Philadelphia office. He is a graduate of Villanova University and Widener University School of Law. Mr. Alivernini is admitted to the Pennsylvania, New Jersey and District of Columbia Bars, the United States District Court of the Eastern District of Pennsylvania, the United States District Court for the Middle District of Pennsylvania and the United States District Court for the District of New Jersey. He is a member of the Pennsylvania Bar Association. Mr. Alivernini is co-author of an article entitled: Do Pennsylvania Lawyers Have an Ethical Duty to Advise Clients about ADR?

Mr. Alivernini practices in the areas of property, general liability and automobile liability defense; subrogation/recovery; surety and fidelity litigation; and first party property insurance coverage. Mr. Alivernini has represented clients in large loss property subrogation matters in which he has negotiated substantial recoveries and participated in numerous jury trials in securing favorable jury verdicts. In addition he has successfully defended his clients in personal injury and wrongful death claims arising out of premises liability and motor vehicle accidents. In 2010 and 2012, Mr. Alivernini was selected as a rising star in Philadelphia Magazine "Pennsylvania Super Lawyer - Rising Stars," a listing which includes the top 2.5 percent of attorneys in the Commonwealth who are 40 years of age or younger or have been practicing for less than 10 years.

attorneys.name: Chari M. Alson ESQ, CELA
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Media, PA
attorneys.bio:
Chari M. Alson, is a Certified Elder Law Attorney and Partner with Anderson Elder Law. Chari has been practicing in the areas of estate planning, estate and trust administration, and elder law in Pennsylvania since 2003.

Chari is an officer of the Pennsylvania Bar Association Elder Law Section, is a board member of the Pennsylvania Association of Elder Law Attorneys (PAELA) and serves on its Public Policy Committee, is the Co-Chair of the Elder Law Committee of the Delaware County Bar Association, is a board member of the Chester County Estate Planning Council and is a member of the NAELA News Editorial Board. She is a co-Editor the Delaware County Elder Law Handbook and Resource Guide (7th and 8th editions), and was a contributing author to Elder Law in Pennsylvania, Chapter 3, Planning for Incapacity–Financial Issues (5th ed. PBI Press).

Chari is a frequent lecturer for the Pennsylvania Bar Institute in the areas of Elder Law and Estate Planning and has also presented to other professional education seminars and community groups. Chari is a member of the Pennsylvania Academy of Elder Law Attorneys and the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys.

Chari earned her juris doctor degree from Temple University, her Master’s in Public Health and Gerontology Certificate from Boston University School of Public Health, and her Bachelor of Arts from Rutgers University–New Brunswick. She lives in Garnet Valley with her two daughters.

attorneys.name: James J. Amato
attorneys.practice_type: Car Crashes Lawyers in Pottsville, PA
attorneys.bio:
Jim is a partner in the law firm of Fanelli, Evans & Patel, P.C.

Jim is a 1999 graduate of Shenandoah Valley Jr./Sr. High School. Jim earned his Bachelor of Science Degree in Finance from the Pennsylvania State University. Jim went on to earn his law degree from the Pennsylvania State University Dickinson School of Law. While in law school, Jim served as a judicial intern for The Honorable John F. Cherry of the Dauphin County Court of Common Pleas. Jim also interned for the Office of General Counsel under Governor Edward G. Rendell.

Prior to joining Fanelli, Evans, & Patel, P.C., Jim worked for two well-regarded Center City Philadelphia law firms where he devoted his practice to representing insurance companies, contractors and corporate entities in complex civil matters. While in Philadelphia, Jim litigated numerous claims at the municipal, arbitration and trial court levels in Pennsylvania and New Jersey. Jim served as a certified Arbitrator for the Court of Common Pleas Philadelphia Compulsory Arbitration program. Jim also served as a mediator for the Philadelphia Court of Common Pleas Mediation/Dispute Resolution Program.

In 2015, Jim returned to Schuylkill County to join the Firm. Jim dedicates his practice to representing the rights of injured victims in a variety of civil matters. Upon Jim joining the firm Jim secured a verdict of $512,000 in a trip and fall case in Luzurne County where the defense refused to acknowledge fault or make a reasonable offer to compensate the client for his injuries. During his time with the firm, Jim has successfully recovered millions of dollars for clients that suffered catastrophic injuries or death as a result of motor vehicle, construction, dram shop, premises liability, medical malpractice and work related accidents.

Jim is also very active in his community. In addition to his legal practice, Jim is a board member of the Schuylkill Economic Development Corporation, an entity dedicated to stimulating and improving economic development in Schuylkill County. Jim serves as the Solicitor for West Mahanoy Township Board of Supervisors and the Girardville Area Municipal Authority. Jim also coordinates the Firm’s annual holiday Bike Give-Away event. The event was created as a way for the Firm to give back to the people of Schuylkill County by giving children in the community bikes and helmets. Jim is also a member of the Schuylkill County Civil Rules Committee and Schuylkill County Bench Bar Committee.

Jim is admitted to practice before all courts in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania and the State of New Jersey. He is also admitted to the United States Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit, the United States District Court for the Eastern and Middle Districts of Pennsylvania and the United States District Court of New Jersey.

attorneys.name: Linda M. Anderson Esq, LLM, CELA
attorneys.practice_type: Elder Law Lawyers in Media, PA
attorneys.bio:
Linda Anderson has over 36 years of experience in the elder law field. She is also a Certified Elder Law Attorney, as conferred by the National Elder Law Foundation and authorized by the Pennsylvania Supreme Court.

Linda Anderson is an active and distinguished member of her evolving field. She is an accredited attorney with the Department of Veteran Affairs as well as a Charter Member of the Life Care Planning Law Firms Association and a long-time member of the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys. In addition, she is an invited member of the Special Needs Alliance, which distinguishes lawyers with dedication and skill in aiding special needs clients while also serving the wider community of disabled individuals and their families through local, state, and national organizations.

Linda Anderson is a past President of PAELA (Pennsylvania Association of Elder Law Attorneys (2018-2019)) and has served as Chair of the Pennsylvania Bar Association Elder Law Section (2009) and as Co-Chair of the Delaware County Bar Association’s Elder Law Committee (2004-2018). Ms. Anderson has been recognized as a Pennsylvania Super Lawyer® in the field of Elder Law since 2004, and repeatedly as one of the Top 100 Lawyers in Pennsylvania and as a Top 50 Women Lawyers in Pennsylvania. She was awarded the 2012 PAELA Member of the Year Award and Anderson Elder Law has been distinguished by U.S. News and World Report as one of the top law firms in the country and she has been selected for Best Lawyers in America. Ms. Anderson also received the prestigious AV® rating from Martindale Hubbell and is a Fellow of ACTEC (The American College of Trust and Estate Counsel).

Linda Anderson not only volunteers with community and professional groups to share her knowledge but is also a regular faculty member and course planner for the Pennsylvania Bar Association in areas of elder law, estate planning, long-term care planning, special needs planning, and veterans’ benefits. She received her bachelor’s degree from Sarah Lawrence College, has a master’s degree in Taxation from Villanova University, and graduated from the University of San Francisco School of Law.

attorneys.name: Maureen L. Anderson
attorneys.firm_name: Maureen L. Anderson Elder Law, LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Doylestown, PA
attorneys.bio:
Background

From an early age, Maureen had an interest in the law and planned to become an attorney. Consistently throughout her lifetime, she has advocated for those who need help and protection. While growing up, Maureen always cared for and respected seniors, whether they were family members, neighbors, or any other members of the older population that she encountered. She revered her elders and appreciated all of the things she learned from their wisdom and experience. The law gave Maureen the ability to merge her two passions of practicing law and caring for seniors into her destined career as an Elder Law Attorney.

Maureen is a Philadelphia native who earned her Bachelor's Degree (B.A., Politics) and Master's Degree (M.S., Criminal Justice) from St. Joseph's University. She later earned her Juris Doctorate Degree from the University of the District of Columbia in Washington D.C. She began her career as an advocate for crime victims in the Philadelphia District Attorney's Office. While attending law school, she worked on state and federal legislation that included protection and advocacy for senior citizens.

Her education and experience laid the foundation for her desire to pursue a career in Elder Law. In addition to the knowledge required, Maureen's true compassion and sensitivity to the needs of seniors and their families allows her to provide the best service to her clients. She understands the challenges and feelings of being overwhelmed that seniors may encounter. Her caring and personal approach helps her clients navigate through those difficult situations.

Having practiced elder law for over 20 years, Maureen is knowledgeable, experienced and an expert in her chosen field. She is Certified Elder Law Attorney ("CELA") having been certified by the National Elder Law Foundation which is accredited by the American Bar Association and authorized by the Pennsylvania Supreme Court to certify elder law attorneys. Additionally, Maureen's expertise has been recognized by her peers with the distinction of "Super Lawyer".

She is a member of the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys ("NAELA") and the Pennsylvania Association of Elder Law Attorneys ("PAELA"). Maureen is active in the Bucks County Bar Association, where she has served as a Board Member, and the Pennsylvania Bar Association.

Maureen is licensed to practice law in Pennsylvania and New Jersey. She focuses her practice in the Philadelphia region, including Bucks County, Montgomery County, Philadelphia, and other surrounding areas.

attorneys.name: Benjamin D. Andreozzi Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Sexual Abuse Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Ben Andreozzi has dedicated his career to representing survivors of child sexual abuse in civil cases. Ben has represented hundreds of clients across the country in some of the nation's most high-profile sexual abuse cases, including many of Jerry Sandusky's victims and dozens of Catholic clergy victims, to name just a few.

Ben regularly appears in the media, including on the Today Show, Good Morning America, NBC Nightly News, ABC World News, CBS Evening News, Anderson Cooper, and in the New York Times, USA Today, and many others. Ben also teaches other lawyers across the country on handling child sexual abuse and crime victim cases.

Along with co-counsel Nathaniel Foote, Ben obtained a record $88 million-dollar jury verdict for a young sexual abuse victim. He has also received significant noneconomic results for clients and takes pride in forcing institutions to change their operations to better protect children in the future. Ben believes each survivor's path to recovery is unique, so he gets to know each client and maintains communication throughout their case.

Ben is admitted to practice in Arizona, all Pennsylvania state and federal courts, and practices across the country through associations with local counsel. He is a member of the National Crime Victim Bar Association Advisory Board, the Pennsylvania Association of Justice, Million and Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Club, and other local bar associations.

Ben enjoys spending his free time with his wife, Ciara, and three young children, Rocco, Cecilia, and Anthony.

attorneys.name: Robert S. Andrews Jr. Esquire
attorneys.firm_name: Robert S. Andrews, Jr. Attorney at Law
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Cranberry Township, PA
attorneys.bio:
I was born and raised in Tire Hill, a small coal mining community outside Johnstown, Pa. I graduated from Conemaugh Township High School and then attended the Indiana University of Pennsylvania, graduating in 1986 with a Bachelor of Arts degree in political science and a pre-law minor. In 1990, I graduated from the University of Toledo School of Law and passed the Pennsylvania bar examination.

I began my legal career in January 1991 with the Pennsylvania Office of the Attorney General. I served as a senior deputy Attorney General for the state of Pennsylvania and retired in 2003. While working at the Attorney General's office, I served under Attorney Generals Tom Corbett, who subsequently was elected Governor of Pennsylvania, and Mike Fisher, who subsequently was appointed as a Judge to the United States 3rd Circuit Court of Appeals. For the past 17 years, I have been in the private practice of law, which included nearly five years as a partner with Meyer, Darragh, Buckler, Bebenek & Eck. During both my time at the Attorney General's office and in private practice, I have handled various cases and have litigated numerous criminal and civil cases across the Commonwealth.

attorneys.name: O. Daniel Ansa
attorneys.practice_type: National Trial Practice Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Ansa has a diversified civil trial practice, with a particular emphasis on transportation, products liability, commercial disputes and tort litigation. He has also handled employment discrimination litigation, environmental abatement actions, class actions, construction disputes and mass tort.

The majority of his practice involves the representation of Fortune 500 and international companies involved in transportation, products liability, catastrophic personal injury and property tort matters and commercial litigation. He is frequently retained to assume lead role in high exposure cases on the eve of trial.

He serves as national coordinating counsel for an international package delivery company. As national counsel, he actively litigates cases venued throughout the United States, manages a network of local counsel and oversees a rapid response team consisting of attorneys and retained consultants whose mission is to triage and manage catastrophic events. He also serves as regional counsel for an international manufacturer of vertical transportation equipment.

He has defended the design and manufacture of many products produced by his clients including: automobiles, tractors, trains, elevators, escalators, power walks, motorcycles, personal water craft, ATVs, vibratory compactors, heavy and light industrial vehicles, construction equipment, mining equipment, power tools, milling machinery, steel fabricating systems and equipment, firearms, anti-lock braking and conventional braking systems, tractor-trailer air brake systems, seat belt assemblies, air bags, flex fans, consumer products, snow throwers, bicycles, helmets, locks, door closers, pneumatic, hydraulic and mechanical controls, press machines, paper mill machines, boilers, fire cause and origin cases, chemicals, and multiple chemical sensitivity cases. As an associate, he served as a member of a national trial team for an automotive component manufacturer.

Mr. Ansa is a graduate of the Naval Justice School and is a retired Lieutenant Colonel in the United States Marine Corps Reserve. He held a reserve billet in the office of the Chief Defense Counsel of the Marine Corps, was a member of the Marine Corps Trial Advocacy Team and lectured nationally and internationally on trial practice. Mr. Ansa has lectured in Europe, Africa and Asia as an adjunct faculty member of the Defense Institute for International Legal Studies. He has served as a guest lecturer on products liability at the Wharton School and on trial practice at Villanova University, has conducted in-house seminars for corporate legal departments and has participated in panel discussions at client legal symposiums. He has also written extensively on products liability, rules of evidence and construction disputes.

Mr. Ansa is a member of the following bars: Pennsylvania, United States Court of Military Appeals, U.S. District Court, Eastern District of Pennsylvania, Third Circuit Court of Appeals, United States Supreme Court, U.S. District Court, Western District of Pennsylvania, New York, U.S. District Court, Northern District of Texas, Texas, Fourth Circuit Court of Appeals, and Colorado.

attorneys.name: Steven E. Angstreich
attorneys.practice_type: Sophisticated Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Steven is a co-founder of the firm, its managing shareholder and Chair of the firm's Commercial and Environmental section.

He actively engages in the litigation of sophisticated and complex individual and class action cases. He has successfully handled numerous class actions in the fields of securities, antitrust, consumer fraud, toxic exposure, breach of fiduciary duty, waste and mismanagement, and land fraud.

A lecturer in the areas of toxic tort, environmental law, and legal malpractice, he is often called to be an expert witness retained by both plaintiffs and defendants in the field of legal malpractice. As part of his practice, Steven serves as a mediator and arbitrator in complex alternative dispute resolution efforts and is active as an arbitrator on behalf of the United States District Court for the District of New Jersey.

Born in the Bronx, NY, Steven attended the University of Pennsylvania, receiving a B.S. in Economics in 1967. He received his J.D., with honors, from Temple University School of Law in 1970 where he was a member of the Law Review.

Steven is admitted to the Pennsylvania and U.S. District Court, Eastern District of Pennsylvania Bar; the U.S. Court of Appeals, Third Circuit; and the U.S. Supreme Court. attorneys.name: Michael H. Applebaum
attorneys.practice_type: DUI/DWI Lawyers in Bensalem, PA
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Michael H. Applebaum has tried hundreds of cases and represented thousands of clients in his nearly 37 years of practicing law in Pennsylvania. His professionalism, conversational style, statesmanlike honesty and tenacious trial methods have earned him the respect of Judges, jurors, clients, associates, and the community as a whole.

Perhaps one of the most difficult and best known cases in which Michael H. Applebaum was involved was the murder of a Philadelphia teenager named Eddie Polec on November 11, 1994 about which the book In Eddie's Name: One Family's Triumph over Tragedy was written.

In 1960, entered Temple University in Philadelphia, working his way through undergraduate school as a longshoreman on the docks of Philadelphia.

In 1964, Michael H. Applebaum graduated from Temple University with a B.S. in Accounting with a Minor in Journalism and Communications. While at Temple, Michael H. Applebaum served as the Press Secretary for the Temple University Newspaper.

After Temple, Michael H. Applebaum received a full scholarship to the prestigious Louis D. Brandeis School of Law at the University of Louisville (considered by many legal scholars to be the Harvard of the South). At law school, he was a member of the much esteemed Law Review and graduated in the top 10% of his class in 1967 earning a Juris Doctor degree. He also served as Chairman of the Law Student Civil Rights Counsel which was involved with protecting the rights of minorities and ensuring that they were not singled out and persecuted because of their race, color or creed. Additionally, the counsel was responsible for organizing many of Dr. Martin Luther King's speaking engagements to The Brandeis School of Law.

In 1967, Michael H. Applebaum was accepted to the University of Cambridge, in the United Kingdom, as an International Exchange Scholar at one of the oldest and most renowned colleges in the world, Cambridge's Clare College which was founded in 1326.

A sudden family illness made it impossible for Michael H. Applebaum to continue his studies overseas at Cambridge. He then entered the one year program Masters of Taxation at New York University (NYU) in 1967.

In 1968, Michael H. Applebaum returned to Philadelphia and successfully completed the Pennsylvania Bar Exam after which he began practicing law in Pennsylvania.

Over the last 37 years, Michael H. Applebaum has built the powerful practice, Applebaum and Associates. The practice has five offices with a team of strong associates and very skilled paralegals. Applebaum and Associates are trial lawyers who represent their clients' interests daily in court.

One of the most distinguishing characteristics of Michael H. Applebaum's approach to representing his clients can be summed up by this quote after he was asked "What is the hardest aspect of having practiced law all these years?" Michael H. Applebaum replied; "Each trial is like my first, I don't sleep well at night, even now after all these years, when I have a trial in the morning. It's a huge responsibility to have my clients' futures in my hands and I always prepare the best possible case to ensure the best possible outcome for them (my clients) and their families."

attorneys.name: Sierra S. Applegate
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Sierra is a dedicated professional with a service-oriented approach to her Trusts and Estates practice. She is an enthusiastic problem solver with experience in navigating complex legal issues, assessing liabilities and risks, and providing thoughtful guidance to ensure the best possible outcomes.

Sierra is as an Associate Attorney in the firm and focuses on estate planning and estate administration. Prior to joining the firm, Sierra worked as a Deputy City Solicitor for the City of Philadelphia Law Department in the Real Estate and Economic Development Unit, handling complex real estate transactions and charitable trust matters. Previously, she worked as an Associate Attorney at Kleinbard, LLC, in the Business and Finance Department, as a member of the Firm’s Trusts and Estates Group.

Before joining Kleinbard, Sierra clerked in the Orphans’ Court Division of the Philadelphia Court of Common Pleas for the Honorable Sheila Woods-Skipper. While working as a law clerk, she served as a volunteer attorney for Philadelphia VIP, representing tenants at eviction hearings in Municipal Court. Sierra continues to serve as a probono counsel for Philadelphia VIP on a range of legal matters, including estate planning, tangled title, and deed transfers.

Sierra is an active board leader, who brings a deep commitment to public service to her board leadership. Currently, she serves on the Board of Directors for Senior Law Center. Also, she serves as Recording Secretary on the Executive Board of the Barristers' Association of Philadelphia. Sierra also serves as Treasurer on the Executive Board of the National Bar Association Women Lawyers Division.

Bryan Arce is a Managing Partner at Phillips & Associates | Sexual Harassment, Discrimination & Employment Lawyers. His main area of focus is Employment Law, specifically harassment and other misconduct, such as wage and hour violations. He is currently admitted to practice in New York, New Jersey, Washington, D.C. Pennsylvania, the Southern District of New York, the Eastern District of New York, the District of New Jersey, the Eastern District of Pennsylvania, the Western District of Pennsylvania, and the Second Circuit. He is fluent in Spanish and German.

attorneys.practice_type: Arbitration Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Areman is a partner at the firm of Markowitz and Richman. His practice focuses on the representation of public and private sector labor unions, benefit funds and individual employees. Mr. Areman specializes in grievance arbitration, interest arbitration, unfair labor practices, disciplinary matters, civil rights litigation, pension disputes, ERISA matters and workers’ compensation.

Mr. Areman serves as Labor Counsel to the New Jersey State Lodge of the Fraternal Order of Police and the Fraternal Order of Police, New Jersey Labor Council. He also represents employees and their unions in the public safety, healthcare, construction, trucking and service industries. He is admitted to practice in Pennsylvania and New Jersey; the United States District Courts for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania and the District of New Jersey; and the United States Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit.

Prior to joining Markowitz and Richman, Mr. Areman served as National Negotiator for the National Treasury Employees Union in Washington, DC. Mr. Areman also previously worked in the legal departments of the International Brotherhood of Teamsters and the American Federation of Teachers, both in Washington, DC. Mr. Areman received his undergraduate degree from Hamilton College in 1996 and his law degree from the George Washington University National Law Center in 2003.

Mr. Areman is active as a volunteer in his neighborhood and with local youth sports. In November 2019, Mr. Areman was elected to serve his community as Cheltenham Township Commissioner.

attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
Jonathan C. Ascher received his Doctor of Jurisprudence from Drake University School of Law. He received his Bachelor of Arts from the University of Pittsburgh, where he placed on the Dean’s List, was awarded the Robert Murphy Academic Scholarship, and was selected to the Big East All-Academic Team in soccer. He is admitted to practice law in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania and the State of Iowa.

His practice is focused in the areas of workers’ compensation and occupational disease litigation. This includes the successful representation of numerous employers, including commercial retailers, moving companies, trucking companies, school districts, local municipalities, health-care providers, construction companies, and both small and large corporate entities. Mr. Ascher practices before Workers’ Compensation Judges throughout western Pennsylvania, the Workers’ Compensation Appeal Board and Commonwealth Court of Pennsylvania.

Mr. Ascher frequently lectures on workers’ compensation topics to insurance companies, third party administrators, and employers. He counsels employers on risk management issues that assists them in handling and defending their workers’ compensation cases.

He was acknowledged by Law & Politics and the Philadelphia Magazine as a Rising Star Super Lawyer in 2005, 2006, 2007 and 2008. From 2010-2019, Mr. Ascher was named by his peers as a Pennsylvania Super Lawyer as published by American Lawyer Media and Philadelphia Magazine. The Best Lawyers in America, a highly respected national peer-review publication, selected Mr. Ascher for inclusion in its most recent 2020 Edition in the category of Workers’ Compensation Law (Employers).

attorneys.name: Julie A. Auerbach
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Julie A. Auerbach is a partner at Astor Weiss Kaplan & Mandel, LLP and has been with the firm since 2001. Her practice is exclusively focused on family law where she handles issues relating to complex divorces, child custody, child and spousal support, prenuptial agreements, same sex family law and protection from abuse. She practices in Philadelphia, Delaware, Chester, Bucks and Montgomery counties. She is a member of the American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers, a national organization of prominent family law lawyers. She serves on the legislation committee as well as the committee for the bi-annual nationally recognized Journal of the American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers.

Julie frequently lectures on family law related topics, including for the Pennsylvania Bar Institute and the National Business Institute. She has written extensively on family law issues with articles appearing in the Legal Intelligencer, the Philadelphia Bar Association Reporter and the Pennsylvania Family Law Reporter. Julie has an AV rating from Martindale-Hubbell.

Julie is actively involved in non-profit activities. She has been a board member of the Supportive Older Women's Network since 2005 which provides support for older women, including grandparent resources. She has been an attorney affiliate for the Women's Resource Center in Wayne since 2002, where she volunteers regularly for the legal night program that provides free 30 minute consultations for women with family law related issues.

When Julie is not working she enjoys biking, cooking, pickleball and spending time with her husband and children.

attorneys.name: Leon Aussprung
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Leon Aussprung, M.D., J.D., LL.M practices in the area of catastrophic injury litigation, including medical malpractice, product liability, and other complex personal injury cases. Additionally, he represents qui tam Relators in health care fraud and abuse litigation.

Shortly after joining Kline & Specter in January 2001, Dr. Aussprung worked with Tom Kline in the Matteo case, a complex case that involved the death of Suzanne Wester Matteo, who suffered internal bleeding following a routine medical procedure. Her doctors did not notice the bleeding nor did they act to help her. Suzanne’s husband, Tony Matteo, performed emergency surgery and saved his wife’s life, but days later she suffered respiratory arrest. Tony Matteo sued his late wife’s doctors and a jury returned a $25 million verdict in his favor.

In March 2006, Dr. Aussprung was co-counsel in a case in which a woman died after an elective bowel resection due to a bowel perforation and sepsis because her surgeon failed to timely diagnose the problem. The trial resulted in a jury verdict of nearly $2.7 million, which was the largest verdict ever in a death case in Lackawanna County. (See the Hook case.)

Dr. Aussprung has handled a multitude of medical malpractice suits with Kline & Specter, many of them resulting in substantial settlements. In two cases against Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, settlements were reached in suits in which children died, one a five-year-old boy who was over-transfused during a surgery and the other a two-month-old infant whose infection following surgery was never properly diagnosed.

Among Dr. Aussprung’s other cases that produced substantial settlements was that of a teenager who had been severely brain injured at three years of age when his diabetes mellitus was not

properly managed. In yet another case, he helped win a settlement for a baby who was brain injured after getting improper care during delivery by a nurse midwife.

Dr. Aussprung earned his B.A. degree from the University of Virginia in 1987, his M.D. degree from Jefferson Medical College in 1991, and his J.D. from the University of Pennsylvania Law School in 1997. In 2006 he received an LL.M. in Trial Advocacy, with honors, from Temple University Beasley School of Law.

Dr. Aussprung is a member of the Pennsylvania Bar Association and has been admitted to practice law by the Supreme Court of Pennsylvania, the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania and the U.S. Court of Appeals, Third Circuit.

Dr. Aussprung received residency training in pediatrics at the Medical Center of Delaware and Thomas Jefferson University and has been board certified in pediatrics since 1994. Before becoming a practicing attorney, Dr. Aussprung was a pediatrician at duPont Hospital for Children and Thomas Jefferson University.

Dr. Aussprung’s areas of interest include medical malpractice, complex pediatric health law issues, health care fraud and abuse litigation, and the federal False Claims Act. He has written and lectured on the topic of federal civil health care fraud and abuse.

He is a member of the Philadelphia Bar Association, the Pennsylvania and Philadelphia trial lawyers associations and the American Association for Justice.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Mt. Lebanon, PA
attorneys.bio:
Elizabeth A. Avon, Esquire is an attorney with over a decade of experience in litigation. Well-versed in all aspects of Family Law, her primary focus is on divorce, custody, and fertility law.

Attorney Avon became an attorney because she loves working directly with clients and helping people achieve a sense of calm and hope in an otherwise stressful time. Attorney Avon has chosen to focus her career on family law as it is one area of law where the work that she does will ultimately have an impact on her clients' day-to-day lives. Attorney Avon recognizes that when someone needs to contact an attorney for assistance on any matter, they are most likely going through one of the most difficult experiences they may ever face. It has always been Attorney Avon's goal to help guide her clients through this frightening, and often confusing process and assist them in regaining a feeling of security and sanity. Attorney Avon always strives to ensure that each client feels heard, prioritized, and knows that their legal team is working hard to advocate for them and their family.

attorneys.name: Geoffrey J Ayers
attorneys.firm_name: Rieders, Travis, Dohrmann, Mowrey, Humphrey & Waters
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Rights Lawyers in Williamsport, PA
attorneys.bio:
Geoff was born and raised in Williamsport, and decided he wanted to be a trial lawyer when a local county judge explained the legal system to his kindergarten class at St. Anne’s Elementary School. He is a member of Loyalsock Township High School’s class of 1984. He earned his undergraduate degree at the College of William & Mary, where he joined the Sigma Chi fraternity, participated on the varsity debate team, and graduated in 1988 with a degree in Economics. He attended law school in Washington, D.C., at the American University’s Washington College of Law, where he served as a Dean’s Fellow for two professors in his second the third years (assisting in the drafting of two legal text books); secured the reversal of a life sentence in a felony murder case tried in the Maryland state courts; and graduated in the top five present of his class.

Geoff’s roots with the Rieders Travis Law Firm can be traced back to the early 1980’s when he was fortunate enough to befriend Ronald C. Travis on a tennis court at the Williamsport Tennis Club. Mr. Travis introduced Geoff to the law firm’s attorneys and staff, and Geoff worked at the firm part-time for a number of summers through high school, college, and law school. Mr. Travis ultimately sponsored Geoff for his subsequent bar memberships.

Upon graduating from law school in 1991, Geoff served as a term law clerk for the Hon. Malcolm Muir in the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Pennsylvania. At the conclusion of that two-year term, Geoff was the first Assistant Counsel hired to serve in the Williamsport office of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania’s Department of Environmental Resources (which later became the Department of Environmental Protection). In 1999 Geoff accepted Judge Muir’s invitation to return as one of his two permanent law clerks. In 2010, after Judge Muir reduced his caseload to the point that he required the services of only one permanent law clerk, Geoff returned to the Department of Environmental Protection and served as the Regional Counsel (supervising attorney) in the Department’s Williamsport office for approximately thirteen years.

Geoff retired from Commonwealth service and returned to the Rieders Travis Law firm in 2025.

attorneys.name: Tiffeny Ayoola
attorneys.practice_type: Insurance Defense Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
As an attorney with Hardin Thompson, P.C., Ms. Ayoola focuses her practice on defending insured clients in general liability matters. Her work includes representation in cases involving negligence, premises liability, and automobile liability.

Prior to joining Hardin Thompson, P.C., Ms. Ayoola practiced at a local general practice law firm where she handled a range of matters, with a primary focus on real estate litigation and criminal law.

Ms. Ayoola earned her Juris Doctor from the Thomas R. Kline School of Law of Duquesne University. During law school, she served as President of the Black Law Students Association and as a Student Bar Association Senator, reflecting a strong commitment to leadership and professional engagement. Her academic achievements and contributions were recognized through several honors, including the PLDIC Susan Yohe Scholar Award, the Ms. JD Limitless Leadership Award, and the Robert Scott Memorial Award.

Her legal education is complemented by a Master of Legal Studies in Information Security and Privacy Law from Penn State Law. She also holds dual Bachelor’s degrees in Criminology and Psychology from The Pennsylvania State University, along with a minor in African American Studies.

Ms. Ayoola is an active member of the Pittsburgh Legal Diversity & Inclusion Coalition and the Allegheny County Bar Association. Within the ACBA, she participates in the Homer S. Brown Division, Women in the Law Division, Young Lawyers Division, and the Legal Technology and E-Discovery Committee.

Outside of her legal practice, Tiffeny enjoys coding and exploring emerging issues at the intersection of litigation and technology.

attorneys.name: Nora A. Babcock
attorneys.practice_type: Elder Law Lawyers in Wexford, PA
attorneys.bio:
Nora Babcock has been practicing law in Allegheny and surrounding counties for over twenty years. Her private practice is located in the North Hills and focuses on elder law, wills and estates and in the general legal areas encompassing litigation, insurance issues, personal injury, real estate and small business matters.

As a graduate of the University of Pittsburgh School of Law in 1985, Nora began her career in civil defense law. She represented clients in insurance claims involving personal injury, property damage, toxic tort, workers compensation and first party insurance issues. In 1991 she became staff counsel for one of the nation’s largest commercial insurance carriers and for the next 10 years litigated cases on a wide range of issues including auto and trucking, fire loss, premises liability, underinsured motorist, defamation, industrial accidents, product liability, construction and boundary disputes. She has appeared before the Common Pleas courts in numerous counties in Pennsylvania and also before the Superior Court of Pennsylvania and the Federal District Court for the Western District of Pennsylvania. In 2000 she was engaged as a claims attorney for a specialty insurance company insuring architects and engineers where she managed litigation on large construction claims throughout the Eastern United States. She has significant jury trial, non-jury trial, alternative dispute and mediation experience.

Currently, in her private practice, Nora relies on her solid legal experience to advocate for individuals, families and small businesses. She is particularly concerned for individuals and families who are planning for or confronted with the issues related to aging, illness and end of life.

attorneys.name: Rebecca L. Bailey
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Chambersburg, PA
attorneys.bio:
Rebecca earned her law Degree from Widener University School of Law in 2015. While in law school, Rebecca was a Student Mentor, a Public Interest Initiative Member, Woman's Law Caucus Member, and garnered many academic achievements. Rebecca maintained her full-time paralegal position at a local law firm throughout law school, until she became an associate shortly after earning her Juris Doctor degree. Rebecca's extensive legal background and prior hands-on experience gives her an edge when it comes to handling workers' compensation and personal injury claims. Prior to law school, Rebecca worked for years as a workers' compensation paralegal. In 2010, she was the recipient of the Central Pennsylvania Paralegal Association's Outstanding Paralegal of the Year Award, in recognition of her commitment to the legal profession, quality work product, noteworthy paralegal skills, and civic involvement.

At Marzzacco Niven & Associates, Rebecca represents individual victims injured in all types of motor vehicle crashes, premises liability cases, dog bite cases, and construction site accidents. Rebecca also represents injured workers in workers' compensation claims and handles a broad range of employment discrimination matters, helping employees who have been discriminated on the basis of race, age, sex, sexual orientation, religion and gender identity. Rebecca also handles Americans with Disability Act (ADA) violations, Wage and Hour violations and other general employment law matters. Rebecca is licensed to practice in PA and NJ.

Rebecca was recently recognized for her excellent work in Pennsylvania personal injury law by being selected as a 2019 and 2020 Super Lawyers "Rising Star." Super Lawyers list is peer-reviewed, highly selective and is only awarded to attorneys who show outstanding skill and promise in their respective legal areas.

Rebecca enjoys dedicating her time providing legal services for those in need. Rebecca regularly volunteers for the Dauphin County Bar Association's Pro Bono programs including Wills for Heroes, Homeless Outreach Project, Homeless Veterans Stand Down, and the Bethesda Mission Legal Clinic.

attorneys.name: James R. Baker Esquire
attorneys.practice_type: Elder Law Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
James Baker joined Sikov and Love, P.A. as an associate attorney in 2021. He previously worked as an Assistant Public Defender for the Allegheny County Office of the Public Defender, where he represented clients from preliminary hearings before local magistrates to non-jury and jury trials in the Court of Common Pleas. Mr. Baker has also argued cases on appeal all the way to the Pennsylvania Supreme Court. His experience in court is invaluable to clients who are pursuing guardianships or involved in will contests.

Mr. Baker follows a client-centered approach, one that is responsive to his clients and their individual needs. He believes that a client who is informed about his legal options is in the best position to make the decisions suited to their situation. He serves his clients in preparing their Wills as well as Financial and Health Care Powers of Attorney and Living Wills. Mr. Baker advises his clients on long-term care and asset protection, which provides comfort and peace of mind to his clients and their families.

Mr. Baker grew up in Indiana, Pennsylvania and studied Mathematics and History at Allegheny College in Meadville, Pennsylvania. He then attended the University of Pittsburgh School of Law, where he graduated with a concentration in tax law in 2016 and earned the distinction of serving on Law Review. Mr. Baker is active in the Young Lawyers Division to the Allegheny County Bar Association and the Hay-Sell Inn of Court. He volunteers his time on the Board of the Community for Pittsburgh Ultimate.

attorneys.practice_type: Civil and Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Pottstown, PA
attorneys.bio:
Bruce L. Baldwin was born in Blue Bell, Pennsylvania. He graduated from Souderton Area High School in 1977. Mr. Baldwin attended West Chester University, graduating in 1981 with a Bachelor of Arts in Literature, Summa Cum Laude. Following his undergraduate work, Mr. Baldwin studied at Villanova University School of Law, where he was active in the Moot Court Board, and earned his Juris Doctor in 1984.

Mr. Baldwin began his practice of law in Collegeville before coming to Pottstown in 1987, when he started practicing law with firm founder Jack F. Wolf. Mr. Baldwin is past president of the Pottstown Optimist Club. He is a past recipient of the PBA's Pro Bono award, and has served on various non-profit boards in the Pottstown area. Mr. Baldwin is also a frequent lecturer on business, employment and civil litigation for the National Business Institute.

Mr. Baldwin is licensed to practice law before all Pennsylvania courts, the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania and the United States Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit. He is a member of the Pennsylvania and Montgomery County Bar Associations. Mr. Baldwin concentrates his practice in business law, employment law and commercial litigation.

attorneys.name: Lee B. Balefsky
attorneys.practice_type: Mass Tort Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
As the partner heading up Kline & Specter’s Mass Tort Department, Lee B. Balefsky is involved in lawsuits dealing with a wide range of products and toxic substances, from pharmaceuticals such as Vioxx to defective medical devices, from asbestos to denture creams containing zinc.

Balefsky’s Mass Tort department at Kline & Specter was recently named in Best Law Firms in the nation following a survey conducted by U.S. News Media Group and Best Lawyers. The "Tier 1" designation was awarded to only 22 law firms in the United States and was announced in the October 2010 issue of U.S. News & World Report.

Belefsky's three decades of experience in complex litigation puts him at the forefront of Mass Torts, a burgeoning area of the law whose genesis can be traced only as far back as the late 1960s and “mass accident” claims (generally airline mishaps) and to “Agent Orange” claims that arose in the 1970s over the herbicide used in the Vietnam War.

Balefsky has been active in mass tort claims in recent years involving asbestos and, most commonly today, pharmaceuticals. He currently serves as Plaintiff's Liaison Counsel in Philadelphia Vioxx litigation.

Balefsky's experience helped earn him a spot among “The Best Attorneys in Pennsylvania” as

selected by Super Lawyers magazine for 2004 - 2010. He was also selected for the latest edition (2010) of The Best Lawyers in America.

Mass tort practice requires knowledge and the ability to handle several issues simultaneously, with cases often filed in both state and federal courts and with multiple plaintiffs and defendants. Clients are individually represented in mass tort cases but the system allows for centralizing and sharing of information, such as documents and depositions, among various parties in trials and settlement negotiations.

Balefsky’s department at Kline & Specter is currently representing clients in claims against the makers of prescription and over-the-counter medicines as well as cases involving asbestos, medical devices and MBTE, a gasoline additive that has been found to have polluted community water supplies.

In addition to his lead role with Philadelphia Vioxx cases, Balefsky has been named Philadelphia Mass Tort Program Liaison Counsel in cases targeting the diet drugs commonly known as Fen-Phen, as well as for cases involving PPA, an ingredient used in over-the-counter cold remedies. In that liaison role, he aids the court in case management while providing other attorneys with information in the various cases.

Balefsky’s Mass Tort Department recently obtained significant settlements in lawsuits against the makers of Baycol, Fen-Phen and PPA.

His department also is involved in claims involving Vioxx, Celebrex, Bextra, Ephedra, and Atypical Antipsychotic medications including Zyprexa and Risperdal.

Over the past two decades, Balefsky has won numerous cases, particularly those in which clients were found to have contracted cancer because of their exposure to asbestos, a substance which still poses a danger to the general public and, most commonly, to workers at aging factories and facilities.

Balefsky is a member of the Plaintiff’s Steering Committee in Pennsylvania Diet Drug Litigation. He has lectured extensively in the area of pharmaceutical litigation. Balefsky is board certified in civil litigation by the National Board of Trial Advocacy. He is an active member of the American Association for Justice, the Pennsylvania Association for Justice and the Philadelphia Trial Lawyers Association.

A graduate of Temple University in 1974 and Wake Forest University Law School in 1977, Balefsky has been admitted to practice in the U.S. District Eastern and Middle Districts of Pennsylvania as well in the U.S. Third Circuit Court of Appeals and the U.S. Supreme Court.

attorneys.name: Todd L. Baritz
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Todd L. Baritz is an experienced attorney with nearly two decades of experience advocating for clients across a broad spectrum of real estate matters, with a particular emphasis on landlord-tenant disputes. As a dedicated problem-solver, Todd brings a firm practical approach to every case he handles, balancing legal strategy with a deep understanding of the client’s practical needs and goals.

After earning his B.A. in Administration of Justice from Penn State University in 1999, Todd went on to obtain his Juris Doctor from Widener University School of Law in 2002. During law school, he interned at the Philadelphia District Attorney’s Office, gaining valuable courtroom experience and developing a strong foundation in litigation.

Todd’s legal career began as a law clerk for the Honorable Joseph A. Dych in the Philadelphia Court of Common Pleas. In 2005, he joined Baritz Law, where he has since built a reputation for thoughtful advocacy and thorough legal analysis. His practice today focuses on all facets of real estate law, including lease enforcement, eviction proceedings, and Landlord and Tenant disputes.

Todd is committed to delivering clear, solution-oriented counsel, ensuring that property owners and tenants alike receive fair representation. Whether guiding clients through complex negotiations or appearing before housing court, Todd combines legal precision with a pragmatic mindset aimed at reaching efficient and just resolutions.

attorneys.name: Timothy M. Barrouk Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: DUI and DWI Lawyers in Gettysburg, PA
attorneys.bio:
Timothy M. Barrouk, Esq.

I have developed an excellent reputation in Central Pennsylvania for successfully representing clients in litigation areas including criminal law and DUI. With over a decade of criminal law experience, I am a strong trial court advocate who is not afraid to fight for my clients. I have tried well in excess of five dozen cases through to verdict, and have set many more for trial - only to have the opposing counsel settle with a favorable pre-trial resolution. I have also successfully argued multiple cases before the Pennsylvania Appellate Courts, including Com. v. Gause, a case that substantially limited the admissibility of police officers observations of impairment in atrial for Driving Under the Influence of a Controlled Substance. In addition, I have successfully fought to reinstate the driving privileges of individuals who refused to submit to chemical testing.

At home in the courtroom, I have earned a statewide reputation as one of the state's top cross-examiners of cooperating witnesses (snitches), complaining witnesses (alleged victims), and police officers (especially the State’s forensic DUI experts). I have been named a 2010 Rising Star and a Super Lawyer every year from 2013 until the present, by Super Lawyers, a prestigious nationwide legal association.

I frequently give presentations to other attorneys at continuing legal education seminars on DUI. These lectures have included topics such as standardized field sobriety testing, defending against a drug recognition expert, defending DUI controlled substance cases, chemical testing, and general DUI defense strategies. I also frequently lecture in the area of self-defense law. In addition to lecturing, I have stayed on the cutting edge by participating in classes and interactive seminars conducted by nationally renowned experts in criminal law, DUI law, forensic science, and trial advocacy.

attorneys.name: Dina K. Bastianini
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
Dina is an attorney with both in-house and law firm experience. Dina graduated from the University of Pittsburgh School of Law after receiving a B.A. in Political Science from the Mercyhurst University Honors College. Dina has tried multiple bench and jury trials to verdict as first chair counsel.

As General Counsel, Dina independently handled all litigation matters and represented the company in legal actions including: claims sounding in mandamus, tax appeals and tax litigation, breach of contract claims, civil litigation relating to property damage and land use issues, debt collection cases, fraudulent conveyance claims, zoning hearing board appeals, and confession in judgement cases.

Dina's law firm experience includes involvement in each step of the litigation process, from pre-litigation inception through appellate practice. She has experience litigating both state and federal civil cases in the fields of: insurance defense, labor and employment law, dram shop litigation, business law, contractual disputes and defamation.

Representative Cases:

• Obtained dismissal of a high-value slip and fall case through a motion for summary judgment on the basis of the Hills and Ridges Doctrine. The dismissal was confirmed on appeal by the Superior Court after briefing and oral argument.

• Obtained complete dismissal of a major-injury premises liability case via motion for judgment on the pleadings.

• Successfully negotiated a substantial settlement for my client at mediation in a complex case for defamation, tortious interference with business relations, and invasion of privacy.

• Secured the dismissal, with prejudice, of two separate land use statutory appeals.

• Negotiated a highly favorable settlement of a mandamus action filed by my client against a municipality, resulting in the prompt release of my client’s escrowed funds.

• Engineered the significant reduction (greater than 75%) of a mechanics lien claim against my client’s property following preliminary objections and presentation of evidence and testimony at an evidentiary hearing.

When not practicing law, Dina is passionate about travel and enjoys cooking and baking. She loves spending time with her family, including the best nieces and nephews in the world!

attorneys.name: Corey A. Bauer
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
Corey Bauer practices in the firm's litigation practice group with an emphasis on the substantive areas of Business Litigation, Intellectual Property Litigation, Cybersecurity and Data Breach Response, Employment, Trade Secret and DTSALaw®, Insurance Coverage and Bad Faith, and UAS/UAV (drone) Litigation and Investigations.

Corey handles sophisticated matters involving UAS/UAV (drone) technology. He has represented and/or counseled individuals and corporations in FAA regulatory compliance, FAA investigations, and even successfully defended an individual in a UAS-related jury trial in Pennsylvania. He has spoken and been published on the subject of UAS technology in the judicial system on both a state and national level.

To compliment his Business Litigation practice, he also maintains a Federal Criminal Defense practice where he represents individuals in federal criminal investigations, grand jury matters, and throughout the criminal procedural process after arrest. He has experience in counseling corporations and individuals on "dawn raids" and various constitutional protection issues arising out of criminal investigations.

Mr. Bauer has amassed a considerable amount of trial and motions practice experience in both civil and criminal matters, and he uses that experience to fearlessly prepare his clients' cases for any potential strategy or outcome.

He has been voted by his peers to be a Thomson Reuters Super Lawyer Rising Star in Business Litigation and a National Trial Lawyers Top 40 Under 40 in Criminal Defense.

In his time outside the firm, he is extremely active in the community on both a professional and personal level. He currently sits on the Council of the Allegheny County Bar Association's Young Lawyers Division, the American Bar Association's Drone Law Committee, and represents indigent criminal defendants in federal court for the Criminal Justice Act

Panel of the Federal District Court for the Western District of Pennsylvania, among other groups. Being an avid outdoorsman, he is also a member of the Rocky Mountain Elk Foundation which aims to enhance conservation efforts across the nation.

attorneys.name: Charles L. Becker
attorneys.practice_type: Appellate Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Charles L. Becker is a partner and appellate lawyer at Kline & Specter. He received his B.A. from Williams College and his J.D. from Yale Law School. After law school, he served as a law clerk for the Honorable Sandra L. Lynch of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit in Boston, Massachusetts.

Becker’s first job as a practicing lawyer was with Kline & Specter, which he joined in 1998. He left the firm in 1999 when he moved for four years to North Carolina and Womble Carlyle Sandridge and Rice, where he worked in the litigation department handling a variety of product liability and commercial matters. In 2003, he returned to Philadelphia and joined Reed Smith, LLP, where he became a partner in the Appellate Practice Group in 2006. Becker returned to Kline & Specter in 2007 to head the firm’s appellate and legal issues practice.

In his role as appellate counsel at Kline & Specter, Becker has primary responsibility for presenting written and oral argument in both state and federal appellate courts. He also consults with Kline & Specter’s trial lawyers on substantive and procedural issues to help shape litigation strategy and trial presentation, to make the best record possible for an eventual appeal, and to facilitate case resolution. These consultations include working on jurisdictional and venue issues; briefing and arguing dispositive motions, expert motions, and in limine motions; pursuing or seeking to defeat interlocutory appeals; and preparing or defending post-trial motions. Becker has participated in litigation in the Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and North Carolina state courts, in the United States Courts of Appeals for the Third and Fourth Circuits, and in the United States Supreme Court.

Becker has been active with numerous professional organizations. He serves on the Pennsylvania Supreme Court’s Appellate Courts Procedural Rules Committee, which advises the Supreme Court on the promulgation and revision of appellate rules. He serves as a governor of the Third Circuit Bar Association and as secretary of the Third Circuit Historical Society. He was appointed by the Third Circuit Judicial Counsel to serve on the Merit Selection Commission for the appointment of a new bankruptcy judge. He served as chair of the Appellate Courts Committee of the Philadelphia Bar Association from 2004 through 2007 and remains a member of that committee. He is a member of the American Law Institute, publisher of the Restatements of the Law and dedicated to producing scholarship that clarifies, modernizes and improves the law. He is secretary of the Yale Law School Association, the school’s alumni organization. He is also a member of the Philadelphia Trial Lawyers Association, the Pennsylvania Association for Justice, and the American Association for Justice.

In addition, Becker has taught on appellate practice and various substantive matters. He is a lecturer in appellate advocacy at the University of Pennsylvania Law School. He has served as faculty in numerous continuing legal education classes. He also authored the chapter on Motion Practice in the Pennsylvania Bar Institute’s Third Circuit Appellate Practice Manual.

Becker was named a “Lawyer on the Fast Track” by American Lawyer Media in 2007. He also was named by Pennsylvania Super Lawyers magazine as a 2006, 2007, 2008, 2009 and 2010 “Rising Star,” considered among the best 2.5 percent of attorneys in the state who are 40 or younger.

Becker was named a “Lawyer on the Fast Track” by American Lawyer Media in 2007. He also was named by Pennsylvania Super Lawyers magazine as a 2006, 2007, 2008, 2009 and 2010 “Rising Star,” considered among the best 2.5 percent of attorneys in the state who are 40 or younger.

attorneys.name: Thomas A. Beckley
attorneys.practice_type: Construction Lawyers in Harrisburg, PA
attorneys.bio:
Thomas Atcheson Beckley, Esquire, of Camp Hill, Pennsylvania, passed from this life on August 10, 2023. He was born in Somerset, Pennsylvania, on May 29, 1933, the son of C. Owen and Dorothy Taylor Beckley. He graduated from Camp Hill High School in 1951 and from Dickinson College in 1955, where he served as the Cadet Colonel of the College’s ROTC program. After graduation, he served for two years on active duty as an officer in the Counter Intelligence Corps of the United States Army, most of which he spent stationed in Stuttgart, Germany. His duties took him behind the Iron Curtain and afforded him the opportunity to travel throughout Europe and North Africa.

In 1957, Tom married Mary Louise Sanford, of Williamsport, Pennsylvania, and entered Dickinson Law School, where he served as Articles Editor of the Law Review. Upon graduation, he accepted an appointment as an Honor Graduate with the National Labor Relations Board in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, as a field attorney. After a year, he accepted a position with Rhoads & Sinon in Harrisburg. In 1969, Tom became one of the founding partners of the Harrisburg law firm now known as Mette, Evans & Woodside. In 1973, he established Beckley & Madden, where he remained the senior partner until his retirement in 2013.

Being a lawyer was not just a career for Tom. It was who he was. He frequently worked seven days a week and was proud of the service he gave to his many clients. His word was his bond, and he often impressed upon those working with him the importance of maintaining one’s credibility and civility in the legal profession. He served on the Joint State Government Commission’s Advisory Committee on Decedents’ Estates Laws, testified before Congress concerning issues relating to federal labor law, established a legal writing award at Dickinson Law School, and was admitted to practice in Pennsylvania and the District of Columbia. All of Tom’s four children followed his footsteps into the law, three of whom joined his firm.

When he was not working, Tom enjoyed taking his family on “mystery” vacations to Europe, the Caribbean and elsewhere. He particularly liked Walt Disney World, which he visited at least 25 times. Tom was a voracious reader and a charter member of the “Bumblers,” and loved military history and anything to do with airplanes or submarines. On several occasions he went for rides in vintage World War II aircraft. He had an engaging sense of humor, liked music and had a fine singing voice, appreciated automobiles, especially fast ones, and liked to play golf. He also enjoyed taking the family English bulldogs for rides in his old green pickup truck and playing soccer with them in the yard.

Tom was a member of the Allegheny County, Dauphin County, Pennsylvania and American Bar Associations. He was a 32nd Degree Mason. He also served on the Board of the Leukemia Society and was active in the Camp Hill Presbyterian Church, where he served as a Deacon and an Elder and helped establish the Church’s Foundation. Tom was a formidable presence in the lives of his family, who stressed the value of education and the need for hard work. He will be greatly missed.

Tom’s wife Mary, to whom he was married for 63 years, died in 2020. He is survived by his son Charles Beckley and his wife Susan, of Camp Hill; his son Frederic Beckley and his wife Frances, of Philadelphia, and their two children, Samuel and Sarah, of New York and Philadelphia; his daughter, Judge Elizabeth (“Liesl”) Beckley, of Camp Hill; and his son Thomas Beckley, his wife Karen (“Missy”) Minehan and their two children, Madeline and Jack, of Camp Hill. Tom is also survived by his sister, Ann Barasch, and her husband, Mal, of New York; his niece Amy Barasch, her husband Ray Brescia and their son Leo, of New York; his niece Jody Barasch and her partner Edward Wieland, of Washington, D.C.; and his brother-in-law, RADM Frederic G. Sanford, Medical Corps, USN (Ret.), of Rockville, Maryland.

attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Ryan’s practice at Baritz KBK Law Group focuses on real estate and civil litigation. He advises residential and commercial property owners, landlords, and asset management entities in matters involving lease enforcement, ejectments, uninsured injury claims, and regulatory disputes. His approach combines strategic insight and practical problem-solving.

Ryan earned his Bachelor of Arts in Criminology from Wilkes University. He earned a law degree at Villanova University, where he worked as a Certified Legal Intern in the Civil Justice Clinic and was published by the Jeffery S. Moorad Sports Law Journal. Speak Your Mind and Ride the Pine: Examining the Constitutionality of University-Imposed Social Media Bans on Student-Athletes - 25 Jeffrey S. Moorad Sports L.J. 51 (2018).

Ryan began his legal career as a Judicial Law Clerk to the Honorable Edward C. Wright in the First Judicial District of Pennsylvania. Prior to joining Baritz KBK, Ryan practiced at boutique litigation firms, where he handled commercial disputes, personal injury claims, medical malpractice, and institutional abuse cases.

At Baritz KBK, Ryan litigates property disputes, fair housing disputes, rent collection actions, and emergency motions. Ryan is admitted to practice in Pennsylvania and the Eastern District of Pennsylvania.

attorneys.practice_type: Corporate Lawyers in Narberth, PA
attorneys.bio:
Before and during law school, Anthony J. Beldecos worked in several positions with the Commonwealth Court of Pennsylvania and with the Philadelphia County Court of Common Pleas. Mr. Beldecos’ experience as a business, real estate and estate planning attorney since 1980 has established him as an effective representative in these technically complicated areas of law.

His clients range from individual proprietors to businesses with hundreds of employees. Mr. Beldecos’ practice includes forming corporations, partnerships and limited liability companies. He also represents clients in matters relating to real estate acquisitions, real estate sales, leasing and financing, liquor licensing in Pennsylvania and New Jersey, estate planning, probate and zoning.

He negotiates and prepares shareholder, buy-sell and partnership agreements, and represents clients in business transfers, corporate reorganizations and commercial landlord tenant litigation.

Mr. Beldecos is fluent in Greek and uses that ability to effectively represent his Greek speaking clients and numerous non-profit Greek community organizations.

attorneys.name: Elizabeth L. Bennett Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Wayne, PA
attorneys.bio:
Elizabeth Bennett is recognized as a leader in Pennsylvania, and nationwide, in the field of family law. In particular, she broke new ground with her practice in collaborative law. Practicing family law since 1978, she has established a reputation for excellence in advocacy and innovation in managing family law matters.

Libby's leadership and many contributions have led to the betterment of family law in America. Her work includes advocating for reforms for the family court processes. These reforms have been adopted in numerous jurisdictions. She has continuously been visible speaking and writing articles for publishing on the now hot topic of hidden assets. Libby was also a regular lecturer for Surgeant & Associates, the largest purveyor of tax information for accountants related to the tax aspects of family law. Another highlight of Libby's experience is her authorship of ABA resolutions intended to provide divorced women and children with medical insurance.

Libby has built a successful family law practice working in large firms as an Associate and rising to Partner, all while being a single mother and active member of her community. Her practice offers big firm experience provided in a comfortable atmosphere. She has assembled a dedicated staff of professional attorneys and support personnel to enable her to provide her successful brand of family law representation to clients throughout Pennsylvania.

attorneys.practice_type: Business Succession and Estate Administration Lawyers in Feasterville-Trevose, PA
attorneys.bio:
William J. Benz is of Counsel to High Swartz LLP and practices out of our Feasterville law office. He has been representing clients in Bucks County and throughout Pennsylvania for over 30 years. Bill is dedicated to achieving positive outcomes for all his clients.

Bill’s practice focuses on probate and estate administration. He also provides counsel for estate planning, business law, business succession planning and real estate transactions. Within Bucks County, Bill has prior experience serving as Magisterial District Judge for Northampton and Upper Southampton Townships. He also served as Township Supervisor and Zoning Board member in Northampton Township.

Bill works with his estates clients to preserve and protect their legacy. Executors and families turn to him when estate issues become overwhelming. More importantly, Bill understands that the practice of law is about humanity. He will listen to your story and guide you to the legal services that fit your needs. To view some of Bill's legal content regarding estate administration, probate, business succession, real estate and more, click here.

Bill is no stranger to community work in and around lower Bucks County. In fact, he has received two citations by the Pennsylvania State Legislature for outstanding community service.

Bill attended La Salle College High School in Glenside, PA, earned his bachelor’s degree from La Salle University and law degree from McGeorge School of Law, University of the Pacific in Sacramento, California. In his earlier years, Bill played semi-pro football for the Somerton All-Stars in Northeast Philadelphia.

attorneys.name: Erik M. Bergenthal
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
As a litigation attorney, Erik has a diverse legal background covering complex civil litigation, non-compete disputes, construction litigation, petitions for guardianship, zoning appeals and collection cases. He has additional experience researching chain of title and drafting Certified Title Opinions.

Erik has a keen interest in technology, and has worked on cases involving software design and development. His understanding of the technology behind e-discovery has helped clients realize cost savings when responding to discovery requests and subpoenas. Erik also serves on Houston Harbaugh's Technology Committee.

Erik attended the University of Pittsburgh School of Law where he received a J.D. degree and a certificate in health law. While at law school, his legal commentary was published in the New York Times and Washington Post.

In his down time, Erik enjoys photography and traveling with his wife. His charitable activities have included serving as a board member of a private foundation and involvement with legal aid.

attorneys.name: Cynthia C. Berger
attorneys.practice_type: Social Security Disability (SSD) Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
Born in Gettysburg, PA in 1950, Cynthia C. Berger graduated from the University of Pittsburgh with her bachelor's degree in 1972. She then went on to earn her Juris Doctor from the University of Pittsburgh School of Law in 1975. Ms. Berger began her legal career as a staff attorney working for the Judges at the Pittsburgh Social Security Office of Hearing and Appeals. She left the Office of Hearing and Appeals to become a founding member of the law firm of Berger and Green, P.C., representing disabled individuals throughout Western Pennsylvania and surrounding areas in Social Security Disability (SSD) and Supplemental Security Income (SSI) claims.

Attorney Berger has assessed over 50,000 Social Security disability claims in the tri-state area during the course of her career. Because of Ms. Berger's experience and expertise in Social Security disability cases, she is often invited to lecture on a variety of topics concerning Social Security disability. She has lectured at conventions of the National Organization of Social Security Claimants Representatives (NOSSCR), the Pennsylvania Bar Association (PBA), the Federal Bar Association (FBA), the National Business Institute (NBI) and the Allegheny County Bar Association (ACBA).

For more than 39 years, Attorney Berger has established a respected reputation for representing people who are no longer able to work due to their disabilities. Ms. Berger is an experienced Pennsylvania Social Security disability attorney who other attorneys turn to for advice and knowledge. Attorney Berger understands the difficulties an individual faces when they are no longer able to work due to their conditions. She is aware of the complexity of a Social Security disability case and works hard to make this process easier on her clients so they can ultimately focus on their health.

Ms. Berger is licensed to practice in all Pennsylvania State and Federal Courts and in any Social Security Court throughout the United States, as well as in the United States Supreme Court. Attorney Berger is the Chairperson of the ACBA Social Security Practitioners Committee and a Fellow of the Allegheny County Bar Foundation.

Attorney Berger serves as current president of the National Organization of Social Security Claimants Representatives (NOSSCR). With over 4,000 members, NOSSCR is the largest group of attorneys advocating for the rights of claimant's trying to receive Social Security disability benefits. Ms. Berger has been a leader for NOSCCR for several years. As president, Attorney Berger will work with the Social Security Administration and Congress to resolve current backlogs and issues that impact the disability determination process.

Attorney Berger is an active member in the legal community. She is a member of many professional organizations including NOSSCR, the American Bar Association (ABA), the American Association for Justice (AAJ), the Pennsylvania Association for Justice (PAJ) and the Western Pennsylvania Trial Lawyers Association (WPTLA). Ms. Berger is also a 2011-present Pennsylvania Super Lawyer. As a Super Lawyer, attorney Berger represents the top five percent of all lawyers in Pennsylvania. Ms. Berger is also a Martindale Hubbell AV rated attorney. This is the highest level of professionalism an attorney may be rated by their peers.

Clients appreciate Attorney Berger's compassion, preparation, concern, and attention to detail in their cases. Ms. Berger is a hardworking and driven attorney who fights hard for her clients.
