attorneys.name: Matthew Alan Diemer
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Offices of Campana, Hoffa & Morrone, P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Williamsport, PA
attorneys.bio:
Matt has been employed with our firm since April 2023, and licensed to practice law in Pennsylvania since May 2020. His practice is concentrated mostly in Criminal Defense, but he also zealously represents clients in custody, divorce, and Protection from Abuse matters. He also is a Guardian Ad Litem for Lycoming County, where he is tasked as a neutral party to represent the best interests of children in custody matters. Matt has secured victories for his clients in all aspects of the criminal justice system, to include dismissal of charges at the magistrate level, suppression of evidence in pretrial matters, and not guilty verdicts in multiple felony and misdemeanor jury and non-jury trials. He currently represents clients charged with crimes ranging from driving under the influence to attempted homicide. He has gained a reputation as being a skilled and fierce advocate for all of his clients. Matt represents his clients in appellate and post-conviction matters as well before the Pennsylvania Superior, Commonwealth, and Supreme Courts. Matt attended law school at the Widener University Commonwealth Law School in Harrisburg, PA, where he was ranked in the top 10 of his class each semester, and graduated cum laude. He was a member of the law review and an executive board member of the trial advocacy honor society. While in law school he was an intern with the Lycoming County Public Defender's Office. Upon passing the bar exam, Matt was employed by the former Callahan Gardner law firm, which ultimately transitioned into the Lovecchio Diemer Law Firm. Prior to attending law school, Matt graduated from Lycoming College with a degree in Political Science, is a member of Pi Sigma Alpha—the National Political Science Honor Society, and was a proud member and officer with the local United Steelworkers Union.

attorneys.name: Cory Dillinger
attorneys.practice_type: Renewable Energy Law Lawyers in York, PA
attorneys.bio:
Cory joined MPL Law Firm, LLP in October of 2020 with a focus on Municipal Law, Renewable Energy Development and Business Law.

A significant portion of Cory’s practice is dedicated to the development of renewable energy projects. Recently, Cory has assisted numerous solar energy developers across Pennsylvania on a variety of matters including initial project planning phases, navigating municipal ordinances, zoning approvals, entitlements, land-development approval, building permits, stormwater management, etc. He has successfully assisted these developers from the land acquisition phase to a myriad of post-construction issues a solar project may face.

Prior to joining MPL Law Firm, LLP as a full-time attorney, Cory worked for two years as a law clerk for a Personal Injury and Workers’ Compensation firm based out of Pittsburgh. In his last year of law school, Cory assisted and represented Pro Se individuals for various domestic and family law matters in the Allegheny County Pro Se Assistance Program as a Certified Legal Intern.

A 2020 graduate from the University Of Pittsburgh School of Law, Cory was frequently involved in the W. Edward Sell Chapter of the American Inns of Court. Cory, as a new member of the York County Bar Association, is looking forward to getting involved in the Greater York Community.

Attorney Betty Dillon has been a member of the John McMillan Presbyterian Church for more than 35 years, and serves as their Corporate Counsel. For fun, she enjoys reading and loves the beach. She likes to play bridge and also has an interest in following politics. She was a long-time member of the Bethel Park League of Women Voters.

Educated in Pittsburgh

Originally from Johnstown, Pennsylvania, Attorney Betty Dillon is a graduate of the University of Pittsburgh and the School of Law at the University of Pittsburgh. Following law school she gained experience in the areas of Estates and Trusts at Pittsburgh National Bank's Estates and Trusts Department. Because of her interest in this area of law, Attorney Betty Dillon went on to establish her own practice focusing on estates, estate planning, elder and family law.

Focused Experience

While maintaining her own practice, Attorney Betty Dillon served part time as a telephone consultant for seven years for the AARP Legal Hotline for Older Americans. She provided legal advice to senior citizens across Pennsylvania on a wide variety of subjects, including estates, wills, family, consumer, and elder law issues. Her overall exposure to numerous legal issues provides her with the background and knowledge to effectively handle your legal issues.

attorneys.bio:
Gino comes from a family of professionals. He is the son of the late Arthur DiNicola, M.D., family physician for over 40 years and Elizabeth, a retired R.N. His brothers and sisters consist of three physicians, an engineer and a physician’s assistant. Gino chose to practice law and he began his legal career after graduating the prestigious Dickinson School of Law of Penn State University practicing Workers’ Compensation in both Luzerne and Schuylkill County. His law career began in 1990 and he has since represented individuals in Workers’ Compensation, Personal Injury and Social Security Disability. Since 1990 he has cumulatively recovered millions of dollars for his clients with his zealous representation. For example, in what appeared to be only a modest slip and fall case, Gino generated a claim and recovered a settlement worth over half a million dollars for an elderly woman from a well known global petroleum client.

In the Workers’ Compensation field Gino is unwavering in his representation of injured workers and he can immediately call upon his vast medical knowledge and also rely upon the medical expertise of his family to determine if you have a successful claim.

Like Rob, Gino never charges to answer your questions or to meet with you for advice. If you hire him for a Workers’ Compensation matter he will always reduce his fee in all lump sum settlements. In all cases Gino will pay every cost necessary to litigate and win your case.

With a background in family law in Pennsylvania since 2011, Rebecca seamlessly transitioned her practice to address the unique needs of clients facing complex estate planning issues.

Graduating cum laude from Saint Joseph’s University and earning her Juris Doctor degree from Villanova University School of Law, Rebecca distinguished herself as the associate editor of the Villanova Law Review and President of the Family Law Society. In 2023, she furthered her expertise by obtaining an Estate Planning Certificate from Temple University Beasley School of Law.

Beyond her legal accomplishments, Rebecca has been an active member of the Malvern Library community, serving as vice-president on the Board of Trustees since 2021. Her commitment to community engagement reflects her dedication to fostering positive connections beyond the legal realm.

Residing in West Chester with her husband, son, and daughter, Rebecca brings a compassionate and informed approach to her role at Anderson Elder Law, where she looks forward to leveraging her family law skill set to provide comprehensive counsel to clients navigating estate planning challenges.

attorneys.name: Geoffrey W. Dlin
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Law Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
The Honorable Geoffrey W. Dlin (ret.) has returned to private practice and joined KK &O after serving more than 15 years as a Workers' Compensation Judge. As a judge, he decided thousands of contested workers' compensation cases and frequently taught other lawyers, judges and private organizations about workers' compensation matters. In addition to those traditional roles of a judge, Geoff developed a statewide mediation practice. His skills in settling workers' compensation cases were highly sought after and well regarded by lawyers and litigants on both sides of a case. Lawyers and judges hold him in high esteem for his knowledge of the law, dedication and ability to resolve even the most complex cases--including those that involved personal injury or employment law

Before his judgeship, Geoff represented injured workers and people who were injured either as the result of the negligence of others or dangerous products. He has also represented employers and insurance companies in personal injury and workers' compensation matters. Geoff brings a unique and varied perspective to the firm and his clients.

Geoff's is devoted to representing injured workers. His clients reap the benefits of the broad and deep experience he brings to the firm. They can rely on Geoff to be thorough, thoughtful and informative. In the court room or at the negotiating table, his goal is the same--success.

In addition to his speaking engagements and publishing, Geoff served as a guest expert on the television show, American Law Journal.

attorneys.name: Jeffrey C. Dohrmann
attorneys.firm_name: Rieders, Travis, Dohrmann, Mowrey, Humphrey & Waters
attorneys.practice_type: Employee Rights Lawyers in Williamsport, PA
attorneys.bio:
Jeff is originally from Woolrich. His father, Bernhard Dohrmann, was an attorney, public defender, and district attorney in Lock Haven, and his mother, Mary, was his assistant. Jeff was his father’s Paralegal until he passed away in November 1983. When Jeff became an attorney, he proudly hung his father’s original shingle in his own office, where it remains.

Jeff graduated from Penn State in 1982 with a BA in English/Writing, and an Area of Knowledge in Theater Performance. He has acted in and directed many productions over the years, with favorite roles being Stanley Kowalski in A Streetcar Named Desire, and, in 2017, Vladimir in Waiting for Godot. In fact, he met his wife, Melanie, while playing Harold Hill to her Marian the Librarian in The Music Man. Her voice definitely outshone his.

In December 1983, after his father passed away, Jeff was hired at Rieders Travis as Cliff’s Litigation Paralegal. He went to law school while working, graduating Magna Cum Laude from Widener University School of Law in 1993. After being admitted to the Pennsylvania and Middle District of Pennsylvania bars in November 1993, Jeff began representing as their attorney clients he had worked with as a Paralegal, and was trying their cases in federal court as early as 1994.

The most important advice Jeff received in law school was, “Don’t conform yourself to the practice of law, conform the practice of law to yourself.” That is why most often when you come into the office, Jeff will be wearing blue jeans and a Woolrich shirt, and his suit will be waiting on the back of his door, ready for the next trial or hearing. He only represents people. People who have been physically or emotionally injured, at work or in personal injury situations. People who have been wrongfully treated, terminated, harassed or discriminated against at work. People who have had their civil rights violated.

Jeff has two stepsons, a daughter and a son with Melanie. For years, Jeff and Melanie coached all four in soccer. During one memorable season, the four “kids” were on six different soccer teams, with Jeff coaching two of the teams, and Melanie coaching one of the teams. Melanie has the well-deserved bragging rights of going undefeated in that season.

Although now “empty-nested” as far as kids go, Jeff and Melanie are “full-housed” with two German Shepherds and four cats. And the German Shepherds are excellent soccer players.

As things go full circle, like Bernhard Dohrmann’s shingle now hanging in Jeff Dohrmann’s office, Jeff and Melanie now live in the same Woolrich home Jeff’s parents built in 1958.

attorneys.name: Mary Cushing Doherty
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Norristown, PA
attorneys.bio:
Mary Cushing Doherty is a family law attorney and Of Counsel at High Swartz. She concentrates her practice on marital dissolution and a wide range of family law issues. An experienced and certified Arbitrator and Mediator, Ms. Doherty strives for the amicable resolution of divorce when possible; however, she is a zealous litigator when it serves her clients' best interests.

Some of Mary's noteworthy accomplishments include:

She specializes in finding the optimal monetary settlement for complex marital cases. She works alongside financial experts and forensic accountants for high-income individuals and dependent spouses.

She arbitrates complicated financial analysis matters to resolve monetary awards typically unobtainable in court.

Drafts comprehensive and protective prenuptial agreements and marital settlement agreements by anticipating the problems that clients can't or haven't envisioned

Drafts "romantic" prenuptial agreements that are designed to foster a long healthy marriage based on communication and shared values

Beginning her career in Philadelphia, she served as chair of the Philadelphia Bar Family Law Section in 1985 and as its representative on the Judicial Selection Commission. She was a co-chair of the Montgomery County Family Law Committee in 1994 and chair of the Pennsylvania Bar Association Family Law Section in 1999-2000.

Mary served as President of the AAML Pennsylvania Chapter from 2006 to 2007. After that, she served as Chapter Leader Coordinator from 2010 to 2013 and co-chaired the AAML Legislation Committee for several years. She will co-author her second law review article for AAML in 2024.

Mary has rightfully been honored over the years for her unparalleled community work and dedication to marital and family law. Super Lawyer consistently ranks her as a Top Lawyer in America®. She's also received honors as a Top Attorney in Suburban Life Magazine and an honoree in the Montgomery and Pennsylvania Bar Association. In 2012, she was a Legal Intelligencer Women of the Year recipient and PBA Lynette Norton Award honoree. In 2018, Mary received the prestigious honor of The Leukemia & Lymphoma Society Woman of the Year for the Philadelphia area and top state Advocate in 2023.

As an attorney, Ms. Doherty has enjoyed a distinguished career. She's been a Course Planner and Lecturer for The PBI (and served on its board for seven years), the Philadelphia Bar Association, and MBA Family Law Sections, and a Lecturer for the American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers (AAML). She has been a spokesperson for legislative reform for the Pennsylvania Bar Association. The PBA has honored her for acting as its spokesperson for reform of the custody statute and the Divorce Code to ease lengths of no-fault divorce. She chaired the Supreme Court Committee on certification organizations that qualify lawyers as experts. She served on the Pennsylvania Domestic Violence Task Force. Plus, she participates in the PA Joint State Legislative Committee on Family Law.

Outside the Office

Mary's civic and community activities are varied and numerous. She chairs the Pennsylvania Advocacy Committee for the Leukemia & Lymphoma Society addressing state and federal legislators to pass laws to help blood cancer patients and their caregivers and received the National Award as Outstanding State Leader in 2023 She's also serves on the BucksMont Light the Night Executive Committee.

She is active in her church, St. Catherine of Sienna, as a lector in Horsham. She also organizes the Holy Innocents memorial every Christmas in memory of infants children who have died and is an active supporter of the St. Vincent DePaul Society. She was an adjunct instructor in Child Development to Upper Dublin High School youth for 28 years. Mary has served as an Inn of Court mentor and Master of the Bench for Doris Jonas Freed Inn since its inception in 1995.

attorneys.name: Lorraine Donnelly
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Lorraine Donnelly is a trial attorney who has spent her career fighting for victims of crime and neglect, first as a criminal prosecutor and now as a civil plaintiffs’ attorney. At Kline & Specter she focuses on medical malpractice, nursing home neglect and other catastrophic injury cases.

Donnelly worked as a prosecutor at the Philadelphia District Attorney’s Office for more than a decade, assigned to the homicide unit her last four years. During her tenure there, Donnelly tried 91 jury trials that resulted in guilty verdicts in major felony and homicide cases. In that capacity, she gained experience in all phases of criminal prosecutions, from advising police regarding their investigations, understanding forensic science evidence, questioning hostile witnesses at trial and handling issues of witness intimidation and attempted jury tampering.

In March 2015, Donnelly accepted a position at a national plaintiffs’ law firm, where she continued to fight for victims of neglect on the civil side. During her four-year tenure, she managed a large inventory of nursing home abuse and neglect cases throughout Pennsylvania and New Jersey. Donnelly was co-counsel in a Lancaster, Pa., jury trial that resulted in a $7.5 million verdict against a nursing home and its corporate owner for failing to protect a nursing home resident from sexual assault by another resident.

Donnelly earned her undergraduate degree from La Salle University, graduating maxima cum laude. She earned her law degree from Temple University Beasley School of Law, where she graduated cum laude and was a staff member and then article editor for Temple Law Review. Donnelly is admitted to practice in Pennsylvania, New Jersey and the Eastern and Middle U.S. District Courts of Pennsylvania. She is a member of the American Association for Justice, Pennsylvania Association for Justice and the Temple Law Alumni Association.

attorneys.name: Harry A. Dorian Jr. (1953
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Bensalem, PA
attorneys.bio:
Harry A. Dorian, Jr. has been practicing law since 1978. He is a graduate of Ohio Northern University School of Law, where he was co-editor of the Ohio Northern University Law Review. In 1975, he graduated with honors from Penn State University with a BA degree in English. He grew up in Montgomery County, graduating from Lower Merion High School in 1971. He was awarded the rank of Eagle Scout in 1970.

Mr. Dorian is a senior managing partner of the firm of Dorian, Goldstein, Wisniewski & Orchinik, P.C. where, for the past 35 years, he has concentrated his practice in the areas of medical malpractice, nursing home negligence, motor vehicle accidents, product liability and other cases involving serious injury or death.

For more than twenty years, he has consistently received the highest possible peer-review rating available ("AV Preeminent") from Martindale-Hubbell for maintaining the highest standards of professional ethics and legal ability. This rating is based upon an extensive peer-review survey of practicing attorneys and judges.

Also, he was recently again named "Pennsylvania Super Lawyer" by Philadelphia Magazine and Law and Politics, based upon a confidential survey of over 39,000 attorneys in Pennsylvania. Only 4% of attorneys in Pennsylvania are awarded the status of a "Pennsylvania Super Lawyer". He has also consistently obtained a rating of "Superb" by Avvo (receiving a perfect 10.0 score), and The National Association of Trial Lawyers has named him one of the "Top 100 Trial Lawyers in Pennsylvania".

He has obtained numerous multi-million dollar recoveries in various types of negligence cases, such as motor vehicle accidents, slip and falls, medical malpractice, nursing home neglect/abuse, dog attacks, premises defects and product liability.

Mr. Dorian has also been appointed a Special Judge Pro Tempore and Settlement Master by the Philadelphia Court of Common Pleas in its Civil Case Management Program. He is also a frequent Arbitrator for the Bucks County Court of Common Pleas.

Mr. Dorian has given lectures to physicians and surgeons on issues related to patient safety and medical malpractice, and he has taught other attorneys at legal seminars involving various areas of the law. Recently, he spoke to hundreds of dentists and dental professionals about oral cancer and dental malpractice at Continuing Dental Education seminars at the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor, and the Temple University School of Dentistry in Philadelphia.

Mr. Dorian has tried numerous cases in both state and federal court in Pennsylvania. He has argued appeals before the Pennsylvania Supreme Court, Pennsylvania Superior Court and the Commonwealth Court of Pennsylvania. He is a long-time member of the American Association for Justice, Pennsylvania Association for Justice, Pennsylvania Bar Association, Bucks County Bar Association, Philadelphia Bar Association and the Philadelphia Trial Lawyers Association, as well as a certified member of the "Million Dollar Advocates Forum". He is also an AARP-approved attorney with the AARP Legal Services Network.

Harry and the law firm also donate a significant amount of time and funds providing legal services to disadvantaged clients who cannot afford an attorney.

Harry's hobbies include fishing, tennis and hoping that the Phillies win the World Series again in his lifetime.

attorneys.name: John B. Dougherty
attorneys.practice_type: Labor Lawyers in Harrisburg, PA
attorneys.bio:
John (Jack) Dougherty is a resident of Lower Paxton Township where he resides with his wife and two children. He is a graduate of Villanova University and Widener University School of Law. For the past seventeen years he has represented working men and women for various legal issues including but not limited to personal injury, workers compensation, unemployment compensation, discrimination, criminal and traffic issues. In addition, he has represented labor unions before the Pennsylvania Labor Relations Board, the National Labor Relations Board and he has handled numerous grievance arbitration hearings and negotiations. He frequently speaks to unions including the Teamsters and the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers regarding common legal issues faced by Union Stewards and members in the workplace, including the effects of Act 60 on Unemployment Recipients in the Building Trades. He has also represented Union Trustees in Multi-Employer Taft Hartley employee benefit plans. He is actively involved in his community as a member of the operations board of the Lower Paxton Township Friendship Community Center as well as various school and sports associations.

Attorney Dougherty’s practice is focused on a full service approach to helping Unions and working men and women navigate the legal system and assisting them with the numerous legal issues that they can encounter over the course of a lifetime. If you have legal issue that you would like to discuss contact Attorney Dougherty at 717-238-1657 or at jdougherty@weinstocklaborlaw.com.

Erika works with injured and disabled individuals on Social Security Disability and Veterans’ Disability Compensation Claims. She received a B.A. from Duquesne University in 2018, majoring in Journalism and Multimedia, and received her law degree from Duquesne University School of Law in 2021, graduating cum laude, with a concentration in healthcare law. Erika is a member of the Allegheny County, Westmoreland County, and Pennsylvania Bar associations, as well as the National Organization of Social Security Representatives (NOSSCR) and the National Organization of Veterans Advocates (NOVA). She is admitted to practice before the courts of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania and the United States Court for the Western District of Pennsylvania. Outside law school, she worked to help low-income individuals receive Social Security Disability, Veterans Disability, and other government benefits with Neighborhood Legal Services in Pittsburgh and Butler, Pennsylvania. A western Pennsylvania native, Erika and her husband currently live in the South Hills of Pittsburgh, where they enjoy hiking, biking, kayaking, and following the Penguins, Steelers, and Pirates.

attorneys.name: David J. Draganosky
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Blue Bell, PA
attorneys.bio:
David J. Draganosky graduated from LaSalle University in 1986 with a Bachelors of Arts, majoring in English. Subsequently, he obtained his Juris Doctor, cum laude, from the Temple University School of Law in 1990. While in law school, Mr. Draganosky served on the staff of the Temple Law Review, an honor for which he was chosen based upon his performance in a rigorous research and writing competition.

Following his graduation from law school, Mr. Draganosky joined the Montgomery County law firm of Pearlstine/Salkin Associates where he practiced general litigation, with an emphasis in family law. In 1996, Mr. Draganosky began exclusively practicing family law when Pearlstine/Salkin Associates merged with and became the Montgomery County office of Fox Rothschild LLP, a prominent then Philadelphia-based, regional law firm. In 2000, Mr. Draganosky became a partner at Fox Rothschild where he remained until he joined Shemtob Law in June, 2008. During his 12 years with Fox Rothschild, Mr. Draganosky saw the firm grow to 400 lawyers with 14 offices coast to coast and one of Pennsylvania’s premier and largest family law departments.

Mr. Draganosky is admitted to practice before all state and federal courts in Pennsylvania and New Jersey. He is a frequent lecturer and has been interviewed by the press regarding various family law topics including divorce, equitable distribution, custody and support. He has also authored numerous family law articles that have been published both in print and on line. Mr. Draganosky is a member of the Pennsylvania and Montgomery County Bar Associations and their respective Family Law Sections. Additionally, he serves on the Montgomery Bar Association’s Joint Liaison with Accountants Committee, Membership Committee and Sidebar Committee. Mr. Draganosky lives in Montgomery County with his wife and three children.

attorneys.name: Laura Ann Dugan
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Offices of Kevin M. O'Neill, LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Media, PA
attorneys.bio:
Laura Dugan, Esquire, joined the Law Offices of Kevin M. O'Neill, LLC, as an associate in February 2022. Laura zealously represents clients in all criminal law matters ranging from summary citations to felony charges. Due to her considerable work experience in the criminal justice field as well as the professional relationships she has forged through that work experience, Laura is well-equipped to handle her clients' criminal matters.

In 2011, Laura graduated from Villanova University with a B.A. in Psychology and a Criminal Justice minor. While attending Villanova University, Laura volunteered to tutor inmates at S.C.I. Graterford. Additionally, she interned at George W. Hill Correctional Facility, where many of her current clients are housed, as a case manager. Both of these experiences allowed Laura to familiarize herself with the criminal justice system early on.

In 2015, Laura graduated from Widener University School of Law located in Wilmington, Delaware. While attending law school, Laura completed an externship as a judicial clerk with the Honorable James F. Nilon, Jr., at the Delaware County Courthouse. She also served as a legal intern in the criminal division of the United States Attorney's Office located in Philadelphia. Finally, Laura served as a certified legal intern with the Delaware County District Attorney's Office. Through each of these experiences, Laura obtained a thorough understanding of criminal law and is now able to thoroughly explain the criminal process to her clients in a way that is easy for them to understand.

After passing the bar exam in 2015, Laura became an associate with the Delaware County law firm Raffaele Puppio and remained with that firm for over six years. Her practice at Raffaele Puppio concentrated on criminal defense, personal injury, and workers' compensation matters. In fact, Laura successfully argued before the Commonwealth Court of Pennsylvania in a workers' compensation matter. During her six years with Raffaele Puppio, Laura passionately advocated on behalf of her many clients to ensure she was always getting the most favorable result possible for her client.

Laura has been an active member of the Delaware County Bar Association since 2015.

attorneys.name: Mitchell H. Dugan
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
Mitchell H. Dugan compiled experience representing clients at Pittsburgh area law firms and then created a firm that extends legal representation to injured persons without fee unless recovery is made. Mitch has more than 17 years of experience. He focuses on workers' compensation, personal injury and social security disability. Most importantly, he remains committed to trying to help clients get the compensation they may be entitled to.

A graduate of the University of Pittsburgh School of Law, Mitch practiced at Fingeret, Pollock, Cohen & Zavarella, Stone & Stone and Alexander J. Pentecost prior to starting his own firm in 2000. He also interned in the Allegheny County District Attorney's office and with Zittrain & Zittrain. He has spoken about injuries, workers' compensation and social security disability to audiences throughout the state. He has presented for the Allegheny County Bar Association and has spoken for continuing legal education credits for lawyers with the National Business Institute, Clearwater Information Systems, Inc. and Sterling Education Services, LLC.

He is a member of the American Bar Association, the Pennsylvania Bar Association, the Allegheny County Bar Association, the American Association for Justice, the National Organization of Social Security Claimants Representatives and the Western Pennsylvania Trial Lawyers Association. He is licensed to practice in the Pennsylvania State Courts and in the Western District of the Federal Courts. He also belongs to the North Boroughs Rotary Club where he served as a past President.

attorneys.name: Aaron Dunbar
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Prior to joining Kline & Specter, Aaron L. Dunbar was a prosecutor representing victims of violent crimes at the Philadelphia District Attorney’s Office. At Kline & Specter he represents plaintiffs in personal injury and mass tort litigation.

Dunbar was co-counsel in a case that concluded in July 2023 with an $11 million settlement with a Philadelphia community umbrella agency for failing to oversee an infant’s care, leading to catastrophic child abuse. The child suffered a traumatic brain injury resulting in quadriplegia and blindness, requiring lifetime skilled care. (See media coverage)

Dunbar was also co-counsel in filing suits claiming that dozens of people contracted cancer from exposure to ethylene oxide, or EtO, emitted from a B. Braun plant in Allentown, Pa., at which the colorless gas was used to sterilize medical equipment. (See news coverage on WFMZ-TV, The Morning Call, Law360 lehighvalleylive.com)

In 2022 and 2023, he was named by Super Lawyers* as a Pennsylvania Rising Star, placing him among the top 2.5 percent of lawyers in the commonwealth who are 40 or younger or practicing 10 years or less.

Dunbar previously worked in civil litigation at Post & Schell, P.C., in Philadelphia, where he handled product and general liability claims. Before that, he worked at a regional defense firm where he represented commercial entities and medical care providers.

As an assistant district attorney for three and a half years, Dunbar managed a caseload of approximately 120 complex criminal matters through various phases of prosecution, including pre-arrest investigations, grand jury indictments and trying bench and jury trials to verdict. Dunbar prosecuted offenders for crimes that included burglary, arson, robbery, narcotics, weapons violations, aggravated assault, sexual abuse against children and rape.

Dunbar graduated magna cum laude from the University of Maryland Eastern Shore with a degree in criminal justice. He earned his law degree from North Carolina Central University School of Law, where he was staff editor of the NCCU Law Review.

While in law school, he worked with the Small Business and Community Development Clinic, the Criminal Defense Clinic and the Veteran’s Law Clinic. During law school Dunbar worked as a summer associate at the Raleigh, N.C., law firm Gray Newell Thomas, LLP, and as a legal intern for Philadelphia Common Pleas Judge Karen Shreeves-Johns.

Dunbar is former treasurer of The Barristers’ Association of Philadelphia, an organization founded in 1950 to address the professional needs and development of Black lawyers in the city. He also serves on the committee for communications and fundraising for the Share Food Program and is a former member of the board of directors for Men’s Center for Growth and Change.

attorneys.name: John H. Dumont
attorneys.practice_type: Businesses Organizations Lawyers in Newtown, PA
attorneys.bio:
John H. Dumont represents closely-held businesses and nonprofit organizations. He provides guidance on various matters such as initial formation, capital raising, shareholder relations, equity and debt utilization, and regulatory compliance for New Jersey businesses. Additionally, he has extensive experience in estate planning and a wide range of real estate activities, including acquisition, financing, tax-free exchanges, leasing, low-income housing utilization, tax credits, and the establishment of joint ventures, investor-oriented limited partnerships, and land use law. Mr. Dumont collaborates with nonprofit organizations in New Jersey to create affordable housing.

Mr. Dumont obtained a B.A. degree from the University of Michigan in 1963 and completed his studies at Michigan Law School in 1966. He holds memberships in the Princeton Bar Association and New Jersey State Bar Association.

attorneys.name: Ryan Duty
attorneys.practice_type: Nursing Home & Elder Abuse Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
Ryan Duty is proud to be Morgan & Morgan's first attorney in the Pittsburgh Office. He has roots in the area, as he has lived around Pittsburgh for most of his life and attended law school there, graduating from Duquesne University School of Law in 2010.

Ryan has spent his entire legal career advocating for victims of nursing home abuse and neglect, often at the hands of large nursing home corporations that unfortunately too often emphasize profits over the care provided to the residents. He has proudly represented nursing home residents and their families when severe injuries resulted from inadequate nursing care. Prior to joining Morgan & Morgan, Ryan worked for a nationally preeminent nursing home litigation firm in their Pittsburgh office. During this time, Ryan was involved in numerous high profile nursing home cases in Pennsylvania, and tried multiple cases to verdict, most recently obtaining an $800,000 verdict on behalf of a nursing home resident in western Pennsylvania. Overall, he helped recover more than $50 million on behalf of his injured clients in Pennsylvania and West Virginia. At Morgan & Morgan, Ryan continues to represent those who have been harmed due to inadequate care, at nursing homes as well as hospitals and other healthcare facilities.

While in law school, Ryan was a member of Duquesne's nationally recognized Trial Advocacy Program. He competed in multiple national competitions and was selected to the Order of the Barristers for his advocacy skill.

Ryan is licensed to practice law in Pennsylvania, West Virginia, Ohio, and Arkansas. He is a member of the American Association of Justice, the Western Pennsylvania Trial Lawyers Association, and the Pennsylvania Association of Justice.

attorneys.bio:
David V. Dzara is an associate with Pepper Hamilton LLP, resident in the Philadelphia office. Mr. Dzara concentrates his practice in commercial litigation, with a focus on contract and appellate matters.

Mr. Dzara's recent commercial litigation engagements include:

· representing a multinational corporation as both plaintiff and defendant in numerous matters involving contract, negligence, and related common law claims

· representing a multinational petroleum corporation in connection with claims for breach of franchise agreements

· representing a multinational manufacturing corporation in connection with conversion and contract claims

· defending a state agency in a preliminary and permanent injunction matter.

In addition, Mr. Dzara devotes considerable time to pro bono matters, including representation of clients through the Support Center for Child Advocates and the Philadelphia VIP/LawWorks Quiet Title Program. He also represents pro bono clients in guardianship matters.

attorneys.name: Drew P. D’Angelo
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Rights Litigation Lawyers in Cheltenham, PA
attorneys.bio:
Drew P. D'Angelo has been a trial attorney for more than 30 years, representing plaintiffs and defendants in various civil matters including civil rights litigation. His practice now focuses on a variety of complex civil litigation matters including representation of plaintiffs in connection with catastrophic personal injury, negligence, automobile accidents, wrongful death, premises liability, liquor liability, product liability, medical malpractice and construction-related accidents. Drew also handles workers' compensation matters.

Prior to his current position at Stampone Law, Drew was a City Solicitor for the City of Philadelphia from 1974 to 1981. During that time he represented the Police Department and other City agencies in high profile matters. Drew also served as a civil rights teacher to the Philadlephia Police Academy. He taught the officers in training how not to violate the Civil Rights of those being arrested and others.

Drew is admitted to practice in the Supreme Court of Pennsylvania; the Bar of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania; the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania; and the United States Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit.

Born and raised in Northeast Philadelphia Drew currently resides in Erdenheim, Pennsylvania with his wife and two children. He married a soloist from the Pennsylvania Ballet and has many artistic and cultural ties to the City of Philadelphia. He is actively trying to produce a musical comedy called "The 25th Century Comic", which was written by his Father, Lenny Payton, a well-known jazz musician and television personality from Philadelphia. Drew is active in coaching sports, such as CYO basketball and soccer.

attorneys.name: Marc H. Edelson
attorneys.practice_type: Antitrust Law Lawyers in Newtown, PA
attorneys.bio:
Marc H. Edelson is a founding partner of Edelson Lechtzin LLP, and leads the firm's practices in the areas of antitrust law, defective drugs & medical devices, and property insurance litigation. Mr. Edelson received his J.D. from the University of California, Los Angeles School of Law, in 1987 and his B.S. in Economics from the Wharton School of The University of Pennsylvania, cum laude in 1984. He has practiced class action litigation for over 30 years and has been appointed to leadership roles in many MDL cases including several involving the pharmaceutical industry.

Mr. Edelson's MDL experience in pharmaceutical cases includes an appointment by Judge Patti Saris in In re Pharmaceutical Industry Average Wholesale Price Litigation, MDL No. 1456 as one of the four lead counsel firms. Mr. Edelson was one of the first attorneys to initiate a series of class actions on behalf of end payors against numerous pharmaceutical defendants which were eventually consolidated into MDL 1456. The case involved an in depth analysis of pharmaceutical pricing and resulted in numerous settlements totaling $341,000,000.

Additionally, Mr. Edelson served as co-lead counsel in New England Carpenters Health Benefit Fund v. First DataBank, Inc. and McKesson Corp., C.A. No. 05-11148 (D. Mass) and District 37 Health and Securities Fund v. Medi-Span, C.A. No. 07-10988 (D. Mass). This case was against pharmaceutical wholesaler McKesson Corporation and pharmaceutical publishers First DataBank and Medi-Span. The case focused on unlawful drug pricing markups of various drugs resulting in overpayments by end payors. The case settled for $350,000,000 in addition to an agreement to roll back drug prices by five percent (5%) resulting in additional end payor cost savings totaling hundreds of millions of dollars.

Mr. Edelson has also served as co-lead counsel in additional pharmaceutical cases including In re Ciprofloxacin Hydrochloride Antitrust Litigation, MDL 1383 (EDNY), Sandhaus v. Bayer AG, et al., Case No. 00-cv-6193 (Kansas State Court), In re Premarin Antitrust Litigation, Case No. 1:01-cv-00447 (SD Ohio), and Blevins v. Wyeth Ayerst Laboratories, Inc., Case No. 324380 (Superior Court State of California).

Mr. Edelson was appointed one of the co-lead counsel in In re Western States Wholesale Natural Gas Antitrust Litigation, MDL 1566 (D Nevada) and In re HELOC Minimum Payment Calculation Litigation, Case No. 15-cv-00267 (EDPA).

Mr. Edelson has served as a member of the Executive Committee in In re Copper Antitrust Litigation, MDL 1301 (WD Wisc), In re Certainteed Corp. Roofing Shingle Product Litigation, MDL 1817 (EDPA), and In re HP Inkjet Printer Litigation, Case No. C053580JF (ND Cal, San Jose Div.).

Mr. Edelson has also served as lead or co-lead counsel in numerous state court class actions involving consumer fraud and defective products.

attorneys.name: Scott M. Eden
attorneys.practice_type: Business & Commercial Law Lawyers in York, PA
attorneys.bio:
Scott joined MPL Law Firm, LLP in October of 2025. Prior to joining MPL Law Firm, LLP as the Director of Practice Development, Scott has enjoyed a diverse career in both law and as a successful business owner. Although a York Suburban High School graduate, Scott lived in North Carolina and graduated from North Carolina Central School of Law as Salutatorian in 2000. Immediately following law school, Scott attended NYU School of Law and earned an LLM in Taxation. For the next 10 plus years, Scott practiced law throughout the Southeast. He first practiced at a large North Carolina law firm in the tax, corporate and M&A areas. Scott eventually transitioned to working as in-house counsel for a variety of publicly traded companies in the software, auto insurance and pharmaceutical industries. Scott specialized in securities, corporate governance, software licensing and professional services agreements. He also gained vast experience in all legal aspects of a public company while serving in legal leadership positions at these corporations.

In 2010, Scott moved back to York and founded and managed a popular restaurant and bar in Downtown York. Scott’s successful restaurant and business experience brings an invaluable perspective to advising hospitality industry and corporate clients. Scott has first-hand knowledge in starting a business, creating value and an eventual exit plan. He also has experience with PA Liquor Law regarding compliance, violations and the purchase and sale of PLCB licensed businesses.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Hollidaysburg, PA
attorneys.bio: Kaitlyn G. Edmiston was born in Altoona, Pennsylvania, and has remained local for the majority of her life. She graduated Summa Cum Laude in 2020 from Saint Francis University, receiving a Bachelor of Arts degree in Global Social Justice with a Pre-Law Concentration. Ms. Edmiston received her Juris Doctor from Widener University Commonwealth Law School in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania in 2023, graduating Magna Cum Laude. During her time in law school, she interned at the Blair County Courthouse, the Pennsylvania State Police Office of Chief Counsel, and at Tibbott and Richardson, P.C. She was admitted to the Pennsylvania Bar in 2023. Prior to joining Evey Black Attorneys, Ms. Edmiston worked as an Associate Attorney with Margolis Edelstein, and most recently, as the Staff Attorney at Your Safe Haven, Inc., where she primarily practiced in Family Law related matters. During her time at Your Safe Haven, Inc., Ms. Edmiston served as Vice President of the Bedford County Bar Association and served as a member of the Bedford County Board of Arbitrators and the Bedford County Co-parenting Committee. She plans to become involved in the Blair County Bar Association and associated committees in the near future. Her writing has been published in the Pennsylvania Family Lawyer, the Pennsylvania State Police Communicator, and Spectrum, and she enjoys volunteering with various community organizations. She currently concentrates her practice in Family Law (Custody, Visitation, Divorce, Property Division, Alimony, Child Support and Spousal Support) and under the guidance of the experienced attorneys of Evey Black intends to expand into other areas of the practice of law as well.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law / Divorce Lawyers in Hatboro, PA
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Michael E. Eisenberg has been serving the Philadelphia Metropolitan area since 1987. He has practiced in Federal Court, the county trial courts, commonly known as the Courts of Common Pleas, and Bankruptcy Court.

He has practiced in the local magisterial District courts and he is therefore familiar with the practices and rules of the trial courts and local magistrates. Attorney Eisenberg has practiced before the Superior Court of Pennsylvania and is familiar with the need to appeal a final order to a higher court for review of the trial court's decision, should that decision not be based upon law or fact.

Attorney Michael E. Eisenberg's practice philosophy is based upon responsiveness to client needs, client goals and navigating the often complex legal system. In order to offer full service, Attorney Eisenberg will obtain the important facts from the initial interview and explore the facts and circumstances during the representation. Attorney Eisenberg believes that there is a balance to be struck between an aggressive approach to representation as well as the need to balance that with reasonable use of billed time and expenses.

Attorney Michael Eisenberg's staffs are experienced professionals who are devoted to the same practice philosophy as Attorney Eisenberg. They are knowledgeable, responsive and accessible. Dianne Sebald has over 30 years of experience in the areas of personal injury, family law, estate administration and general legal practice. Lynn Killen, who is a degreed paralegal with over 20 years of experience.

attorneys.name: Susan Levy Eisenberg
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Langhorne, PA
attorneys.bio:
For three decades, Susan Levy Eisenberg has been one of the top matrimonial attorneys in Bucks and Montgomery counties. She has an excellent reputation as an experienced, caring advocate. "Matrimonial law is a very specialized field," she relates. "Having the right lawyer can make or break your case."

Susan points out to her clients that if both parties in a divorce case fight like cats and dogs over every single issue, "The lawyers rack up their fees." She relates that "As an advocate, you want to aggressively pursue your client's claims but you do it in a rational and reasonable manner. The best course of action for an attorney, in a matrimonial action, is to protect your client's rights while you resolve their case quickly and amicably, if possible. You litigate when you have to, but you point out to your clients that a trial is the last and most expensive resort."

She notes that in a matrimonial case the most important and personal issues of a person's life are at stake, such as children, money and assets like the marital home. It is a very emotional situation, and the clients need someone that they can lean on and trust. If the clients get too emotional, they will feel it in their pocketbook. Susan tells her clients to: "Let me handle the stress for you, that's what I'm here for."

Susan says "As your advocate, I come up with a plan to protect your interests. If a financial advisor is needed, we call them in. I discuss with my client what is worth litigating over. I help the client make informed decisions about what they can expect if they take several different paths with their case. I have extensive trial experience, and I give my best opinion to the client as to whether the case will have to go to trial or if an amicable resolution is possible."

She points out that a person just thinking about ending his or her marriage should contact an attorney for advice. "If you act too late then the other party can rush to close bank accounts, cancel credit cards and empty safe deposit boxes."

It is very important for a person to really know their financial situation. "Don't just sign the joint tax return, get a copy of it and read it over. Check out the credit card statements. Know what your monthly expenses are. If the kids are in school, do you know what it costs per year?"

Custody, visitation, child support, spousal support and the distribution of marital assets are all topics of interest that must be resolved. "You must remember," Susan states. "In a divorce you're sharing your child's time, and splitting your assets and your income. The lawyer's job, as your advocate, is to get you out as whole as possible."

Susan is an advocate of counseling for parents and children who are going through a divorce. "There is a psychological impact here for all parties involved. A good, caring therapist can be invaluable to a family in turmoil and can help them cope."

When asked to describe her manner in handling matrimonial cases, Susan says "I try to be empathetic and I try to be there for the client to work with. I am very conscious of the cost of a divorce and I strive to protect my client's money. I make myself available to my clients because I know how draining the entire process is. I'm tough if I have to be, but I always try to get the other side to see that there can be a better way. I am very lucky to have such a caring staff and I think that I have a great location for my office in Newtown."

She points out that, "In life, the greatest emotional trauma, short of death of a loved one, is going through a divorce. If I can protect my client and make them as whole as possible at the end of it, then I have done my duty to them."

attorneys.bio:
Doug practices in the areas of toxic tort, products liability, aviation, FELA and premises liability. He has extensive experience defending a variety of toxic tort matters on behalf of manufacturers, suppliers, distributors, contractors and premises owners throughout the country. Doug has served as national trial counsel for companies named in asbestos lawsuits. In addition, he has served as national coordinating counsel for a manufacturer of asbestos-containing products which required him to manage tens of thousands of active cases.

Doug has particular experience in defending fixed-wing and rotary aircraft manufacturers. In addition to securing voluntary dismissals of these clients, he has successfully argued summary judgment for these manufacturers under the Government Contractor Defense.

Doug has experience representing Class One railroad defendants in a variety of claims including FELA claims, occupational disease claims, premises liability claims and real property issues.

attorneys.name: Jessica A. Ellel
attorneys.practice_type: Health Care Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
Chair of Houston Harbaugh's Health Law Practice, Jessica works almost exclusively with health care entities and health practitioners. She has extensive experience with:

• Drafting and negotiating physician employment agreements from both the physician and employer perspectives

• Negotiating contracts between physicians and hospitals

• Preparing purchase agreements to govern the sale of medical practices

• Advising on corporate governance issues, from practice formation to dissolution

• Developing comprehensive compliance plans for physician practices, hospitals, third-party billing administrators, and other health care and related entities

• Organizing strategies for compliance with fraud and abuse laws

• Addressing HIPAA compliance

Jessica is especially well-versed in HIPAA compliance and authors numerous client updates and bulletins on the subject. She conducts on-site and remote HIPAA training and also maintains Houston Harbaugh's HIPAA compliance manual, " Federal HIPAA Privacy Standards Simplified: A Comprehensive Tool-Kit".

As an outgrowth of her work with non-profit health care entities, Jessica also helps non-profit organizations and foundations with their corporate affairs, such as obtaining and maintaining 501(c)(3) tax-exempt status and handling regulatory compliance matters. Her experience in the non-profit industry includes serving as counsel during the merger of several multi-state non-profits into one regional entity which required communication and information sharing with the Pennsylvania Attorney General's Office to obtain approval for the transaction.

Jessica frequently publishes articles and presents on issues relating to physician employment agreements, the Affordable Care Act, and other compliance issues. She has published articles in the Allegheny County Medical Society Bulletin and in the Physicians News Digest.

Jessica is also an adjunct professor at the University of Pittsburgh School of Law teaching the course Legal Aspects of Health Care Compliance.

She draws her thirteen years of experience from both large and small law firms, where she earned her reputation as one of the highest rated personal injury lawyers in Western Pennsylvania. Eve has successfully represented injured clients in matters involving wrongful death, negligent security, liquor liability, premises liability, medical malpractice, nursing home negligence, as well as catastrophic trucking and motor vehicle accidents. In addition, she has represented workers across Western Pennsylvania that have been catastrophically injured on the job. To date, Eve has recovered over twelve million dollars in combined verdicts and settlements for her clients.

Eve’s hallmark is her deep compassion and personal attention given to her clients. Through experience she has learned the importance of connecting with her clients so she can effectively tell their story. During the course of representation, clients come to trust that Eve has their best interest at heart, not only by how hard she fights for them but by her sound process, consistent communication and effective advocacy.

In recognition of her tremendous results for her clients, Eve was accepted to the Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum, which is reserved for attorneys who have achieved resolutions in excess of two million dollars on a single matter. In addition, she is a member of the Academy of Trial Lawyers of Allegheny County, a prominent invite-only organization of distinguished lawyers. She has been named “Top 40 under 40” by the National Trial Lawyers Association in 2019, 2020 and 2021 and “Top 25” in Workers’ Compensation.

Within the legal community, Eve invests her time in organizations that dedicate their mission to “justice for all”, serving on the Board of Governors for the Pennsylvania Association for Justice, and as a Council Member for the Civil Litigation Council of the Allegheny County Bar Association. She also holds memberships with the Western Pennsylvania Trial Lawyers and the Allegheny County Bar Association.

While originally from North Carolina and a proud alumna of the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, Eve is proud to call Pittsburgh home. After college she completed an intensive yearlong language immersion program at the Beijing Institute of Education. Thereafter she pursued her lifelong dream of becoming a lawyer, attending the Thomas R. Kline School of Law at Duquesne University, where she was the Founder and Executive Editor of the Duquesne Criminal Law Journal. Eve was also recognized early on for her outstanding courtroom and oratory skills, being awarded the CALI Award for Excellence in Trial Advocacy and the regional champion of the American Bar Association Arbitration Competition.

Outside of law, Eve is a highly involved member of St. Nicholas Greek Orthodox Church in Oakland. She dedicates her time leading the Oratorical Festival, an annual competition where students write and deliver speeches, progressing from local parishes to a national stage. Eve made nationals as a teenager, an early sign of her natural oratory ability. She also sits on the Board of Philoptochos, a women’s organization whose purpose is service, helping the less fortunate both locally and across the world. She also teaches Greek dancing to the children who perform at the annual Greek food festival.

Eve has always had a passion for foreign languages. She speaks fluent Greek and is highly conversational in Mandarin Chinese. These skills have enabled her to represent numerous international clients that need legal guidance in their native language.

Eve lives in the North Side with her husband and two young boys. She is active in the North Side community and participates in the North Side Chamber of Commerce. She spends many of her weekends cheering on her boys as they engage in a multitude of sports and also enjoys the Pittsburgh restaurant scene, especially in the vibrant North Side. She also loves to travel with her family, including to Greece and Italy.

attorneys.name: Daniel P. Emkey
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in West Reading, PA
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Emkey is a lifelong resident of Berks County. After graduating from Holy Name High School, Mr. Emkey went to Alvernia College where he majored in Criminal Justice. While attending Alvernia College, Mr. Emkey was a member and President of the St. Thomas More Honor Society, Alpha Phi Sigma (National Criminal Justice Honor Society), and was an All-American Scholar. Mr. Emkey graduated cum laude.

Upon earning his undergraduate degree, Mr. Emkey earned his Juris Doctorate from Widener University School of Law. At Widener Law, Mr. Emkey was a member of the Harrisburg Civil Law Clinic and also participated in the Intensive Trial Advocacy Program.

Following his passion for criminal law and litigation, Mr. Emkey found his success as a Berks County Assistant District Attorney, where he spent the majority of his time in the courtroom prosecuting major criminal cases. In total, Attorney Emkey prosecuted hundreds of cases ranging from child sexual abuse, rape cases, felony gun and drug cases, burglary, and aggravated assault. Attorney Emkey quickly gained the reputation of being an aggressive yet compassionate attorney.

Although Attorney Emkey enjoyed the public position of the District Attorney's office, he felt his skills could be better utilized by helping people in the private sector, therefore, he joined the law firm of Sodomsky and Nigrini where he practiced criminal defense. While at Sodomsky and Nigrini, Mr. Emkey defended hundreds of clients in over 15 counties (in PA) with charges ranging from summary offenses to attempted murder.

In 2009, Attorney Emkey started his own law firm based on the principles that people's rights come first and that a law firm should be primarily committed to the client.

Mr. Emkey is a member of both the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers and the Pennsylvania Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers. Mr. Emkey was an Adjunct Professor at Alvernia College in 2008, teaching Criminal Law. He has also spoken at numerous events and functions in Berks County. Attorney Emkey is a member of the Berks County Bar Association, the Pennsylvania Bar Association and the American Bar Association.

attorneys.name: Ann E. Endres
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Reading, PA
attorneys.bio:
Ann is a native of Berks County who was raised in Birdsboro and graduated from Central Catholic High School. She received her Bachelor of Arts in Political Science from the University of Pittsburgh in 1993, and her Juris Doctorate from Widener University School of Law in 1996, where she graduated cum laude. In law school, Ann was a member of the law review for Widener’s Delaware Journal of Corporate Law. Ann was also a member of the Phi Delta Phi legal fraternity.

Ann began her legal practice as an associate at Henry & Beaver LLP in Lebanon County, Pennsylvania, where she concentrated her practice in the area of family law. Ann returned to Berks County in 2002 when she became Special Counsel for the Domestic Relations Section of Berks County. While with Domestic Relations, Ann helped develop and implement policies and assisted clients with support and paternity matters, including inter-state and intra-state support matters.

In 2004, Ann returned to private practice concentrating in the area of family law. In 2005, Ann joined Dawn Palange to form Palange & Endres, P.C., where she continued her focus on clients dealing with divorce, separation, custody, and support issues.

Ann is a member of the Pennsylvania Bar Association, Family Law Section, the Berks County Bar Association, Family Law Section, and the Justice William Strong American Inns of Court.

Ann resides in Sinking Spring with her husband, Eric, and their two children. Ann enjoys reading, skiing, theater and music, and spending time with her family.

attorneys.name: Kelly L. Enders
attorneys.practice_type: Auto Collisions Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Kelly Enders is the managing partner at Caroselli, Beachler & Coleman, L.L.C. She graduated from the University of Pittsburgh in 1988 with a Bachelors of Science degree in political science. She continued her studies at the University of Pittsburgh in the Psychology in Education Master's Program and the Duquesne University School of Law where she earned her J.D. in 1998.

She is admitted to practice in Pennsylvania and the U.S. District Court, Western District of Pennsylvania.

Attorney Enders is a civil trial attorney and has trial experience in cases involving auto collisions' premises liability, tractor-trailer collisions, product liability, assault, battery, intentional infliction of emotional distress, false imprisonment and negligent hiring. In addition to the above, her case experience also includes bad faith insurance, breach of contract, civil rights, mental health malpractice, negligent entrustment of a firearm, medical malpractice, negligent security, mold, asbestos, Federal Torts Claim Act, Federal Employers' Liability Act, and actions involving the Commonwealth and local agencies.

Her jurisdiction experience includes Pennsylvania state and federal courts, West Virginia Federal Court and Ohio state courts. She has experience handling various state subrogation issues arising under Pennsylvania, Ohio, West Virginia, Florida, Indiana and California state law, as well as federal subrogation issues.

Attorneys Enders was selected to be included in the Pennsylvania Super Lawyers list of Rising Stars in both 2006 and 2007, and as one of the top 5 percent of attorneys in Pennsylvania in 2013, 2014, 2015 and 2016. She was listed by Best Lawyers in America for both Personal Injury Litigation and Product Liability Litigation in 2013, 2014, 2015 and 2016.

She is a member of the Allegheny County Academy of Trial Lawyers, Allegheny County Bar Association (member, Judiciary Committee 2007-2010), Pennsylvania and American Bar Association, Western Pennsylvania Trial Lawyers Association, the Pennsylvania Association for Justice (member, Board of Governors 2007-2013) and the American Association for Justice.

Attorney Enders is also very active in Pittsburgh and the surrounding communities through her involvement since 2001 with the nonprofit volunteer group, The Junior League of Pittsburgh (Board of Directors 2004-2006, Executive Board 2007-2008), and as a former member of the Advisory Council for the nonprofit organization, Strong Women Strong Girls.

attorneys.name: Roger M. Epstein
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Offices of Brian E. Quinn
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
I grew up in the East Oak Lane section of Philadelphia. While in law school, I clerked for a small firm in their labor and employment law department.

After being admitted to the Pennsylvania Bar in 1989, I did work in the fields of toxic tort litigation and labor law. I then worked for eight years for the law firm that held the legal services contract to represent Philadelphia Police Officers. There, I concentrated in Domestic Relations cases, including Divorce, Protection from Abuse, Child Custody and Support. I also represented members of the Fraternal Order of Police in disciplinary matters before the Internal Affairs Division.

Since joining the Law Offices of Brian E. Quinn in 2003, I continued to specialize in Family Law matters in Philadelphia, Delaware, Bucks and Montgomery Counties. I also handle Social Security disability claims.

My approach to Family Law cases is to first negotiate with the other party (or their counsel). I find that working together to reach an agreement, particularly in custody and divorce cases, is often the best solution. It also saves a client in attorney fees. However, if the other party is unwilling to negotiate, I am always prepared to fight in Court to obtain the best result.

In child and spousal support cases, I work hard to obtain the maximum level of support for parties seeking support, and work equally as hard to prevent defendants in support cases from having unreasonable or exorbitant orders entered against them.

I can handle your divorce if it is a simple no-fault or consent divorce, or a complex divorce matter involving property division and alimony. While I have negotiated very favorable settlements for numerous clients, I will also fight in Court for what you are entitled to. Having practiced Family Law for nearly 25 years, I am familiar with the Judges and Masters who hear domestic relations matters and know what arguments they find persuasive.

In my Social security practice, both individuals who were gainfully employed until they recently became disabled due to a physical or mental health problem, and individuals with no prior work history and minimal additional household income who are seeking Social Security Supplemental Security Income benefits. In the majority of cases. I am able to obtain Favorable decisions.

In my cases, whether family law or social security, I meet with my clients personally. I will evaluate and assess your matter, and discuss with your best options. My experience will help you to get your best result. Let me work for you!

LEGAL EXPERIENCE

Represented Philadelphia Police Officers through their Legal Services Plan (1995-2002)

Family Law

Labor Law

Civil Litigation

attorneys.bio:
Gordon Erdenberger has been assisting clients with legal advice and litigating civil cases for plaintiffs and defendants - from simple to complex - for more than 29 years in all the county courts of southeastern Pennsylvania and the Federal District Court in Philadelphia.

Newly based at the Farm office complex located just outside Doylestown off Route 202 in the county seat of Bucks County, our offices are easily accessible for all, with easy parking. We represent individuals and business entities in Bucks, Montgomery, Delaware, Northampton, Lehigh, Chester and Philadelphia counties.

You can access us electronically through our website (www.buckscountylawyer.com); by fax (215-489-5009); email (gerdenberger@buckscountylawyer.com); telephone (215-489-7506); or in person at The Farm @ Doylestown. We will respond promptly to all inquiries.

All consultations are confidential. We do not charge for initial consultations before we mutually agree to enter into a lawyer-client relationship.

If we do agree to a lawyer-client relationship, you will receive written confirmation of the arrangement and any fees to be charged. Our rates are competitive and reasonable.

You will receive timely and periodic reports on the status of your case. You will not have difficulty communicating with us or getting a prompt response.

You are not obligated to engage us as your attorneys unless you are comfortable with our proposals for your representation.

We stand ready to listen to your problem(s) and recommend solutions - whether you are an individual, a business entity or an insurance company; whether your problem involves real estate, personal injury, business, internet, consumer, family, legal documents, leases, contracts, discrimination, insurance policies, defective products, collections, professional malpractice or litigation of any kind.

Mr. Evans has served as President of the American Board of Trial Advocates, Western Pennsylvania Chapter since 1998; He is a Past President of the Pennsylvania Trial Lawyers Association and also of its Western Chapter; He is the former Statewide President of Lawyers for Consumer Rights. attorneys.name: Albert J. Evans
attorneys.practice_type: Car Crashes Lawyers in Pottsville, PA
attorneys.bio:
Albert (B.J.) Evans has devoted his entire legal career to obtaining the best results for his clients. For the past 25 years, Attorney Evans has gone into courtrooms throughout Pennsylvania and New Jersey and obtained large monetary verdicts for his clients in civil cases and not guilty verdicts for his clients in criminal cases. Attorney Evans has fought major corporations including, auto manufacturers, hospitals and insurance companies to obtain justice and money for his clients. He has obtained numerous million dollar settlements and verdicts and been named a member of the Million Dollar Advocates Association. Among Attorney Evans’ recent successes, were a $23,000,000.00 settlement in a multiple fatality truck accident, close a $3,000,000.00 settlement in a motorcycle fatality, $1,200,000.00 verdict in Carbon County involving the death of a construction worker, a $1,700,000.00 settlement for a chemical worker who was burned and a $200,000.00 settlement for a mom who sustained a brain injury when a wheelchair lift malfunctioned. In criminal law, Attorney Evans was one of the few lawyers under the age of 30 to have tried a murder case. He has successfully obtained not guilty verdicts for numerous clients charged with serious felony and misdemeanor charges.

Attorney Evans has also represented numerous corporations in commercial litigation and business dealings. Attorney Evans successfully handled commercial lawsuits involving anti-trust, valuation, shareholder disputes and contract interpretation. Attorney Evans has also represented corporations in sales and purchases who values were well in excess of One Million Dollars.

Attorney Evans has been appointed to the Board of the Pennsylvania Trial Lawyers Association. He is a Diplomat of the American Trial Lawyers Association. He is the current Acting Vice President of the Schuylkill County Bar Association. He has, for many years, served on an Advisory Committee to the United States District Court for the Middle District of Pennsylvania. He was nominated and selected to the National Top 100 Trial Lawyers. In 2020 he was selected as a "Super Lawyer" in Pennsylvania.

Attorney Evans has been elected to the Board of Directors of the Riverview Bank, Harrisburg, PA. He has been selected to serve as a Solicitor for multiple municipalities and a water authority. He serves on numerous local non-profit boards such as the Schuylkill Haven Island Committee, Inc. and YMCA. He is a Eucharistic Minister and church council member of the St. Nicholas Ukrainian Catholic Church, Minersville, PA. He regularly volunteers his time in the local community speaking to high school students on legal issues.

Attorney Evans is a 1986 graduate of The Hill School, Pottstown, Pennsylvania. He received his undergraduate degree from Colby College in 1990 and his law degree from Widener University in 1993. Attorney Evans resides in Schuylkill Haven, Schuylkill County, PA with his wife, Dr. Kim Hashin and their two sons, Albe (age 18) and Alan (age 11).

attorneys.name: Steven F. Fairlie Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in North Wales, PA
attorneys.bio:
Steven F. Fairlie has been named one of Pennsylvania's "Rising Stars" as published in Philadelphia Magazine in 2005, 2006 and 2007. He is also one of just a handful of attorneys with offices in the Philadelphia Suburbs to be named a "Lawyer on the Fast Track" by The Legal Intelligencer in 2006.

He has successfully handled numerous civil (slip and fall, auto accidents, land development litigation, etc.) and criminal trials (narcotics, DUI, capital murder, robbery, rape, etc.). Prior to private practice, he worked on the Narcotics Team and the Major Crimes Team of the Montgomery County District Attorney's Office from 1996 to 2000. He successfully argued for the death penalty in 1999 and was lead prosecutor in a case involving $55 million of cocaine. Subsequently, as a defense attorney, he took the appeal of a client sentenced to death and convinced the prosecutor to vacate the death sentence. He used forensic tire print evidence to prove another client not guilty of attempted murder. In yet another case he uncovered evidence which reduced the offer on a robbery case from 25–50 years down to 2 years probation. He represented one individual charged with 3 separate charges of DUI and had the first case dismissed at the Preliminary Hearing, the second accepted into the A.R.D. program, and the third case dismissed after a trial judge granted suppression of all evidence in the case. Mr. Fairlie has obtained not-guilty verdicts in major jury trials involving shootings, burglaries, etc. despite positive eyewitness identifications of his clients. On appeal, he has successfully argued for reversal of a death sentence in one case and a sentence of 70 years in another case.

In 2007, Mr. Fairlie went to trial on a case involving more than $50 million of land transactions and settled the case in the second week of trial. He has obtained six-figure settlements in numerous personal injury cases.

Mr. Fairlie often serves as a speaker for various organizations such as the Pennsylvania Bar Institute's Annual (2007–2009) Criminal Law Symposium in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania. He also teaches numerous other continuing legal education seminars for lawyers every year.

He earned his B.A. in Government and Law from Lafayette College in 1991 and his J.D. from The Dickinson School of Law in 1995 where he was a member of the Appellate Moot Court Board, the Environmental Law Journal, and a Chairman of the Student Bar Association. He has been Chairman or Vice-Chairman of the Montgomery County Bar Association's Criminal Defense Committee since 2001, a member of the Montgomery County Bar Association's Trial Lawyers' Section, a member of the Pennsylvania Bar Association's Professionalism Committee and Civil Litigation Section, a member of the Pennsylvania Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers Hotline Panel of Experts Committee, and an Associate Member of the Philadelphia Bar Association. Mr. Fairlie's areas of practice include civil litigation, personal injury, criminal law and construction litigation.

Mr. Fairlie enjoys scuba-diving, hunting, fishing and coaching youth sports.

attorneys.name: Amee S. Farrell
attorneys.firm_name: Kaplin Stewart Meloff Reiter & Stein, P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Land Use, Zoning & Development Lawyers in Blue Bell, PA
attorneys.bio:
Amee Smith Farrell is a member of the firm's Land Use, Zoning & Development Department. She concentrates her practice in the areas of land use, land development and zoning of commercial, public and residential real estate. Ms. Farrell represents private developers throughout Pennsylvania and New Jersey before municipal boards and state and federal agencies and in state courts. A significant portion of Ms. Farrell's practice focuses on responsibilities under the Pennsylvania Construction Code Act and the International Building Codes. She assists developers in procuring the necessary approvals to undertake development projects and works with developers throughout the construction process to ensure municipal compliance with applicable building code regulations for a timely procurement of construction permits and certificates of occupancy.

Prior to joining the firm, Ms. Farrell was a member of the design staffs at Daley + Jalboot Architects and Cope Linder Associates, both of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. While at Cope Linder, Ms. Farrell's practice centered around commercial development. During her six year tenure at Daley + Jalboot, Ms. Farrell gained extensive experience in the design and construction of public school projects in and around the Philadelphia area, with special focus on public bidding and oversight of multi-prime construction projects.

attorneys.name: Jaclyn Faulds
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
An attorney in the firm's Business Law Group, Jaclyn concentrates her practice in the areas of general business law, corporate governance, commercial and banking transactions, and business planning.

Jaclyn serves as outside general counsel to businesses in various stages of their lifecycles ranging from single owner arts organizations to fitness center start-ups, from mid-level real estate developers to multi-national third generation family manufacturing businesses. Jaclyn also serves as a business mentor and counselor for local non-profits in Western Pennsylvania.

Jaclyn's experience includes entity selection and formation and restructuring, and dissolution, along with reviewing and drafting various other corporate documents including operating agreements, purchase and sale agreements, non-disclosure agreements, employment agreements, settlement and release agreements, promissory notes and security agreements. Jaclyn also works with businesses on daily operational issues such as formulating terms and conditions included on purchase orders, negotiating repayment agreements, and drafting internal corporate internet and social media privacy policies.

Prior to receiving her J.D. and M.B.A. from the University of Pittsburgh, Jaclyn was an artist and worked as a therapist with children coping with developmental disabilities. Jaclyn's undergraduate education in sculpture and subsequent experience as a "starving artist" continues to help her assist her creative clients by navigating the legal side of the arts as a counselor and business mentor.
