attorneys.name: Amy Guth
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Amy Guth, a partner at Kline & Specter, represents plaintiffs in catastrophic injury litigation, where she has a special interest in women's health issues, particularly cases in which women have been provided substandard care or their health has been compromised due to medical error.

In a major case, one documented by ABC's Nightline, Guth helped win a $3 million award from a Montgomery County jury for the estate of a woman who died of breast cancer after a doctor misread her mammogram. Dagmar Lackman, 58, left behind her husband, Thomas, and four children.

In a more recent case, Guth served as co-counsel in reaching a $6.2 million settlement with a Lehigh County hospital for a child who suffered brain damage following tonsil surgery. As part of the November 2006 agreement, the hospital also agreed to implement policy changes to improve safety. (See Bates.)

In a 2003 case Guth helped win a seven-figure settlement for the family of Adam Covenko, a healthy 24-year-old former wrestler who checked into the hospital for a nose job two weeks before he was to be married. During the procedure Covenko was improperly intubated, resulting in a lack of oxygen for several minutes, brain damage and, ultimately, his death.

In 2004, Guth worked on a lawsuit against an anesthesiologist who allowed a patient’s blood pressure to drop too low during surgery, resulting in a stroke and paralysis. The anesthesiologist broke down during cross-examination at his trial and admitted he had provided poor care. A substantial settlement was reached in the case.

In addition to women’s health, Guth also is concerned with children's issues and has been involved in the Support Center for Child Advocates.

Before joining Kline & Specter, she was a shareholder at a large Philadelphia law firm, Post & Schell, where she represented a wide range of prominent medical specialists and hospitals. On behalf of both physicians and hospitals, she litigated a broad spectrum of medical negligence cases.

Guth was a member of the Moot Court Honor Society. She received a B.S. from The American University in 1982 and a J.D. from Widener University Law School in 1985.

She is a member of the Philadelphia Bar Association, the Pennsylvania Association for Justice and the Philadelphia Trial Lawyers Association. She is admitted to practice in Pennsylvania, New Jersey and Florida.

attorneys.firm_name: Summers, McDonnell, Hudock, Guthrie & Rauch, P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Tort and Casualty Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Guthrie is a seasoned litigator with over 33 years of civil trial experience defending claims against individuals, large and small corporations, governmental agencies and insurance carriers in state and federal court. After serving as a law clerk in 1990 to the Honorable Carol Los Mansmann of the United States Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit, Mr. Guthrie entered private practice where he has acquired more than three decades of extensive civil litigation experience.

Since 1990, Mr. Guthrie has successfully tried over 100 jury trials to verdict throughout the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania and he has argued cases before the Pennsylvania Superior Court and Supreme Court. Mr. Guthrie has authored Amicus Curiae briefs on behalf of the Pennsylvania Defense Institute and the Insurance Federation of Pennsylvania advocating legal positions of importance to the insurance industry and the business community.

Mr. Guthrie is a member of the Academy of Trial Lawyers of Allegheny County. He has a peer-review rating of AV-Pre-Eminent® by Martindale-Hubbell® and he has been designated as a Pennsylvania Super Lawyer®.

Mr. Guthrie provides clients with thorough, meticulous and aggressive representation. He believes that careful preparation is the key to achieving successful outcomes for clients. Mr. Guthrie abides by the principle embodied in the ancient Latin phrase "Amat Victoria Curam," which translates to "Victory Loves Careful Preparation."

attorneys.name: Kenneth J. Haber
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
Over the course of the last 25 years, Ken Haber has handled cases involving virtually every type of criminal offense, from DUI and drug possession to health care, computer and wire fraud to murder cases in which the death penalty is sought. Ken has successfully defended over 3,000 clients and has won acquittals before juries and judges in hundreds of cases, including rarely earned jury acquittals in federal court.

A Pittsburgh native, Ken received his undergraduate and law degree from the University of Pittsburgh. While at Pitt, he was a member of law review and graduated near the top of his class. Following graduation, Ken was a prosecutor in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania (Allegheny County) for five years. After transitioning into criminal defense work, he has been representing people who have been charged with crimes in federal and state court for over two decades.

Today, Ken tackles the most complex legal and evidentiary issues facing clients in criminal court. Ken has handled over 50 homicide cases, many of which he has tried to verdict and received acquittals for his clients. In 2017, he earned a Not Guilty verdict in a double homicide that was originally charged by the Commonwealth as a death penalty case. After lodging a defense that challenged the validity of the DNA evidence and the credibility of the eyewitness, the Allegheny County jury returned its verdict after only two hours of deliberation.

Ken’s expertise related to criminal defense extends to both state and federal court. While his practice focuses on the representation of people charged with crimes, it also includes the representation of people who are the subject of an investigation (pre-indictment). Representation at this stage is critical, particularly in federal white-collar investigations, where he has had many clients avoid the filing of charges in such instances. A tenacious litigator, Ken’s case work includes challenging the overreaching of law enforcement in Fourth Amendment issues and protecting the rights of those criminally accused at every stage of the prosecution.

attorneys.name: Richard J. Haber
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Bethlehem, PA
attorneys.bio:
"Dick", as he prefers to be called, has enjoyed 44 years as an attorney, having earned his undergraduate degree from Penn State University, where he served as President of the Student Body in 1960-1961, President of the Pennsylvania Association of Student Governments, fraternity president and a member of several honoraries, including Delphi, Androcles, Skull and Bones, Omicron Delta Kappa, and Lion's Paw. In addition, he served as Vice President and then President of the Freshman Class as well as Drum Major of the Air Force R.O.T.C. Band.

He was graduated from Penn Law in 1964 where he was awarded The Publishers' Cooperative Prize for excellence in fiduciary administration. Four months after graduating, Attorney Haber established his own law firm specializing in estate planning and real estate law. Early in his career, he served as Chief Public Defender in Northampton County and also Chairman of the County Cancer Crusade. Dick was elected President of the Pennsylvania Association of Borough Solicitors Association for five consecutive terms.

As an outgrowth of his hobby growing orchids in his greenhouses, the American Orchid Society elected Dick as an accredited orchid judge in 1990. Each year thereafter, Mr. Haber was invited to judge the world renowned Philadelphia Flower Show, as well as many other national and international venues. Recently, he was elevated to Senior Orchid Judge status.

Pursuing his interest in music, Richard Haber began formal musical training at The Juilliard School in Manhattan at age 65. Mr. Haber, a consistent honor student for four and a half years, is enrolled in the orchestral conducting program under the supervision of Maestro Vincent La Selva, internationally acclaimed conductor and artistic director of The New York Grand Opera, and innovator of the world-renowned "Opera in the Park" series in Central Park, presenting opera for the masses since 1975.

Mr. Haber recently capped his musical career by conducting the "play out'" for both Mary Poppins and Phantom of the Opera ON BROADWAY. This conducting opportunity came at the invitation of Grammy Award Winning Record Producer for Sony Masterworks, David Lai, the principle conductor of Phantom. Dick received "rave" reviews from the audience, cast, and orchestra. On the occasion of his conducting "gig" at Mary Poppins, Gavin Lee (Burt) stopped the show to introduce Dick "as an inspiration to all of us who dream of starting a second career later in life." The conductors of the Liberty High Schools internationally famous Grenadier Band have also honored Dick by inviting him to conduct his own composition America the Melting Pot, selections from Verdi's opera, Aida, Haydn's Surprise Symphony #94 and selections from Bizet's opera Carmen. During one of his guest conducting appearances, Dick told the audience, "I am very moved and inspired by opera owing to the influence of Maestro La Selva, a world authority on Verdi, and I could not be more grateful for the opportunity to conduct such a group of talented student musicians. It has helped me regain my youth." This spring he will be picking up his baton to conduct the Liberty High School Orchestra in Serenada by Leroy Anderson.

Last year, Maestro La Selva granted Mr. Haber leave from Juilliard, in order to revive his ailing law practice, which had suffered during his part time absence. His former firm having disbanded, Mr. Haber took up the private solo general practice of law.

Dick is married to Rosemary, a musical success in her own right, and has two children. Spencer who owns his own hedge fund in Stamford, Connecticut and Jennifer, who is a practicing lawyer, serves people in need in the Annapolis, Maryland area. She also is the adoption coordinator for the Maryland Animal Sanctuary and Rescue Association. The Habers have two grandchildren, Haber and Lauren.

Awards and Honors

Honors

'The Publishers' Cooperative Prize for excellence in fiduciary administration

Attorney Samir Hadeed is a practicing criminal law, personal injury, & auto accidents lawyer located in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Samir graduated with a bachelor's degree from Duquesne University before moving on to receive his law degree from Case Western Reserve University. While Samir was completing his degrees, he had the opportunity to intern in a solicitor’s office and intern for a Judge as well. Both of these offered Samir great insight and experience in the career that he would eventually pursue. Samir was also heavily involved with athletics, specifically hockey as well as track and field while receiving these degrees. He knows the difficulties that student athletes face while at school.

Attorney Samir Hadeed has been practicing criminal defense, personal injury, auto accidents and traffic tickets since 2008. Samir speaks Arabic, Portuguese, Spanish, and Italian. He also plays piano, and is an avid strength athlete/powerlifter. He understands the importance of maintaining balance between his work and personal life and he hopes to continue his successful career moving forward while expanding his knowledge and experience in other areas of life as well.

attorneys.name: Stephen A. Hall
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
Stephen A. Hall joined the firm in January 2026. He primarily defends various product manufacturers, employers, and premises owners in toxic tort litigation.

With over 25 years of experience, Mr. Hall has successfully represented clients in state and federal courts on issues involving personal injury, occupational exposures, estates and trust, professional liability, real estate, insurance disputes, and other commercial litigation. Mr. Hall has also handled various matters before the Third Circuit, the Pennsylvania Superior Court, and the Pennsylvania Supreme Court.

Out of law school, Mr. Hall served for two years as a Judicial Law Clerk to the Hon. John M. Cleland, former President Judge of the McKean County Court of Common Pleas.

Mr. Hall graduated summa cum laude from the University of Pittsburgh in 1996 with a Bachelor’s Degree in Political Science. He went on to receive his Juris Doctor with Distinction from Ohio Northern University in 1999.

While earning his academic credentials, Mr. Hall interned for then Congressman Rick Santorum, the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, and the Supreme Court of Ohio. While in law school, he was invited to join the Law Review, finished as a semifinalist in the 1997 Burke E. Smith Moot Court Competition, and was a member of the William Howard Taft Inns of Court.

attorneys.name: Michael A. Hamilton
attorneys.practice_type: Global Insurance Services Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Mike handles sophisticated and high-exposure insurance coverage claims and litigation. He focuses his practice on environmental, professional liability and business torts/advertising injury claims.

Mike has more than 20 years of experience handling insurance coverage claims and litigation on behalf of major insurers throughout the United States. He has an extensive background in environmental claims under commercial general liability policies and specialty environmental policies. He has assisted clients with claims involving the application of the pollution exclusion, surface and groundwater contamination, ground pollution and hydro-fracking.

Mike also has advised clients on claims involving privacy, intellectual property, false advertising and business torts. He counsels carriers on policy form wording with respect to privacy and intellectual property infringement claims. Mike was involved in two ground-breaking cases holding that claims for faulty workmanship in construction were not covered under CGL policies. He has represented insurance companies in bankruptcy court and has formulated strategies for carriers to best protect their rights when policyholders are in bankruptcy.

attorneys.name: John S. Han
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Norristown, PA
attorneys.bio:
Born in Seoul, South Korea, John S. Han immigrated to the United States with his parents and younger sister at six. He would later graduate with Class Honors from the University of Michigan with a B.A. in Economics in 1990. John then attended The American University, Washington College of Law, earning his Juris Doctor Degree in 1993. Before graduating from law school, John accepted a commission as an officer in the United States Navy Judge Advocate General's Corps and served on active duty from 1993 to 1999. During his naval service, John successfully performed duties as a defense counsel, prosecutor, and general counsel. As a defense counsel stationed in San Francisco, California, and Naples, Italy, John provided high-quality and zealous representation of Navy and Marine Corps service members charged with serious felony offenses involving murder, sexual assault, drug trafficking, and fraud. He obtained 7sevenfull acquittals in contested trials on behalf of his clients.

John received an Honorable Discharge from the United States Navy in 1999. From 2000 to the present, he has continued his military service in the United States Navy Reserve. Respected for his extensive trial experience, knowledge of the law, and superior writing ability, John was appointed to the bench in 2010. From 2010 to 2014, he served as a Military Trial Judge for the Navy-Marine Corps Trial Judiciary. He presided over felony court-martial cases involving sexual assault, violent crime, drug trafficking, child pornography, and fraud. In addition to his judicial experience, John served as the Commanding Officer of two Reserve units and currently holds the rank of Captain in the United States Navy Reserve. From 2000 to 2006, John served as an Assistant District Attorney for the Philadelphia District Attorney's Office. In this capacity, he prosecuted numerous jury and bench trials in cases involving public corruption, fraud, white-collar crime, and violent crime. John was the lead prosecutor in complex and lengthy grand jury investigations. He also conducted criminal investigations of police officers accused of wrongful use of deadly force, corruption, and civil rights violations.

In December 2006, John left the Philadelphia District Attorney's Office to begin his career as a Trial Attorney in the United States Department of Justice in the Organized Crime and Gang Section. From 2006 to 2021, he investigated and prosecuted major federal RICO and Violent Crimes in Aid of Racketeering cases against national and international organized crime groups, including the Mafia and violent street gangs. From 2008 to 2019, John successfully prosecuted several members and associates of the Philadelphia La Cosa Nostra Family. In these complex and wide-ranging prosecutions of criminal organizations, he acquired substantial experience conducting financial investigations, pursuing wiretap investigations, and charging fraud and money laundering offenses.

John sits on the Board of Directors for the Montgomery Bar Association and is a Judicial Council Member for the National Asian Pacific Bar Association. He was honored when selected to serve on the Federal Criminal Justice Act Panel in the Eastern District of PA. The CJA panel is comprised of attorneys chosen by the Board of Judges who possess the competence, experience, and commitment to provide outstanding criminal defense representation for indigent people facing prosecution in federal criminal cases.

attorneys.name: Alexis C. Handrich

attorneys.bio:
Alexis C. Ouseley is a 2002 summa cum laude graduate from Temple University. attorneys.name: Erin Hanlon
attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Erin Hanlon has extensive experience with litigation involving complex civil matters for clients in the healthcare, pharmaceutical, insurance, and technology industries. Erin joined Dailey LLP after eight years at the Federal Judiciary, where she served as the career law clerk for the Honorable Late Marilyn Heffley, United States Magistrate Judge for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania. During her clerkship, Erin advised on cases in a variety of areas of law from initial pleadings through trial. She also served as a Staff Attorney for the United States Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit where she worked on federal appellate matters. Prior to her experience working for the Federal Judiciary, Erin spent seven years in the litigation practice group at a large international law firm in Philadelphia. Erin uses her experience and variety of perspectives – as an advocate, clerk, and appellate staff attorney – to counsel clients on effective and practical litigation strategies.

Drawing from her experience at the Federal Judiciary where she was involved in and advised on all stages of a case, from initial pleadings through trial and appeal, Erin navigates clients through the development of legal strategy in all phases of litigation. Erin also has extensive experience defending clients in matters involving consumer and healthcare fraud, unfair trade practices, commercial and contract disputes, product liability, and violations related to the federal Anti-Kickback Statute and False Claims Act. Her past work has included defending a group purchasing organization and specialty drug distributor in a case alleging violations of the Anti-Kickback Statute and False Claims Act; defending pharmaceutical clients in litigation involving alleged unfair sales and marketing practices, off-label promotion, Medicaid/Medicare compliance, and federal and state price reporting obligations; and representing a global medical technology company in a Foreign Corrupt Practices Act investigation of its sales and marketing practices.

attorneys.name: Jennifer Gomez Hardy
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Phildelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Jennifer Gomez Hardy is a fearless litigator with top tier law firm experience and a passion for helping victims who suffer from injuries, in many instances catastrophic, resulting from transportation collisions, premises/product defects, workplace accidents, negligent security, slip/trip and falls.

She understands that a moment in time can change the direction of your life. And in these instances, in these most vulnerable of times, Jennifer empowers her clients with knowledge and a concrete plan to move forward.

Jennifer strives not only to obtain the highest possible recovery for her clients, but also to provide them with thorough and vigorous representation of their case both in and out of court, so that their rights and interests have been fully and skillfully protected.

The secret behind her success? Her creative energy and desire to practice law with a deep conviction for justice; her compassion and ability to relate to people across economic, racial, and religious backgrounds; and her relentless work ethic and commitment to fiercely advocate for her clients. She has always represented people not companies or big corporations.

But her story didn’t begin in the courtroom. It started at a very young age with a keen sensitivity to injustice and a compassion for people. From there, it evolved into participating in various groups and political activities that fought for civility and equality through grassroots efforts.

On a personal note, Jennifer remains active in the community and invests time mentoring. She is a board member of the Hispanic Bar Association of Pennsylvania, the Philadelphia Trial Lawyers Association, and the Lawyer Referral and Information Service. She is a recipient of the 2018 Super Lawyers Rising Star Award.

attorneys.name: Kenneth J. Hardin II
attorneys.practice_type: Insurance Defense Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
A graduate of Kalamazoo College and Thomas M. Cooley Law School, Mr. Hardin quickly determined that employment and labor issues were primary concerns for companies attempting to cope with, and grow in, the current legal environment. Focusing initially on employment litigation, he soon developed the requisite expertise to help clients prevent workforce problems by preparing and using employment analysis and evaluation of potential claims.

Mr. Hardin started his litigation career trying premises liability and dram shop claims for carriers and trade group limited liability pools. He now represents numerous insurance companies and their insureds in a wide variety of cases, including, construction claims, automobile claims (first and third party), negligence and intentional tort matters and in actions directly brought by or against a carrier.

Mr. Hardin has tried employment cases, completed trials and arbitrations across the States of Pennsylvania, Ohio & Michigan, including over 65 jury trials and achieving 92% success rate. Mr. Hardin has worked with carriers to develop uniform case handling procedures which expedite and simplify the litigation process, and he strives to ensure that the claims representatives and the clients understand the status and exposure of each case based upon its particular details.

A member of the State Bar of Pennsylvania and Michigan, he is also admitted to practice before the Federal District Courts for the Western District of Pennsylvania, Eastern and Western Districts of Michigan, the United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit, the United States Court of Appeals Third Circuit and the United States Supreme Court. Mr. Hardin is a member of the Litigation, Insurance and Indemnity and Employment Sections of the Bar Associations. He also serves as a labor/employment consultant for several start-up companies in the automobile industry.

attorneys.name: Caitlin E. Harper CELA
attorneys.practice_type: Elder Law Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
Background

Caitlin grew up in Moon Township, Pennsylvania. She graduated summa cum laude from Penn State University with a Bachelor of Science degree in Psychology, and was inducted into the Phi Beta Kappa honorary society. She went on to work in the admissions department of a national skilled nursing facility, where her interest and experience in the area of Elder Law began. She earned a Juris Doctor degree from Temple University James E. Beasley School of Law in Philadelphia. During law school, Caitlin was a member of The Temple Political and Civil Rights Law Review. Ms. Harper clerked for the Honorable Amanda Cooperman of the Philadelphia County Court of Common Pleas. While in law school, Caitlin participated in the Temple University Elder Law Clinic where she represented elderly clients in a variety of matters including preparation of estate planning documents.

Professional

Caitlin is Of Counsel with Julian Gray Associates and assists clients in their Medicaid planning needs including negotiating with the Pennsylvania Department of Public Welfare and long term care facilities. Caitlin also provides counsel on a variety of Veterans benefits issues and in the area of general estate planning. She is a member of the Allegheny County Bar Association and the Pennsylvania Bar Association (Elder Law Section) and the Adult Day Care Services Committee through Valley Care Association located in Sewickley, PA. Caitlin is an author and lecturer for continuing legal education programs sponsored by the Pennsylvania Bar Institute. Ms. Harper has been recognized as a Pennsylvania Rising Star.

Personal

Caitlin resides in Moon Township with her husband and their two children.

attorneys.name: Caitlin Harrington
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
Caitlin Harrington has over a decade of experience in litigating complex medical malpractice cases and also has experience in personal injury, motor vehicle accidents, and other serious injury cases. She has also handled various appellate work, including getting a jury verdict against her client overturned and remanded for re-trial. Caitlin is a voracious advocate for her clients and has earned the respect of her peers with her intelligence as well as her compassion. Caitlin has made it her life-long mission to use the court system to fight for those who are injured and aggrieved.

A graduate of prestigious Wellesley College, Caitlin earned her bachelor’s degree in 2006 with a double major in Political Science and Spanish. She graduated cum laude from American University’s Washington College of Law in 2009. During her time in Law School, Caitlin interned for the Department of Justice, United States Marshals Service and was an Honors Intern with the Federal Bureau of Investigation.

In 2022, Caitlin was voted by her peers as a Pennsylvania Super Lawyers Rising Star, an honor reserved to the top 2.5% of attorneys in Pennsylvania who are under the age of 40 or who have been practicing less than 10 years. She is a member of the Pennsylvania Bar Association, Beaver County Bar Association, and Western Pennsylvania Trial Lawyers Association. Outside of the office, Caitlin is a founding member of Cameron’s KidKnees, an organization raising funds for kidney disease related research and treatment. In her spare time she enjoys spending time with her husband and children, playing soccer, and watching soccer.

attorneys.name: John G. Harshman
attorneys.practice_type: Complex Divorce Litigation Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
John G. Harshman joined Frank, Gale, Bails & Pocrass, P.C. as an associate attorney in June 2015 and was named partner in 2017.

Mr. Harshman is a 1991 graduate of the University of Pittsburgh School of Law. He brings over 24 years of experience in complex divorce litigation, including business evaluation issues.

He serves as Solicitor for the Greater Pittsburgh Police Federal Credit Union and also works with the Policemen's Relief and Pension Fund for the City of Pittsburgh. He also has served as a faculty member of the Pennsylvania Bar Institute and conducts continuing legal education credit lecturing on Municipal Pensions and non-ERISA retirement benefits. Mr. Harshman has also dedicated significant personal time to charitable endeavors such as the Susan B. Komen Race for the Cure and the American Heart Association and the American Kidney Fund. Recently, Harshman was honored as the highest private fundraiser for the American Kidney Fund in 2015.

attorneys.name: Thomas S. Harty
attorneys.practice_type: Complex Contract Disputes Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Thomas S. Harty is a member in the Commercial Litigation Group and focuses his practice on complex litigation across a number of disciplines. Thomas has 25 years of trial experience and has appeared in 16 states and 20 different state and federal courts. Over the course of the past 10 years Thomas has served as lead trial counsel in cases which went to verdict and had collectively more than $1,000,000,000 at stake.

Thomas has a wide range of high-profile trial experience in contract claims, anti-competitive and unfair trade practices act (including Federal Trade Practices Act) matters, business and securities fraud claims, shareholder litigation, complicated estate and guardianship litigation, and business related terminations, including serving as counsel to a:

Trustee in a multi-jurisdictional guardianship, undue influence and fraud which, following a 40 day trial resulting in $30,000,000 verdict.

National transportation agency and it’s principle in defeating claims for damages totaling in excess of $25,000,000 for breach of contract, fraud and conversion.

Retail operator of travel centers on a national basis in defeating claims for damages exceeding $1,000,000 for anti-competitive activities alleged by a competitor.

Private investment and international factoring in obtaining judgment in the amount of $1,321,000 for fraud.

Private equity and investment fund in recovering $3,000,000 for breach of contract.

Hotel operator asserting environmental claims in recovering $7,000,000 in damages caused by a water source contaminated with legionella.

Plaintiff in recovering $1,150,000 on grounds of undue influence, incompetence and fraud in connection with the preparation of a family member’s will.

Contractor in recovering judgments totaling $835,000 against its former employees and a check cashing agency for breach of fiduciary duty and violation of the Check Cashers Regulatory Act of 1993.

Regional lender in recovering in excess of $6,000,000 in connection with a commercial loan fraud.

United States Trustee in obtaining $2,200,000 in a claim filed for negligent misrepresentation and fraud.

Plaintiff in recovering $1,200,000 for breach of contract in connection with the sale of a personnel agency.

Thomas is a member of the American, New Jersey and Philadelphia bar associations. He is a member of the American, Philadelphia, and New Jersey State Bar Associations, and the Association of Trial Lawyers of America. Thomas received his undergraduate degree, magna cum laude, from St. Francis University. He earned his law and master of law degrees, with honors, from Villanova University School of Law.

attorneys.name: John M. Hartzell Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Estates and Trusts Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
As chair of the Estates and Trusts Department, John focuses his legal practice on estate planning, and estate and trust administration. With prior experience as a Certified Public Accountant, John leverages his knowledge of tax law for businesses and individuals in preparing estate and gift tax plans, and works with business owners on their succession planning matters. Additionally, John counsels landowners with oil and gas interests on their tax and estate planning challenges. John is skilled at using sophisticated estate planning techniques to minimize federal and state death taxes, and to transfer wealth in a controlled and efficient manner.

John regularly presents seminars to lawyers, accountants, and financial planners for continuing professional education and general information concerning estate planning, corporate tax and business succession planning, and estate administration matters.

attorneys.name: Stephen G. Harvey
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Steve Harvey is an accomplished litigator and trial attorney. For over 30 years, Steve has represented people, families, companies, and nonprofits in important litigation matters. This includes cases involving contracts and commercial litigation; fraud, defamation, and other torts; intellectual property such as infringement of copyright, trademarks, and trade secrets; executive employment, including non-competes and confidentiality contracts, advancement/indemnification of legal fees and costs, and board and internal investigations; and numerous state and federal statutes protecting environmental laws. Steve has litigated multiple cases that have gained national media attention, most notably a 2005 federal case that upheld the teaching of evolution in public school science class and a 2013 federal case that saved the life of a child and led to changes in organ transplant policy. Although Steve spends most of his time litigating cases and working as a trial lawyer, his clients most appreciate the time he spends counseling them in confidence. Prior to founding his firm in 2013, Steve practiced for 20 plus years, including over ten years as a partner at Pepper Hamilton LLP. Early in his career, Steve worked as a trial attorney for the U.S. Department of Justice in Washington, D.C., where he represented federal agencies in important national civil litigation matters. At the start of his career, Steve served as a law clerk for the late Judge Myron H. Bright of the 8th Circuit U.S. Court of Appeals. He graduated magna cum laude from Villanova University School of Law in 1989, where he served as managing editor of the Villanova Law Review. Steve maintains an active pro bono practice. He has served in leadership positions in the American Bar Association, the Philadelphia Bar Association, and the Temple American Inn of Court. He has submitted numerous amicus curiae “friend of the court” briefs in state and federal courts to support civil and environmental justice causes. He is zealously dedicated to helping his clients with their most pressing legal problems. His law firm motto is to counsel each client as if they are his only client.

attorneys.name: Allison G. Hastings
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Lemoyne, PA
attorneys.bio:
Allison has been an associate attorney at Purdy Law Office for 10 years where she focuses her practice on all areas of family law, including support, custody, divorce, equitable distribution, termination of parental rights, adoption, and paternity. She has also acted as a Guardian ad Litem in contested termination of parental rights and custody matters.

Allison particularly enjoys helping clients resolve their family law disputes outside of court. She is a trained Collaborative Law Attorney and mediator and utilizes this training to help parents and spouses reach agreements that take into account the needs and interests of their families.

She is a past member of the William Lipsitt Inn of Court, past president of the Central Pennsylvania Collaborative Professionals, current chair of the Family Law Section of the Dauphin County Bar association, and member of the Family Law Section of the Pennsylvania Bar Association and the International Academy of Collaborative Professionals.

attorneys.name: John M. Hauser III, Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Latrobe, PA
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Hauser was born and raised in Latrobe and is an integral part of Westmoreland County's legal community. After graduating from Greater Latrobe High School in 1997, he subsequently attended Westminster College, where he graduated cum laude in 2001, attaining a Bachelor of Science Degree in the double-majors of Economics and Political Science. In 2004, Attorney Hauser received his Juris Doctorate from The Law School at Duquesne University and he is admitted to practice before the Pennsylvania Supreme Court and the United States District Court for the Western District of Pennsylvania. Attorney Hauser is a member of the Pennsylvania Bar Association, the Westmoreland Bar Association, and the American Inns of Court. In conjunction with these affiliations, Attorney Hauser serves on the Westmoreland Bar Association Planning Committee, serves on the Board of the Ned J. Nakles Chapter of the American Inns of Court, and serves as Chairman of the Explorer's Committee of the Westmoreland Bar Association. Attorney Hauser volunteers as the Attorney Advisor to the Derry Area High School Mock Trial Team and is also a part time adjunct professor at the University of Pittsburgh at Greensburg. Additionally, he is a member of Holy Family Parish in Latrobe and has volunteered with Westmoreland County Pro Bono Assistance program in every year since his admission to practice law.

After practicing in Latrobe for more than 6 years and Greensburg for more than 2 years, Attorney Hauser returned his practice to his hometown of Latrobe, where he founded Latrobe Law Associates, LLC. Continuing to practice primarily in the areas of family law, criminal law, estate planning, personal injury, and small business organization, John is committed to personal attention to each of his cases, to solving problems for his clients, and to treating all of his clients fairly.

Verdicts and Settlements:

Attorney Hauser has personally tried and or/settled numerous products liability and personal injury cases, including causes of action for a mis-filled prescription causing illness, defective medical devices causing pain, as well as defective mechanisms including a $265,000 settlement against the undisclosed manufacturer of a defective carbon monoxide detector. He also regularly handles dog-bite, automobile, and other personal injury actions. In addition to personal injury cases, Attorney Hauser also represents clients in litigation for property damage and contract disputes. In a suit for the loss of a thoroughbred horse, obtained a settlement of more than seven times the price that was paid for the horse one-year prior to its loss.

Representative Clients:

Attorney Hauser represent persons in need in the areas of personal injury, family law, wills and estate administration, and DUI/criminal law defense. If you have an issue in an area of law that I do not handle, I will be happy to refer you to one of my trusted colleagues to ensure that you have trustworthy, reliable representation.

John M. Hauser, III

attorneys.name: E. Patrick Heffron
attorneys.practice_type: General Insurance Defense Lawyers in Scranton, PA
attorneys.bio:
E. Patrick Heffron is a Partner in Chartwell's Scranton office. Mr. Heffron is a 2001 magna cum laude graduate of Marywood University, receiving a Bachelor of Arts degree. He received his Juris Doctorate from the University of Pittsburgh School Of Law in 2004. Prior to joining Chartwell, Mr. Heffron was a Partner in the Scranton office of Cipriani & Werner. While at Cipriani & Werner, Mr. Heffron represented various Fortune 500 corporations, local corporations including non profits, government entities and individual defendants throughout Northeastern Pennsylvania in arbitrations, mediations and trials. He has also practiced before the Pennsylvania Superior and Commonwealth courts of appeal along with the Third Circuit Court of Appeals. Additionally, Mr. Heffron devotes a sizable practice to the defense of employment matters before the Pennsylvania Human Relations Commission, the United States Equal Employment Opportunity Commission and in Pennsylvania's state and federal courts. Mr. Heffron is also a periodic lecturer on industry topics and developments in his practice areas. Since 2010, Mr. Heffron has been recognized by the publishers of Philadelphia magazine and the Pennsylvania edition of Super Lawyers magazine as a "Rising Star," an honor given to the top 2.5 percent of attorneys in the Commonwealth who are 40 years old or younger or in practice for 10 years or less. He concentrates his practice in general insurance defense, civil litigation, municipal law, labor/employment law, employment discrimination, motor vehicle litigation, premises liability and dram shop liability.

attorneys.name: Arnold Heller
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Law Lawyers in Norristown, PA
attorneys.bio:
Real estate attorney Arnold Heller has a lifetime of experience in real estate transactional law and land development law. He advises various clients, including healthcare providers, condominium and planned community developers, and affordable housing developers.

Arnold counseled these clients on a host of legal matters:

Creation and preservation of affordable housing and luxury housing

Formation and negotiation of partnership and limited liability company agreements

Drafting and negotiation of construction contracts

Purchases and sales of many different types of properties

In addition, he has extensive experience counseling clients concerning various types of financing transactions:

Sale/leasebacks

Conventional and HUD-insured construction and permanent loans

Loans from the Pennsylvania Housing Finance Agency and the Pennsylvania Department of Community and Economic Development

Loans provided by various county and municipal agencies

Heller has lectured on condominium law in Pennsylvania and themes about the Americans with Disabilities Act.

Heller served as a law clerk to Judge Charles R. Richey of the United States District Court for the District of Columbia in 1972-73. He then practiced as an attorney with the Appellate Section of the Tax Division of the United States Department of Justice from 1974-1977. Later Heller served as a Deputy Assistant General Counsel to the Presidential Clemency Board formed by President Fording in 1975. Finally, he was an associate and later a partner in the Philadelphia office of Blank Rome LLP from 1978 through July 2009.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Kelly A. Hemple joined Krasno, Krasno & Onwudinjo in 2015. Kelly has devoted her practice to litigating Pennsylvania workers' compensation cases since she became licensed to practice law in 2003. Prior to joining Krasno, Krasno & Onwudinjo, she was a partner at a major Philadelphia defense law firm where she represented self-insured employers and workers' compensation insurance carriers.

In 2013 Kelly was certified as a Specialist in Pennsylvania Workers' Compensation Law by the PA Bar Association's Section

on Workers' Compensation Law as authorized by the Supreme Court of Pennsylvania.

Kelly has been named a "Top Young Attorney in Pennsylvania" as published in the Rising Star Super Lawyer Section of Philadelphia Magazine every year since 2007 and has lectured on workers' compensation matters. Kelly is licensed to practice law in Pennsylvania.

attorneys.practice_type: Estates and Trusts Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
A Director in the Estates and Trusts Group, Dave concentrates his practice on estate planning, wealth management, and estate administration. As a former certified public accountant, Dave has the knowledge, experience and ability to counsel clients on tax minimization strategies with respect to their estate planning, and provides representation to taxpayers in disputes with the IRS with respect to estate and gift tax issues. He also works with family businesses in transferring ownership between generations, and structuring start-up businesses.

An avid animal lover, Dave is a frequent speaker and author on estate planning for pet owners.

Dave has experience with most estate planning techniques including:

Dynasty trusts

Intentionally defective grantor trusts and GRATs

Family limited partnerships

Revocable and irrevocable trusts

attorneys.name: Terry E. Hess
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in State College, PA
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Terry E. Hess grew up in State College and spent his formative years throughout Central Pennsylvania.

Terry is a 1987 graduate of State College Area High School and 1992 Graduate of The Pennsylvania State University with a B.A. in Journalism and a Minor in Exercise and Sport Science.

Following his graduation from Penn State, Terry was a sports writer & columnist for the Centre Daily Times (1992-94) and Johnstown Tribune-Democrat (1994-1999) where he covered various high school, college and professional sports. Terry left the newspaper business to pursue another passion, the law, in 1999.

In 2002, Terry graduated from Thomas Jefferson School of Law in San Diego, California. Shortly thereafter, he relocated to Cleveland, Ohio, where he began a 14-year legal career that saw him ultimately represent some of northeast Ohio’s most serious felony offenders, including several charged with homicide. Along the way, Terry also represented adult and juvenile defendants charged with DUI, other alcohol and drug offenses, traffic offenses, misdemeanor criminal offenses, and nonpayment of child and spousal support.

In the fall of 2015, Terry returned home to State College intent on opening his own practice to assist people from a region that had given him so much growing up. Terry placed special emphasis on representing college and high school students who, hopefully, were experiencing their first brushes with the law. On January 4th, 2016, Terry opened Terry Hess Law at 119 South Burrowes Street in State College, offering free consultation for everyone and retainer discounts for college and high school students.

Terry is a member of the Centre County Bar Association, Pennsylvania Bar Association and the Pennsylvania Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers. Terry, his wife and two children live in State College.

attorneys.bio:
Kevan F. Hirsch is a principal of the firm and represents a diverse array of clients in resolving their commercial claims and disputes through litigation, arbitration and mediation. A large segment of his practice is devoted to representation of national and regional general contractors, trade contractors, and industrial equipment manufacturers, on all phases of major public and private construction projects in the Delaware Valley from bid protests to post-construction claims.

For insurance clients, Mr. Hirsch has developed expertise in defending bad faith claims against carriers, and regularly represents two insurance groups in actions brought directly against the companies in this region. He has represented insurers and insured in complex commercial lines coverage actions and financial disputes relating to sophisticated insurance products.

For business clients, Mr. Hirsch has handled internal and external disputes, representing shareholders, directors, publicly and closely held corporations in matters involving such issues as dissenters' rights, control premiums, fiduciary duties, contract disputes and business torts and has extensive experience with enforcing non-compete and non-disclosure agreements and protection of trade secrets and intellectual property rights. He also serves as general counsel for clients in the commercial software, advertising and telecom sales industries.

attorneys.name: Margaret M. Hock
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
Margaret Hock, the president/shareholder of the law firm of Thomson, Rhodes & Cowie, P.C., first joined the firm in 1999. As a member of the firm, she has devoted her practice almost exclusively to the defense of workers' compensation claims, in addition to being part of the firm’s estate practice.

Prior to working with Thomson, Rhodes & Cowie, P.C., Ms. Hock was employed by the firm of Freeland & Kronz, where she was involved in general litigation and estate practice, but primarily practiced in the field of workers' compensation, representing employers insured through the State Workers' Insurance Fund, as well as the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, in claims filed under the Occupational Disease Act. In addition, she assisted as local counsel for the Pennsylvania Department of Revenue relative to inheritance tax matters.

Throughout her career, she has been dedicated to working with clients to achieve the most favorable results in a cost effective and efficient manner. Given the nature of her practice, she appears on a regular basis before the Pennsylvania Workers' Compensation Judges and the Workers' Compensation Appeal Board, as well as the Commonwealth Court. She also maintains an active workers' compensation practice in West Virginia. Examples of her work include:

Handling of all aspects of litigation of workers' compensation cases, including but not limited to litigation of cases involving claim, termination, suspension, modification, penalty and review petitions, as well as applications for reimbursement from the Supersedeas Reimbursement Fund.

Providing periodic consultation and advice to clients relative to claims handling and related issues.

Assistance in obtaining and clarifying medical opinions for purposes of litigation on an as-needed basis.

Negotiation of settlements on behalf of clients, including, but not limited to Compromise & Release Agreements, protection of subrogation liens, as well as drafting appropriate settlement-related documents.

Assistance with other employment related documents, such as return to work letters, preparation of job descriptions, or any other type of correspondence or notice on an as-needed basis.

attorneys.name: Philip M. Hof
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Bethlehem, PA
attorneys.bio:
Philip M. Hof is one of the few trial lawyers in the Lehigh Valley who is a board-certified Civil Trial Specialist. Since 2010, Mr. Hof has been recognized nearly every year by Philadelphia Magazine as 1 of the top 100 lawyers in Pennsylvania. Since 2006, Mr. Hof has also been selected by Philadelphia Magazine as one of Pennsylvania’s Super Lawyers — a distinction reserved for only 5% of the attorneys in Pennsylvania.

Mr. Hof is a member of the County Bar Association of both Northampton and Lehigh Counties. In practice since 1980, Mr. Hof represents individuals injured as the result of auto and trucking negligence, and malpractice. His experience includes having served as law clerk for the Northampton County Court of Common Pleas and also serving as President of the Northampton County Bar Association. He is a governor, lifetime ex officio, of the Pennsylvania Association of Justice (formerly known as the Pennsylvania Trial Lawyers Association).

Mr. Hof has earned an AV rating through Martindale Hubbell, the leading national lawyer directory, indicating the highest rating for competency and ethics that is awarded.

Following the attacks on 9/11, Mr. Hof was recognized by the Association of Trial Lawyers of America for his pro bono representation before the September 11 Victim Compensation Fund of the family of an electrical engineer who perished when the Twin Towers collapsed.

Mr. Hof is a Senior Hearing Officer for the Pennsylvania Supreme Court’s Lawyer Disciplinary Board.

Mr. Hof has served and continues to serve as a faculty member for continuing education seminars for legal professionals, including seminars organized by the Pennsylvania Association for Justice, Northampton County Bar Association and Bar Association of Lehigh County.

Mr. Hof is a President of the Donald E. Wieand Barristers’ Inn of Court of Lehigh County. In 2016, he was appointed by Governor Tom Wolf to serve as a member of the Governor’s Regional Advisory Commission on qualifications of candidate for judge.

In addition, Mr. Hof has a wealth of experience with alternative dispute resolution, including mediation and arbitration, is an Mcare-approved mediator and is affiliated with ADR Options, Inc. He has been appointed and serves as an approved arbitrator for the federal District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania.

As a highly respected legal mind, Mr. Hof is eager to help and defend those in need and honored to represent his community in the greater Lehigh Valley. Mr. Hof takes pride in successfully aiding clients in Allentown, Bethlehem, Easton and all neighboring communities throughout the Lehigh Valley.

Mr. Hof lives in Palmer Township. He is married and has one son, two daughters, five grandchildren and two beloved Golden Retrievers. He enjoys running, having completed three New York City Marathons and, in 2007 and 2012, the Philadelphia Insurance Triathlon as a member of the Leukemia & Lymphoma Society’s Team In Training.

Rob has appeared in federal courts in the District of New Jersey, the District of Delaware, the Southern District of Illinois as well as the District of Indiana. After relocating to Lycoming County, Rob joined the firm as Of Counsel. In 2012 he became the managing shareholder for the firm.

Rob’s criminal practice concentrates on serious felony criminal charges, drug offenses, homicides, and federal criminal defense.

attorneys.name: Isaac A. Hof
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Bethlehem, PA
attorneys.bio:
Isaac Hof is proud to be an active trial attorney who practices in the Lehigh Valley and throughout Pennsylvania. He understands the importance of helping his clients navigate the legal challenges so often brought on by sudden tragedy. Equally important, Isaac knows what it takes to obtain the results his clients need to help them move forward with their lives.

Isaac has successfully represented injured victims in a variety of personal injury matters, including motor vehicle accidents (car, tractor-trailer, bus, motorcycle, pedestrian, and bicycle), premises liability (slip / trip and fall accidents), nursing home neglect, medical malpractice, FELA claims (railroad accidents), and products liability. He has litigated numerous claims at the municipal, arbitration and trial court levels throughout Pennsylvania. Isaac also serves as an Arbitrator for the Court of Common Pleas Northampton County Compulsory Arbitration program.

Isaac graduated summa cum laude from Temple University Beasley School of Law in 2012, where he received recognition for graduating with one of the five highest GPAs in his class. Prior to joining the firm, Isaac served as a judicial law clerk for the Honorable Legrome D. Davis in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania and subsequently practiced civil litigation at Stradley Ronon Stevens & Young, LLP in Philadelphia.

When not practicing law, Isaac enjoys spending time with his family, playing golf, and rooting for the Philadelphia Eagles. Isaac also is an avid runner. In 2018, he completed the AACR Philadelphia Marathon – a 26.2 mile race throughout the city of Philadelphia.

attorneys.name: Karen Hoffmann
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Karen Hoffmann represents a wide variety of clients in state, federal, and administrative matters including immigration, environmental, FOIA/PA Right-to-Know Law, Federal Tort Claims Act/Section 1983 actions, and general civil litigation.

Prior to joining Ellenberg Law Group, Ms. Hoffmann managed Syrena Law, a Philadelphia solo practice. With Aldea – The People’s Justice Center, she helped create precedential Third Circuit case law on past persecution (Herrera-Reyes v. Attorney General, 3d Cir. 2020). Ms. Hoffmann also worked with Aldea to represent families detained at the Berks immigration prison. Her team received the 2019 Pro Bono Award from the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois for litigation to reunite families separated at the border.

Prior to attending law school at Temple University, she worked as a journalist covering human rights and the environment in Latin America and the Caribbean. Her work has appeared in The Guardian, Earth Island Journal, and The Ecologist.

Ms. Hoffmann speaks Spanish and Portuguese.

attorneys.name: Michael K. Hollinger
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Wyomissing, PA
attorneys.bio:
Born and raised in Lehigh County, Attorney Hollinger later attended the University of Scranton where he graduated with high honors in 1993. During the summer of 1993, he worked as a legal intern with the New York City law firm of Shearman and Sterling. He next attended Widener University School of Law where he again graduated with honors while serving as a member of the editorial board of the University's prestigious Law Review.

Upon his graduation in 1996, Attorney Hollinger came to Berks County where he served as Judicial Law Clerk to President Judge Scott D. Keller (ret.) of the Berks County Court of Common Pleas. In 1998, he entered the private practice of law where he gained extensive experience in the areas of family law, criminal defense, estates, and workers compensation litigation. During this time, he dedicated himself to the compassionate yet aggressive representation of his clients.

In 2009, Attorney Hollinger opened his own law firm. Over the next ten years, he litigated hundreds of cases in numerous Counties across the commonwealth, as well as argued appeals matters in the Pennsylvania appellate courts. In 2019, Attorney Hollinger briefly returned to public service where he served as the primary judicial law clerk to over one dozen Senior Judges from across the Commonwealth-assisting each of the judges in various family, criminal, and civil matters.

Upon joining Rowe Law Offices, Attorney Hollinger brought with him successful and extensive litigation and trial experience. He continues his aggressive yet compassionate representation for each of his clients and continues to focus his practice in the areas of family law, criminal defense, and estates.

Attorney Hollinger lives locally with his wife and daughter and their family cat, Stormi. In his free time, he enjoys playing tennis, martial arts, cooking, and spending quality time with his family.

attorneys.name: Prince Holloway
attorneys.practice_type: Automobile and Trucking Accidents Lawyers in Cheltenham, PA
attorneys.bio:
As an Associate at Stampone Law, Prince is dedicated to standing up for both the injured and the innocent. He is the unique attorney that practices and produces results in both plaintiffs' civil litigation and criminal defense.

Prince's civil practice concentrates on helping catastrophically injured persons obtain the compensation they deserve. Prior to joining Stampone Law, he served as an Associate at a well-respected personal injury firm based in Philadelphia. In this role, he gained invaluable trial experience and developed an interest in representing children and the elderly who were abused and neglected in the foster care and nursing home settings. He has also successfully represented numerous individuals injured by motor vehicle accidents, slip and falls, and medical negligence.

With respect to his criminal practice, Prince represents clients facing all manner of criminal charges, including DUIs. Having previously served as an Assistant District Attorney in Montgomery County, he successfully prosecuted DUI cases and major felony crimes, including attempted murder, aggravated assault, and narcotics violations. This varied and extensive experience further demonstrates Prince's trial expertise, as well as his thorough understanding of how to build a strong case through investigation and evidence gathering.

Prince is currently licensed to practice law in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania; the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania; and the State of New Jersey.

Born and raised in Philadelphia, Prince is a loyal Philadelphia sports fan. He enjoys playing basketball and flag football, as well as attending concerts. Prince lives in the East Falls section of Philadelphia with his wife and his daughter, Charlie.

attorneys.name: Nathaniel M. Holmes
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Camp Hill, PA
attorneys.bio:
Nathaniel M. Holmes is a magna cum laude graduate of The Pennsylvania State University and a 2004 cum laude graduate of Widener University School of Law. A former officer in the United States Army, Mr. Holmes was Chief of the Bureau of Workers’ Compensation Division of Claims Management from June, 2002 through April, 2005. In that capacity he was responsible for managing a staff of over 60 managerial, supervisory and clerical personnel. He conducted training sessions for insurers, employers and third-party administrators addressing all aspects of the Pennsylvania Workers’ Compensation Act and accompanying Regulations. He was responsible for processing all claims forms filed under the Act and for monitoring industry performance to ensure statutory and regulatory compliance. From July, 1999 through June, 2002 he was the Manager of the Claims Management Division during which time he managed one supervisor and 12 clerical staff, and was responsible for processing over 50,000 petitions per year. Before advancing into management, he worked at the Bureau from December, 1993 through July, 1999 as an Administrative Assistant. In that capacity he communicated with attorneys and insurers and employers in order to resolve a variety of disputes and researched, analyzed and responded to questions posed by members of the general public regarding application of the Workers’ Compensation Act and its Regulations. Mr. Holmes joined the Harrisburg office of The Chartwell Law Offices, LLP on May 2, 2005.

attorneys.name: Nichole Camiso Holmes, Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Insurance Defense Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
Ms. Holmes is a seasoned litigator who has almost twenty years of experience as a trial attorney. She has dedicated her career to insurance defense litigation with concentrated experience in construction site/pharmaceutical site accidents, construction defect, wrongful death, traumatic brain injury, products liability, toxic tort, premises/commercial premises liability, insurance coverage, SIU/fraud, DRAM shop liability, professional liability, public entity liability, employment law, education law, Title IX matters, special education/regulatory federal law (IDEA, FAPE), transportation law, and motor vehicle accidents. Ms. Holmes has a wealth of experience representing clients at all stages of trial, mediation and arbitration at the federal, state and national/administrative law levels, skills which are essential to our litigation practice. Ms. Holmes has also represented clients in civil rights and due process matters before various judicial and quasi-judicial forums throughout the country.

Ms. Holmes is passionate about the work that she does and is remarkably dedicated. In the interests of public service, Ms. Holmes serves as an arbitrator for the Superior Court of New Jersey. She is also an advocate for those who cannot defend themselves, assisting with animal rescue personally and professionally, on a pro bono basis.

Ms. Holmes received both her undergraduate degree and law degree from Temple University, where she successfully represented Temple Law at a competitive level in both trial advocacy and appellate work, earning her several accolades and awards.

Ms. Holmes has experience at the State, Federal, and Appellate levels, and is admitted to practice in the States of New Jersey and Pennsylvania, as well as the United States District Court of New Jersey. She has represented clients nationally in both administrative and legal proceedings on a pro hac vice basis, giving her a diverse familiarity with litigation mechanisms nationwide.

attorneys.name: James A. Horchak
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Greensburg, PA
attorneys.bio:
James A. Horchak is an associate at the firm and concentrates his practice in the areas of Estate Planning and Estate Administration.

Mr. Horchak received his B.S. from Saint Vincent College in 1992, where he majored in Business Administration and minored in Finance, and his J.D. from Duquesne University School of Law in 2000. He was a published member of the Duquesne Law Review.

Mr. Horchak has been a Certified Public Accountant since 1995. Before becoming a lawyer, he was an accountant with Sarp & Company for two years, Datemasch Milano & Associates for four years, and Deloitte & Touche for three years. He is a member of the Pennsylvania Institute of Certified Public Accountants.

Mr. Horchak is admitted to practice before the courts of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, the United States District Court for the Western District of Pennsylvania, the United States Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit, the United States Tax Court, and the Supreme Court of the United States.

Mr. Horchak is a member of the Westmoreland County and Pennsylvania Bar Associations. He is a member of the Orphans’ Court and Real Estate Committee of the Westmoreland County Bar Association. He is a past chair of the Young Lawyers and Business/Employment Law Committees of the Westmoreland Bar Association.

Mr. Horchak was recognized by his peers as a Pennsylvania Super Lawyer in 2016 and 2017 as a “Rising Star” in 2005, 2006, and 2010. He was also honored as an Outstanding Young Lawyer of the Westmoreland Bar Association in 2005.

Mr. Horchak grew up in South Greensburg Borough. He graduated from Greensburg Salem High School in 1988. Other than residing in Allegheny County for a few years during law school, he has resided in Westmoreland County all of his life. He is a member of the St. Bruno Parish in South Greensburg. Mr. Horchak currently resides in Youngwood Borough with his wife, Beth, and their three young children. In his time off, Mr. Horchak enjoys organizing and coaching youth sports, spending time with his family, and watching Steelers games.

attorneys.name: Margaret Zylka House
attorneys.firm_name: Margaret Zylka House, Attorney at Law
attorneys.practice_type: Adoption Lawyers in Connellsville, PA
attorneys.bio:
Margaret Zylka House is a native to the Connellsville community. She obtained her Juris Doctorate from the Duquesne University School of Law where she was a member of the Duquesne Law Review, a prestigious honor working on the university's legal journal staff. While at Duquesne, Ms. House also participated in the NASD Securities Arbitration Practicum, a legal clinic representing elder and low-income investors in NASD Arbitration. She worked as a research assistant to one of the Law School's professors and was employed part-time by a number of Pittsburgh law firms during her graduate education at Duquesne University.

Prior to beginning her legal studies, Ms. House obtained her Bachelor of Science in business management with minors in finance and industrial relations from St. Vincent College, Latrobe, graduating cum laude. She was also a William Rafferty scholar athlete award recipient and captain and four-year letter winner on the Women's Cross-Country team.

Ms. House has been a financial planner with her husband's firm, House Financial Services, for six years prior to opening her law practice. She holds her Series 7, 63 and Health, Accident, and Life Insurance licenses, trading through Trustmont Financial Group in Greensburg, Pennsylvania.

Along with memberships in Allegheny County, Fayette County and Westmoreland County Bar Associations, Ms. House is licensed to practice law by the Pennsylvania Supreme Court and the United States District Court for the Western District of Pennsylvania. Additionally, Ms. House is active in volunteer work within her community, serving on the Board of Directors for both Laurel Highlands Regional Family YMCA and Twin Trees, Inc., a network of group homes for the physically and mentally handicapped. She is an active member of the Mount Pleasant Rotary Club, Braddock Trails Chapter of the Daughters of the American Revolution, and pastoral and finance council member of St. John the Baptist Church, Scottdale.

Margaret resides with her husband, Max, and their son in Bullskin Township. She enjoys reading, running and golfing in her free time.

attorneys.name: Matthew T. Hovey
attorneys.practice_type: Municipal & Government Law Lawyers in Norristown, PA
attorneys.bio:
Matthew practices in multiple different legal areas such as civil litigation, zoning, land use, and real estate with an acute focus on municipal law. His municipal work includes multiple appointments in Montgomery County and Chester County.

His municipal work includes multiple appointments to local zoning hearing boards and solicitorships to townships and boroughs. Matthew's regional municipal appointments currently include:

Spring City Borough: Solicitor

Pottstown Borough: Assistant Solicitor

Limerick Township: Solicitor, Zoning Hearing Board

Lower Pottsgrove Township: Civil Service Commissioner, Zoning Hearing Board

West Pottsgrove Township: Zoning Hearing Board

Oley Township: Conflict Counsel, Zoning Hearing Board

Royersford Borough: Solicitor, Zoning Hearing Board

Upper Providence Township: Conflict Counsel, Zoning Hearing Board

Royersford Borough: Civil Service Commission Member

Matt earned his B.A. at Moravian College in Bethlehem, PA, where he majored in Political Science and minored in History. Politics was a big part of his undergrad, as he served as Treasurer, then President of Student Government.

After undergrad, Hovey earned his Juris Doctorate at Villanova University’s School of Law and was a published member of the school’s distinguished Law Review. He later interned with the Litigation, Civil Rights, and Governmental Department for the Legal Department of the School District of Philadelphia. Hovey also interned with Federal District Judge James M. Munley of the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Pennsylvania.

Matt is the former President of the Board of Directors of Multi Service, Inc. in Boyertown, PA, and presently serves as one of their Vice-Presidents. The non-profit operates the Center at Spring Street, which offers case management, tax preparation, emergency financial assistance, and speech therapy for those in need. They also deliver meals to seniors throughout Montgomery County and Berks County. It also operates The Rickets Center in Pottstown which offers educational, recreational, and wellness activities focusing on after-school programming for Pottstown youth and families.

Matt lives in Chester Springs, PA, with his wife and daughter. He enjoys local sports teams, photography, hiking, and golfing in his free time.

attorneys.name: Robert A. Huber
attorneys.practice_type: Motor Vehicle Accidents Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Robert A. Huber, Esquire has been in practice assisting injury and accident victims for over 17 years, founding Huber & Palsir, LLC in June of 2007. He is a former partner of Etkin & Huber, LLP and Yankowitz, Etkin and Huber, LLP. Robert is an experienced litigator, having tried bench and jury trials involving motor vehicle accidents, slip/trip and fall accidents, as well as medical malpractice cases. Over the past 10 years, he has successfully handled multiple seven figure personal injury and many significant work place injury cases. Complex matters such as delayed diagnosis of cancer, failure to diagnosis and treat a stroke victim in a timely manner, and construction accidents involving negligent crane operation, welder's flash injuries and negligent hiring/supervising of employees cases are all within his expertise.

Robert is a graduate of the University of Nebraska with a major in Finance and Villanova University School of Law. He is a member of the American Bar Association, the Philadelphia Trial Lawyers Association, the Workers Compensation Section of the Pennsylvania Bar Association and the American Association of Justice. In addition to his professional training, Robert is also an active member of his parish community and a busy father to three children.

attorneys.name: Christine M. Hunt
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Easton, PA
attorneys.bio:
Christine Hunt is an attorney licensed to practice law in Pennsylvania and Illinois. She earned her Juris Doctor from The John Marshall Law School (now UIC John Marshall) in 2012, where she also received a Certificate in Trial Advocacy. She completed her undergraduate studies at The Pennsylvania State University, earning a Bachelor of Science in Crime, Law, and Justice with a minor in Psychology.

Christine has been recognized by Super Lawyers as a Rising Star each year from 2021 through 2026, an honor awarded to a select group of attorneys demonstrating professional achievement and peer recognition.

Christine joined Goudsouzian and Associates in 2025. Prior to joining the firm, she worked at Bernstein, Litowitz, Berger & Grossman LLP, where she served as a Staff Attorney on a large-scale securities fraud class action matter, contributing to complex litigation involving extensive discovery and significant financial claims.

Earlier in her career, Christine founded Christine M. Hunt, P.C. in Chicago in 2013. She primarily practiced family law, estate planning, and business law. Her family law practice involved litigating contested domestic relations matters in Chicagoland courtrooms. Her business law practice focused on business formation, contract drafting and review, and commercial lease negotiations. She also provided client-centered estate planning services tailored to individuals and families.

Christine served as Adjunct Professor and later as Acting Director of The John Marshall Law School’s Family and Domestic Violence Legal Clinic until its closure in May 2020. In this role, she supervised law students, managed active client files, and provided legal services to survivors of domestic violence.

When she is not practicing law, Christine spends most of her free time with her family, including her two young children.

Her family law practice involved litigating contested domestic relations matters in Chicagoland courtrooms. Her business law practice focused on business formation, contract drafting and review, and commercial lease negotiations. She also provided client-centered estate planning services tailored to individuals and families.

Christine served as Adjunct Professor and later as Acting Director of The John Marshall Law School’s Family and Domestic Violence Legal Clinic until its closure in May 2020. In this role, she supervised law students, managed active client files, and provided legal services to survivors of domestic violence.

When she is not practicing law, Christine spends most of her free time with her family, including her two young children.

attorneys.name: Alexander Hyder
attorneys.practice_type: Brain Injuries Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Alex Hyder is a trial attorney with Morgan & Morgan's Philadelphia office. He has a history of fighting hard for his clients, having obtained millions of dollars in recovery by way of settlement and jury verdict. Mr. Hyder has tried a variety of personal injury cases in both state and federal courts throughout Pennsylvania and New Jersey. His specialties include trucking and motor vehicle accidents, wrongful death/survival cases, slip trip and fall cases, brain injury cases, construction accidents, elevator accidents, negligent security, and dram shop/liquor liability cases.

In 2020, Mr. Hyder was recognized by the National Trial Lawyers Association (NTLA) as one of the Top-40-Under-40 civil trial attorneys in the country. He is also an active member in the Philadelphia Trial Lawyers Association and the Pennsylvania Association for Justice.

In addition to being licensed to practice in Pennsylvania and New Jersey state courts, Mr. Hyder is licensed in the United States District Courts for the Eastern and Middle Districts of Pennsylvania as well as the United States District Court for the District of New Jersey. He obtained his bachelor's degree from Penn State University (University Park) and his law degree from the Duquesne University School of Law.

Mr. Hyder is also an active member of the local community. He assists Philadelphia schools in their mock trial programs, teaching students the ins and outs of jury trials. He also assists low-income families in eviction proceedings through Philadelphia V.I.P. and is an advocate for individuals and families with intellectual and developmental disabilities.

In his personal time, Mr. Hyder is an avid 4-for-4 Philadelphia sports fan. When he's not prepping for trial, he likes to enjoy weekends at the shore with his Goldendoodle.

attorneys.name: Michael A. Hynum
attorneys.practice_type: Healthcare Law Lawyers in Harrisburg, PA
attorneys.bio:
Michael A. Hynum is a lawyer licensed to practice law in all courts of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, as well as US Federal Courts in the Middle and Eastern Districts of Pennsylvania. He is a resident of Dauphin county and is a member of the Lancaster County and Dauphin County Pennsylvania Bar Associations.

Born in Lebanon County, Attorney Hynum attended Annville-Cleona High School. He went on to attend Penn State University and obtained his Law Degree from the Widener University School of Law in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania. Mike also serves on the health law committee of the PA Bar Association.

Attorney Hynum spent approximately eleven years working in the long-term health care industry, acting as Chief Executive Officer of a company providing care and services to elderly residents of Central Pennsylvania. He is a licensed Nursing Home Administrator, has served as administrator of a personal care home, skilled nursing facility and has experience in Adult Day Care Administration LIFE CARE as well.

Mike Hynum began his legal career with a Harrisburg-based firm specializing in the representation of long-term care and skilled nursing facilities and in June 2004 founded his own Firm, Law Offices of Michael A. Hynum. In September 2006, upon hiring an additional attorney, the Firm name was changed to Hynum Law. Mike has considerable experience in both running and representing small businesses. As a lawyer in Harrisburg, PA, Hynum currently focuses his practice on the representation of health care providers, as well as debt collection, administrative and governmental law, labor law, general business law, family law, real estate and litigation.
