attorneys.name: Sean G. Livesey
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Law Lawyers in Norristown, PA
attorneys.bio:
Primarily focusing his practice on real estate, civil, and commercial litigation, Sean G. Livesey is a real estate attorney at High Swartz's Montgomery County law office. His additional areas of experience include zoning and land development, municipal code enforcement, real estate sales, and leasing, business franchising, and landlord/tenant litigation on behalf of landlords.

Mr. Livesey is a member of the firm's municipal law group where he has acted as conflict solicitor to multiple Montgomery County and Bucks County townships. He has also represented the Philadelphia International Airport before the Philadelphia Zoning Board of adjustment. He argued to obtain variances required to relocate a road, paving the way for a new cargo city development adjacent to the airport.

Previously, Sean was a partner at his family's practice in Conshohocken, PA, where he advised Philadelphia area startup companies regarding property acquisitions, business structure, and real estate tax liability. Sean also consulted with Montgomery County businesses to analyze zoning and land development proposals.

Prior to his private practice work, he was an associate at a large Philadelphia law firm’s commercial group where his practice included business litigation, real estate, zoning and land use. He represented real estate developers in Philadelphia, Montgomery County, Bucks County, and Delaware County. Sean also represented landlords in complex, large-scale landlord/tenant disputes.

As a real estate attorney, Sean has:

Represented a real estate developer seeking zoning relief for the redevelopment of a shopping plaza in South Philadelphia against consolidated local opposition

Defended property owners against claims by the City of Philadelphia for failure to comply with local regulations, including unauthorized use, unsafe conditions, air management requirements, etc.

Led community group meetings throughout the Philadelphia area in presenting proposed real estate development projects on behalf of developers

Successfully navigated community concerns over major mixed-use developments in North Philadelphia to secure zoning approval

Guided real estate developers through zoning approval processes, including hard-fought variances

Represented neighborhood objectors in opposing the construction of a super-convenience store in Conshohocken, PA

Represented a business owner in opposing City approval of an adult cabaret in Philadelphia

Defended an apartment owner against human rights violation claims

Defended multiple high rise apartment owners against tenants' habitability claims

As an associate at a large law firm in Virginia in 2018, Sean represented the claims administrator for the NFL Concussion Settlement in negotiating agreements with health systems to incorporate professionals into a diagnosing physicians network. Within the scope of the agreements, former players could be diagnosed with such neurodegenerative diseases as CTE, dementia, ALS, and Parkinson's.

Sean earned his J.D. at the University of Richmond's T.C. Williams School of Law while also obtaining his MBA at Richmond's Robins School of Business. After graduating, he served as a Judicial Intern for the Honorable Thomas N. O'Neill. Jr., United States District Judge for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania.

Sean grew up in Montgomery County, PA and enjoys cheering on Philly sports teams with his German shepherd, Zoe, a rescue from Memphis, TN.

Walter F. Lober received his Doctor of Jurisprudence from Widener University School of Law. While at Widener, he received a Certificate of Achievement in Workers’ Compensation. attorneys.name: Sean Logue
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Carnegie, PA
attorneys.bio:
Sean Logue is a diligent attorney who excels at representing people who have been charged with criminal and traffic offenses in Pennsylvania. He constantly strives to defend his clients in the state and the federal court as well as before other administrative agencies.

He has been given the bar admission in Pennsylvania (since 2008), West Virginia (since 2009), and has the license to practice in the U.S. District Court of Pennsylvania (since 2009), the U.S. District Court Western District of Pennsylvania, the U.S. District Court Northern District of West Virginia, and the U.S. District Court Southern District of West Virginia.

He received his undergraduate degree from Washington and Jefferson College in 2004 with honors in Political Science. Sean went on to earn his law degree at West Virginia University where he was the Student Bar Association Treasurer. His name was mentioned under the top 40 trial lawyers of 2012-2014. He is also a Pennsylvania Super Lawyers, Rising Star since 2014.

Sean achieved his dream of starting his own practice in 2008. He has represented many people in various kinds of criminal cases, such as traffic offenses, sexual assault, homicides, DUI and drug crimes, and other white collar crimes.

He has successfully represented defendants all across western Pennsylvania and the tri-state area. He represents several nation trucking companies and drivers associations for all of their complex traffic ticket needs. The Governor has appointed him to be a member of the council of trustees of California University of Pennsylvania. He is associated with the National College for DUI Defense since 2009.

He is an active member of the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers since 2008. He is also an eminent member of several other associations such as the Pennsylvania Bar Association, West Virginia Bar Association, Allegheny County Bar Association, and Washington County Bar Association. He was also been a proficient clerk at the Pennsylvania Office of Attorney General from 2007 to 2008, where he was involved in preparing organized crime and sex cases for trial. He has been a former member of the Federal Criminal Justice Act panel in the Northern District of West Virginia, where he handled complex federal drug cases as well as prisoner litigation.

He is a proficient legal advocate who is highly professional and immensely knowledgeable. Consistently updated on the recent changes in DUI law, he has also won many DUI trials. He has in-depth knowledge about every aspect of criminal defense and has handled several cases in many district courts too. He is also known to have made professional relationships with judges, prosecutors and magistrates. He believes that trusting your attorney is extremely critical for a case. Therefore, he values honest and frank communication with all his clients. He immediately discusses any information he gathers on the case with his client. He makes sure you are aware of every minute detail regarding the case at every stage of the legal proceedings.

When you are looking for an esteemed lawyer in Pennsylvania, it can be difficult to find the best one. Sean Logue is strongly committed to meeting the growing needs of his clients and provides them with the best possible defense.

attorneys.name: Christine P. Lora
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in West Chester, PA
attorneys.bio:
Christine P. Lora is an experienced litigation attorney who specializes in Criminal Law Matters.

Prior to joining the Ciccarelli Law Firm, Christine was an Assistant Defender with the Defender Association of Philadelphia where she successfully represented clients at every phase and level of the criminal system. During her 8.5-year tenure, Christine handled hundreds of jury and bench trials as well as preliminary and suppression hearings for a wide range of cases from possessory offenses to assaults. Though most of her time was spent in the Major Trial Unit, she also gained significant experience handling juvenile delinquency matters and specializes in cases with possible immigration consequences. Christine's extensive jury and bench trial experience includes a 90% acquittal rate with past victories including not guilty verdicts for numerous third strike cases including attempted murder, burglary, and armed robbery.

Christine is a fierce advocate who has dedicated her life and career to providing quality representation to the criminally accused. She has appeared in court on thousands of occasions, has handled 10,000+ hearings, and consistently succeeds in obtaining the best outcomes with the least amount of exposure for her clients.

Christine graduated Magna Cum Laude from DeSales University with degrees in History and Spanish. After college, she attended and graduated from Temple University Beasley School of Law where she focused on criminal defense and immigration work in both her studies and internships. She is a Gideon Award Recipient.

Christine is a Montgomery County native where she currently resides with her husband and two young sons. She enjoys latin dancing, good food, and the company of friends. She is fluent in Spanish.

attorneys.name: Amanda Lorentson
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Amanda Jonas Lorentson focuses her practice on sexual assault, child abuse, medical malpractice, catastrophic accidents and other personal injury cases.

In her most recent case, in December 2021, Lorentson was lead counsel in litigation that resulted in a seven-figure settlement with a hotel and its security firm for the victim of a sexual assault that occurred on the hotel premises.

Having begun her career as an elementary school teacher (as did Tom Kline), Lorentson switched to the law and attended the University of Pennsylvania Law School, where she was a top student and a prize-winning debater.

She hit the ground running at Kline & Specter, having worked for a year as a law clerk at the firm before passing the bar and being sworn in as an attorney. Lorentson focuses on cases involving child and sexual abuse. In addition to her legal duties at the firm, she also serves as its Coordinator of Diversity, Equity & Inclusion.

Lorentson gained prior legal experience during law school as a trial intern with the Defenders Association of Philadelphia and as a summer associate with the large Philadelphia firm of Blank Rome LLP.

Before that, she worked as a 5th grade teacher in Washington, D.C. and taught 8th grade English at the Young Scholars Charter School in Philadelphia.

Lorentson earned a master's degree in education from George Mason University and her bachelor's degree in English from the University of Buffalo, where she graduated summa cum laude and was the recipient of the Pacemaker Award for Diversity Article of the Year given by the American Society of News Editors and Associated Collegiate Press.

At Penn Law, Lorentson was awarded the Teach for America Scholarship and the Dean's Scholars Scholarship. In her first year she was a Philadelphia Diversity Law Group fellow. Later, Lorentson went on to chair the fundraising effort for the Equal Justice Foundation and was a trial team competitor, winning Best Direct Examination in the 2018 National Trial Advocacy Competition. She is currently assistant coach of the trial team, which participates in various national trial competitions.

Lorentson is a member of the University of Pennsylvania Carey School of Law Inn of Court and Teach for America Alumni 2011 in Washington, D.C.

Lorentson also serves on the board of directors of the Liberation Foundation, a nonprofit organization which advocates for wrongfully convicted persons seeking legal representation.

attorneys.name: Michael G. Louis
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in West Chester, PA
attorneys.bio:
Michael's practice supports the needs of businesses and homeowners in a changing economic environment. He has extensive experience in mortgage foreclosures, collections and loan workouts, general counsel work and real estate litigation.

Recent Representations

Provided local counsel for a bank in litigation with a borrower in which the bank sued the borrower for $60 million and the borrower filed a separate action against the bank, alleging damages in excess of $60 million.

Represented landlord whose tenant defaulted on a commercial lease. Recovered possession of the leased property for landlord and all of the unpaid back rent plus the landlord's attorneys' fees.

Defended client sued as a guarantor of a business loan by filing a petition to strike and/or open the judgment.

Debt workout/restructuring for client in restaurant business that defaulted on obligations to lender due to the slumping economy. Assisted the client in re-working certain loans and obligations and delaying others without losing business.

Obtained retroactive relief from automatic stay on client's behalf after defaulting borrower filed bankruptcy on eve of execution on debtor's real estate.

Represented client in investigation and litigation involving embezzlement and fraud by company employees. Successfully pursued former employees and obtained partial recovery of stolen funds.

Represented client sued by bankruptcy trustee for payments made to it on the eve of debtor's bankruptcy. Resolved the matter with no payment to the bankruptcy trustee.

attorneys.name: Michael A. Luongo
attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation Lawyers in Doylestown, PA
attorneys.bio:
Michael A. Luongo, Esq. is a Bucks County attorney in the firm's business litigation, municipal, and criminal defense practices. Michael joined High Swartz after practicing in the litigation department at a prominent law firm in Blue Bell, PA.

Michael defends depositions, drafts and argues various motions, and serves as first and second chair in complex trials. He represents his clients in a variety of commercial and business litigation matters, including:

Breach of Contract

Business Divorces

Construction Litigation

Execution & Enforcement of Judgments

Employment Litigation

Estates and Trusts Litigation

Will contest litigation

Preliminary and Permanent Injunctions

Breach of Warranties & Representations

Temporarily Restraining Orders

Uniform Trade Secrets Act

Landlord/Tenant Eviction and Ejectment

Land Use & Zoning Disputes

Unfair Trade Practices & Consumer Protection Law

Prior to his time there as a business litigator and criminal defense attorney, Michael served as an Assistant District Attorney in the Philadelphia District Attorney’s Office. Mr. Luongo litigated multiple high-profile criminal cases, including hundreds of bench trials and jury trials. He was the designated vertical prosecutor handling all Press Cases, Non-Fatal Shootings and Gunpoint Robberies. He also conducted hearings for motions to suppress, bail, quash, discovery, reconsider, and consolidate prior bad acts. It was Michael's trial and prosecution acumen that assisted him in getting a promotion to Northeast Philadelphia's top prosecutor position.

Michael displays strong business knowledge and skill in his work as a small and medium-sized business litigator in the Philadelphia region. He also assists the firm's municipal group, consisting of attorneys who counsel multiple first and second class townships in the region as solicitors. Michael acts as conflict solicitor for High Swartz to multiple Bucks County Zoning Hearing Boards and Montgomery County Municipalities. Conversely, he represents individuals, property owners, and business owners before zoning hearing boards in the region.

While at law school at Rutgers of Camden, Michael served Philadelphia County's Court of Common Pleas judge, the Honorable Rose Mare Defino-Nastasi as a summer law clerk. He earned a Master's of Business Administration from LaSalle University and a Bachelor's of Science from Lehigh University. Michael also studied International Business during his time at Villanova University's Post Grad Program and worked at a marketing firm during his law school days.

Michael currently lives in Doylestown, PA and is active in the Montgomery Bar and Pennsylvania Bar Associations. He is currently the Vice President of the Montgomery American Inn of Court. The American Inns of Court are associations where lawyers, judges and other legal professionals can come together to discuss legal issues.

Brendan focuses his practice on protecting the rights of people and small businesses injured by the carelessness of others. This follows his 2011 induction into the Academy of Trial Lawyers of Allegheny County- an invitation only organization limited to 250 of the most exceptional civil trial lawyers in Allegheny County – of which Brendan was one of the youngest members ever admitted. Brendan is “privileged to serve members of our community injured through no fault of their own due to the carelessness of others.” Brendan’s singular goal and passion as a lawyer is to improve the safety of our community through zealous advocacy of his clients civil rights. When avoidable tragedy arises, the attorneys of Meyers Evans Lupetin & Unatin, of whom Brendan is a proud partner, are there to enforce the rules, protect the injured and bring about just outcomes.

attorneys.name: Alvin J. Luschas Esquire
attorneys.firm_name: Law Offices Of Luschas & Naparsteck, LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Elder Law Lawyers in Bloomsburg, PA
attorneys.bio:
Alvin J. Luschas, Esq., of Mahanoy City and Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania, joined the law offices of Derr & Pursel in 1978. He graduated (cum laude) from the University of Scranton in 1972 and received his Juris Doctor degree from St. Louis University School of Law in 1975. That year he was admitted to practice law in Pennsylvania and became a member of the Columbia-Montour Bar Association. Shortly thereafter he was also admitted to practice law before the United States Middle District Court (Pennsylvania) as well as the United States Claims Court. Attorney Luschas was commissioned as an officer in the United States Army in 1972 and was a member of the US Army Reserve from 1972-1982. He attained the rank of Captain and served as a company commander with specialized training in chemical, nuclear, and biological warfare.

Attorney Luschas served as the solicitor of Columbia County from 1979-1991. In 1989 he received statewide recognition as the Commonwealth’s Outstanding County Solicitor by the Pennsylvania State Association of County commissioners. Attorney Luschas became general counsel for the Columbia Montour Area Agency on Aging serving in that capacity from 1991 to the present. He is currently general counsel for First Columbia Bank & Trust Co., the Hemlock Municipal Sewer Cooperative, the Mifflin Township Board of Township Supervisors, the Central Columbia School District, the Columbia-Montour Vo-Tech School, and the Bloomsburg Area Municipal Authority.

He currently serves on the Board of Directors of First Columbia Bank & Trust Co. and is a member of the Trust and Technology Committees of that Board. He is the past President of the Board of Directors of the Bloomsburg Area YMCA and held leadership roles in the fund-raising for and construction of the Bloomsburg Area YMCA in 1995. He has served as President of the pastoral council of St. Columba Church and has served as a member of the St. Columba Church school board. He also currently serves on the Board of Directors of Downtown Bloomsburg, Inc., and the Board of Directors of the Columbia Montour Visitors Bureau. Attorney Luschas is a Real Estate Title Insurance Agent and is certified to practice before the United States Veterans’ Administration.

He is a current member of Elder Counsel, the Pennsylvania Elder Law Association, National Association of Elder Law Attorneys, Pennsylvania Bar Association, the Pennsylvania Association for Justice, Pennsylvania Municipal Authorities Association, and the Pennsylvania Association of Township Supervisors. His areas of concentration are Elder Law, Trusts & Estates, Business Law, Municipal Law, and Real Estate Transactions. He resides with his wife of forty-four years, Elaine Luschas, in the Berwick, Pennsylvania Area.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Received statewide recognition as the Commonwealth’s Outstanding County Solicitor by the Pennsylvania State Association of County commissioners, 1989

attorneys.name: Barbara N. Lyons Esquire
attorneys.firm_name: Bucks County Mediation and Arbitration Center
attorneys.practice_type: ADR: Mediation Arbitration Case Evaluation Lawyers in Doylestown, PA
attorneys.bio:
Barbara N. Lyons, Esquire, is a certified, skilled and experienced lawyer specializing in neutral arbitration, mediation and case evaluation. She founded the Bucks County Mediation and Arbitration Center (BCMAC) to provide parties to disputes with alternatives to traditional litigation.

Through BCMAC, Ms. Lyons provides full-service Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) solutions for lawyers and their clients. Ms. Lyons addresses issues involving, but not limited to, contract and real estate disputes, equity matters, underinsured and uninsured motorist cases, personal injury, municipal, medical malpractice and employer/employee disputes, business mergers and dissolutions.

An attorney since 1981, Ms. Lyons is a former trial attorney representing both plaintiffs and defendants. This training provides her with a unique prospective on the resolution of legal matters – with a penchant for cutting through to the heart of the dispute. Ms. Lyons has been a dedicated neutral attorney since 1994 when she focused her practice in all methods of resolving disputes outside of the court system. Since establishing BCMAC, Ms. Lyons has resolved thousands of civil actions by mediation and arbitration.

Ms. Lyons is admitted to practice law in the Courts for the County of Bucks, Pennsylvania Supreme Court, and the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania. She is a court appointed arbitrator, mediator and judge pro tem in over 3,000 cases for the Bucks County Mortgage Foreclosure Program, a program she helped create for the court system in 2009. Just before founding BCMAC in 1994, Ms. Lyons taught peer mediation to middle school children in Bucks County and decided to bring her unique talents to the legal community.

Ms. Lyons is a member of the Senate Advisory Commission on Alternative Dispute Resolution and serves on the ABA Advanced Mediation Institute faculty. She works to create systems of alternative dispute resolution throughout the Commonwealth. In March 2013, Ms. Lyons was appointed to the Joint State Government Commission’s Advisory Committee on Violence Prevention. This advisory committee assisted the Commission in researching and drafting violence prevention recommendations to the State General Assembly.

An active member of the legal community, Ms. Lyons has served multiple terms as a Director for the Bucks County Bar Association. She was the founder and editor of the Bucks County Bar Association newsletter, "The Writs," for the Bar Association, a member of the Women's Law Division, and has served as a Trustee to the Charitable Foundation for the Bucks County Bar Association and as a Fellow to the American Bar Association. Ms. Lyons also serves the greater community as a member of the Board of Supervisors for Doylestown Township, a position she has been elected to four times since 2002 and served as Chairman of the Board for over 15 years. Prior to her position on the Board of Supervisors, she served as Chairman of Doylestown Township’s Park and Recreation Board.

Ms. Lyons chairs the Annual Doylestown Township Golf Outing and is the past chair of the Township’s annual Oktoberfest. She has volunteered her time and talents to numerous organizations and has provided pro bono legal representation to abused women and their children for over three decades for which she was recognized by the Pennsylvania Bar Association Pro Bono Award. She received the Central Bucks Chamber of Commerce VIA Women in Business Leadership Award in 2013, in recognition of her outstanding leadership in the Central Bucks community.

From 1992 to 1995, Ms. Lyons served as the Director of A Woman’s Place, a shelter for victims of domestic violence and their children and as President of the Board of CB Cares Educational Foundation, a non-profit organization that works as a coalition with community leaders, agencies, businesses, schools and families for the purpose of helping to grow a healthier youth. Ms. Lyons also demonstrates her commitment to the community as a counsellor to women and families in transition.

Ms. Lyons earned her B.A. summa cum laude from the University of Pittsburgh and her J.D. in 1981 from Temple University School of Law. She is a frequent, dynamic lecturer at high schools and universities.

Ms. Lyons and her husband, Rick Lyons, are the proud parents of three adult children, all of whom are alumni of Villanova University, and four grandchildren. In her spare time, Ms. Lyons enjoys time with family, singing in secular and non-secular choirs and the practicing the game of golf.

She is a court appointed arbitrator, mediator and judge pro tem in over 3,000 cases for the Bucks County Mortgage Foreclosure Program, a program she helped create for the court system in 2009. Just before founding BCMAC in 1994, Ms. Lyons taught peer mediation to middle school children in Bucks County and decided to bring her unique talents to the legal community.

Ms. Lyons is a member of the Senate Advisory Commission on Alternative Dispute Resolution and serves on the ABA Advanced Mediation Institute faculty. She works to create systems of alternative dispute resolution throughout the Commonwealth. In March 2013, Ms. Lyons was appointed to the Joint State Government Commission’s Advisory Committee on Violence Prevention. This advisory committee assisted the Commission in researching and drafting violence prevention recommendations to the State General Assembly.

An active member of the legal community, Ms. Lyons has served multiple terms as a Director for the Bucks County Bar Association. She was the founder and editor of the Bucks County Bar Association newsletter, "The Writs," for the Bar Association, a member of the Women's Law Division, and has served as a Trustee to the Charitable Foundation for the Bucks County Bar Association and as a Fellow to the American Bar Association. Ms. Lyons also serves the greater community as a member of the Board of Supervisors for Doylestown Township, a position she has been elected to four times since 2002 and served as Chairman of the Board for over 15 years. Prior to her position on the Board of Supervisors, she served as Chairman of Doylestown Township’s Park and Recreation Board.

Ms. Lyons chairs the Annual Doylestown Township Golf Outing and is the past chair of the Township’s annual Oktoberfest. She has volunteered her time and talents to numerous organizations and has provided pro bono legal representation to abused women and their children for over three decades for which she was recognized by the Pennsylvania Bar Association Pro Bono Award. She received the Central Bucks Chamber of Commerce VIA Women in Business Leadership Award in 2013, in recognition of her outstanding leadership in the Central Bucks community.

From 1992 to 1995, Ms. Lyons served as the Director of A Woman’s Place, a shelter for victims of domestic violence and their children and as President of the Board of CB Cares Educational Foundation, a non-profit organization that works as a coalition with community leaders, agencies, businesses, schools and families for the purpose of helping to grow a healthier youth. Ms. Lyons also demonstrates her commitment to the community as a counsellor to women and families in transition.

Ms. Lyons earned her B.A. summa cum laude from the University of Pittsburgh and her J.D. in 1981 from Temple University School of Law. She is a frequent, dynamic lecturer at high schools and universities.

Ms. Lyons and her husband, Rick Lyons, are the proud parents of three adult children, all of whom are alumni of Villanova University, and four grandchildren. In her spare time, Ms. Lyons enjoys time with family, singing in secular and non-secular choirs and the practicing the game of golf.

attorneys.name: Joseph E. Maenner
attorneys.practice_type: Intellectual Property Lawyers in Downingtown, PA
attorneys.bio:
Joseph Maenner founded Maenner & Associates, LLC in 2011 after practicing in intellectual property boutique firms and general practice firms, as well as serving as in-house counsel for a small high-technology startup company. He has taken the "best practices" from all of those experiences and has molded them together to produce his firm. In addition, he has eliminated the "billable hour” that all clients loathe, and has replaced it with a fixed fee that is quoted to and agreed upon by the client prior to each phase of his work.

Mr. Maenner graduated from the Dickinson School of Law (now part of the Pennsylvania State University) in 1996 and began actively practicing intellectual property law in 1998. His client base has ranged from Fortune 500 companies, to large research universities, to small, privately held companies, to independent inventors.

Prior to attending law school, Mr. Maenner earned a Bachelor of Science degree in Mechanical Engineering from Drexel University in 1986. He had a seven-year career as an engineer, working for the U.S. Department of Defense at the Naval Surface Warfare Center, located in Philadelphia, PA. His practical engineering experience has been an invaluable tool in assisting his clients through the years in refining their inventions.

Some examples of the technologies in which Mr. Maenner has drafted patent applications are pump action water guns, remote-controlled vehicles, automotive fuel injectors, polymer optical devices, hemodialysis catheters and other implantable medical devices, rechargeable lithium-ion battery chemistry, computer software, piezoelectric oscillators, respiratory devices, and neuropathy diagnostic tools.

Additionally, Mr. Maenner has significant experience in counseling clients in the selection and use of trademarks and in obtaining federal trademark registrations. While in law school, he served as an intern in the U.S. Trademark Office. He has also obtained copyright registrations for artistic designs and three-dimensional articles. Mr. Maenner frequently provides seminars on intellectual property to local university and high school students and has conducted CLE courses on intellectual property for local bar associations.

Mr. Maenner is also an adjunct professor at Lehigh University, teaching a class in Intellectual Property Law for a graduate program in Technical Entrepreneurship. Mr. Maenner is a member of the bar of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania as well as the Middle District of Pennsylvania, and is admitted to practice before the United States Patent and Trademark Office.

attorneys.name: Barry G. Magen M.D.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Barry G. Magen, M.D., J.D., has been involved extensively in medicine and law, first as a physician and as an attorney.

Dr. Magen, who worked as a physician at Thomas Jefferson University Hospital and the former Mt. Sinai Hospital in South Philadelphia, joined Kline & Specter in 2010 after six years with law firms that worked in medical malpractice defense. The firms included Goldfein & Joseph, P.C., in Philadelphia and, more recently, Galli and Reilly, in Bala Cynwyd.

Dr. Magen has been selected for inclusion in Pennsylvania Super Lawyers -- Rising Stars, a publication that uses statewide voting and a special review committee to choose the top 2.5 percent of attorneys who are 40 or younger.

He previously worked at a Philadelphia firm, Hochberg Napoli Diamond, in which he represented patients who had suffered injuries due to medical malpractice. Dr. Magen worked at the Hochberg firm for five years, from 1999 to 2004. He previously worked at Haymond & Lundy, also a Philadelphia personal injury law firm, while in law school.

He worked as a hospitalist at Mt. Sinai in 1996-97, where he handled all types of patient care, including duties in emergency room and inpatient care. He did his residency in anesthesia at Thomas Jefferson University and an internship before that at Reading Hospital and Medical Center.

Dr. Magen attended Temple University School of Law, where he was a member of the International Comparative Law Review. He also earned his medical degree from Temple and his undergraduate degree from Pennsylvania State University, where he majored in vertebrate physiology.

Attorney Mark Malak graduated from Rowan University with honors and earned his bachelor's degree in political science in 2010. Upon graduation, he went on to attend Hofstra University School of Law, where he earned his Juris Doctor in 2013.

During law school, Attorney Malak was awarded a legal fellowship by Legal Services, where he represented and fought for clients who could not afford to hire their own private attorneys. At this position, he was honored and recognized for his service to the public. In addition, Mr. Malak belonged to his law school's Criminal Justice Clinic, where he defended individuals charged with misdemeanors in county court.

Attorney Malak joined Berger and Green, P.C. in 2019, where he proudly represents and fights for disabled individuals. Prior to joining Berger and Green, Mr. Malak litigated Social Security Disability cases in over 30 states. Mr. Malak takes great pride in representing his clients and treats everyone with the utmost respect and professionalism. He is hard-working and determined to make things right for his clients.

Attorney Malak serves on the membership committee of the National Organization of Social Security Claimants Representatives (NOSSCR). With over 4,000 members, NOSSCR is the largest group of attorneys advocating for the rights of disabled individuals. He is also a member of the Allegheny County Bar Association, the Committee on Law and Disability, the Committee for Diversity and Inclusion, as well as the Social Security Practitioners Committee. He is licensed to practice law in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, the State of New York, the State of New Jersey, and in all Social Security Courts throughout the United States.

attorneys.practice_type: Orphans' Court Practice Lawyers in Wilkes Barre, PA
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Malak is a partner in the law firm of Chariton Malak who possesses broad experience in litigation and corporate matters. Mr. Malak has also briefed and argued numerous appeals in both Federal and State Courts including the Pennsylvania Supreme Court, Pennsylvania Superior Court, Pennsylvania Commonwealth Court, Middle District of Pennsylvania and the Third Circuit Court of Appeals. Acting as lead counsel, Mr. Malak has had numerous decisions reported, including several precedential Pennsylvania oil and gas law decisions. Mr. Malak represents individuals, domestic corporations, partnerships, limited liability companies, municipalities, municipal authorities, solar companies, oil and gas companies, oil and gas drilling and production companies, natural gas pipeline/transmission companies, alternative energy companies, estates, trusts, financial and trust institutions and national life insurance companies.

Mr. Malak is admitted to practice law before all State Courts in both Pennsylvania and New Jersey including the Superior Court of Pennsylvania and the Supreme Court of Pennsylvania. He also maintains an active Federal litigation practice before the United States District Court for the Middle District of Pennsylvania, the United States District Court for the District of New Jersey, the United States Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit and the Supreme Court of the United States of America.

Mr. Malak is past Chairperson of the Pennsylvania Bar Association's Shale Energy Law Committee, serves on the Luzerne County Bench Bar Committee, the Luzerne County Estate Litigation and Orphans Court Rules Committee, the Pennsylvania Bar Association Real Property and Trust Section, the Pennsylvania State University, Dickinson School of Law, Board of Governors (at large), was named to the Pennsylvania Disciplinary Board as a Hearing Officer and serves as a Solicitor to Townships, Boroughs and Municipal Authorities throughout Pennsylvania.

Among his noteworthy achievements, Mr. Malak was selected as a Pennsylvania Super Lawyers Rising Star for numerous years and was named one of 30 lawyers in Pennsylvania selected to Lawyers on the Fast Track by The Philadelphia Legal Intelligencer. He is also a past recipient of both the Pennsylvania Northeast Business Journal's and the Wilkes-Barre Times Leaders' Top 20 Under 40.

attorneys.name: Deborah S. Maliver
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
Get to Know Deborah Maliver Dr. Deborah Maliver is a third generation doctor. Dr. Maliver's parents and grandparents were physicians and, as a child growing up, she recalls discussing medicine often around the dinner table. With a strong desire to keep up the family tradition, she graduated from the University of North Carolina Greensboro with a BS in biology and attended Albert Einstein College of Medicine.

Dr. Maliver has extensive experience in caring for adult patients with illnesses like diabetes, high blood pressure, heart disease and cancer. One of her career goals as a physician was to screen for preventable diseases such as breast and colon cancer. She also started a small solo practice in Indiana, PA, where she cared for patients in her office as well as the hospital and Intensive Care Unit. It is this real-life experience that caused Dr. Maliver to notice the errors being made in patient care. She realized that the medical field had no way of policing itself.

It was at this point in her life that she discovered there was a need for qualified medical malpractice attorneys. After completing her law degree from the University of Pittsburgh School of Law, she joined Christine Biancheria to form a small medical malpractice law firm in Pittsburgh . She believes a small law firm can provide the type of individual attention and care that clients deserve when they have become the victim of medical malpractice.

Because of her extensive medical expertise, Dr. Maliver understands the treatments and diseases people are talking about when they call her. She personally overseas every case and does not rely on a third-party explanation. Dr. Maliver was once a part of the healthcare system, and she knows exactly what questions to ask and where to look for answers.

As a physician, Dr. Maliver does not take suing a doctor lightly. However, she believes all doctors have a duty to do their very best for patients and their families. When a doctor makes a mistake or medical malpractice has occurred, it is her job to ensure her clients get a full financial recovery. Money cannot fix the injury or bring someone back, but it can compensate people for medical bills, lost work, pain and suffering, loss of head of household by children, and the loss of your quality of life.

"If you believe you have been the victim of medical malpractice, please call us today. Although we are very selective, I give the same amount of attention to every person that calls or emails me. If you cannot come to us, we will be happy to come to you." ---- Deborah Maliver, MD , Esq.

attorneys.name: Anne Marie Mancuso
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
Anne Marie Mancuso has dedicated her legal career to the vital missions abundant in criminal defense work. She has litigated a wide spectrum of crimes, from the least severe in nature to the most violent of felonies including criminal homicide.

Prior to joining Rothman, Haber & Mancuso, P.C., Anne Marie worked as a private criminal defense attorney practicing throughout western Pennsylvania. Ms. Mancuso began her trial work at the Allegheny County Office of Conflict Counsel advocating for the rights of indigent Pennsylvania residents and protecting the civil liberties of those criminally accused. Ms. Mancuso has successfully defended against thousands of criminal prosecutions, having tried countless non-jury and jury trials to verdict. In 2014, an Allegheny County jury found Ms. Mancuso’s client not guilty of 27 counts of aggravated assault and recklessly endangering another person after a city police chase ended in police gun fire. More recently, Anne Marie received full acquittals in three separate attempted homicide jury trials stemming from shootings in North Versailles, McKeesport and Tarentum. She has obtained not guilty verdicts in numerous violent crimes, sex crimes and gun related cases, as well as the dismissal of homicide charges.

Ms. Mancuso received her undergraduate degree from the University of Pittsburgh, and earned her Juris Doctorate from Ohio Northern University, Pettit College of Law where she received Certificates of Outstanding Achievement in Criminal Law and Civil Litigation.

attorneys.name: David S. Mandel
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Real Estate Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
David S. Mandel is the Firm's Managing Partner and also the Chairman of its Real Estate and Business Law Group. His real estate practice includes but is not limited to the following types of representations:

1) Representation of both landlords and tenants in the negotiation of shopping center leases;

2) Representation of clients in their sale, acquisition and financing of commercial and industrial real estate, including free standing buildings, pad sites and shopping centers;

3) Formation of condominiums for both residential and commercial use;

4) Formation of syndications for the acquisition and development of commercial real estate projects;

5) Representation of lenders and borrowers in loan transactions related to commercial real estate projects;

6) Preparation of real estate syndication documentation.

Mr. Mandel's business practice includes representation of clients in a variety of industries, including the entertainment industry (movie theaters, restaurants and bowling alleys), commercial printing, direct mail marketing, real estate brokerage and management, title insurance agencies, and retail (clothing stores, auto part stores, camera stores amongst others). He counsels clients on general corporate matters including types of business formation, preparation of partnership agreements, limited liability company operating agreements, limited partnership agreements, employment agreements, independent contractor agreements and vendor agreements. He has also been involved in mergers and acquisitions of a variety of sizes representing both the seller and buyer.

In addition, he has also been involved in commercial litigation matters including a recent matter which involved contracts for the sale of industrial real estate valued in the many tens of millions of dollars.

attorneys.name: Frank Mangiaracina
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Frank Mangiaracina focuses his practice on catastrophic personal injury. He is a staunch advocate and proven trial lawyer who helped compile more than $60 million in recoveries in the five years before coming to Kline & Specter.

Most recently, in a COVID-era trial during the summer of 2021, Mangiaracina won a $2.1 million verdict against Domino's Pizza for a client who suffered severe and permanent injuries to his leg when his motorcycle was struck by a delivery driver. As co-lead counsel at trial, Mangiaracina gave a closing argument that helped convince the jury that Domino's was responsible for the actions of a franchisee.

He was also co-counsel in litigation that achieved a $44 million pre-trial settlement in a product liability case for an oil rig worker who was left a quadriplegic after he was struck by a falling light fixture.

He was, simultaneously, staff editor for the Temple Law Review and a member of Temple's renowned National Trial Team, which placed in the semifinals of the National Institute of Trial Advocacy's "Tournament of Champions," an invitation-only competition.

At Temple, Mangiaracina won several awards and scholarships, including the Integrated Trial Advocacy Graduation Award, the Benjamin and Natalie Levin Memorial Scholarship, the Class of 1978 Scholarship and the Faculty Law Scholarship.

Mangiaracina earned his undergraduate degree from Lehigh University.

attorneys.name: Richard L. Manilla
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Mt. Lebanon, PA
attorneys.bio:
Richard Manilla joined Ruppert Law Firm LLC in 2023. His practice primary consists of family latter matters that include Divorce, Custody, Child Support, Protection from Abuse ("PFA") actions, Termination of Parental Rights, Adoptions, and Dependency actions. He is licensed to practice in all of Pennsylvania's state and federal courts. Richard is dedicated to simplifying the complexities of family law matters and providing straightforward representation to his clients.

In addition to family law matters, Richard also has a background in personal injury law (including motor-vehicle accidents, medical/professional malpractice, products liability, industrial accidents, and premise liability), workers compensation, business litigation, construction litigation, appellate work, DUI law, license suspensions, and criminal defense. These practices areas have allowed Richard to litigate in several courts throughout Western Pennsylvania, including Magisterial District Courts, Courts of Common Pleas, the Pennsylvania Superior Court, the Pennsylvania WCAB, the Pennsylvania Supreme Court, and the US District Court, Western District of Pennsylvania.

Richard is a graduate of Claude W. Pettit College of Law at Ohio Northern University, where he was an Associate Justice of the Jessup International Law Team and competed in the Jessup International Moot Court Competition as a team member and coach. Additionally, Richard clerked for the Honorable Gregory L. Frost of the U.S. District Court, Southern District of Ohio. He also worked for the Ohio Northern Legal Clinic that represented indigent clients in domestic relations matters and interned for the Prosecutor's Office of Hardin County, Ohio prosecuting child abuse, neglect, and dependency cases.

He completed his undergraduate studies at the University of Pittsburgh at Greensburg, where he graduated summa cum laude and was inducted into the Phi Eta Sigma National Honor Society, the Phi Kappa Phi National Honor Society, the Pi Sigma Alpha National Honor Society and the University of Pittsburgh Greensburg Ben Franklin Society.

Richard lives in Butler County with his wife, son, their pet bulldog. He is the Armstrong County Bar Present for 2023 and the Zone 10 Governor for the Pennsylvania Bar Association. He is an active member of the Rotary Club of Porterville-Prosect, the Prosect Area Preservation Society, and the St. Christopher Catholic Church. When he is free, Rick enjoys spending as much time as possible with his wife and son, reading fantasy and science fiction novels, and playing music.

attorneys.name: William P. Mansour
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law Lawyers in Allentown, PA
attorneys.bio:
As a lawyer, I pride myself on the relationships I build with my clients. I get to know them through some of the toughest times in their lives, whether they were unfairly fired from their jobs or seriously injured in a car accident. Most of the time, my clients have my email and personal cell phone number. I'm even friends with many of them on Facebook. I work hard to be not just their lawyer, but also their counselor, adviser, and friend.

Because of this client-centered approach, hundreds of people all across Pennsylvania have trusted me to handle their employment and personal injury legal matters.

Pennsylvania is my home. My roots are here. It's where I grew up, where I went to school, and where I am raising my own family. After graduating from Temple University School of Law in 2014, I entered private practice with a small, regional firm in Stroudsburg, Pennsylvania. While there, I represented individuals in various civil matters, including personal injury and employment cases. In 2015, I began working at another regional firm in Pittston, Pennsylvania, where I expanded my personal injury and employment law practice and also began defending municipalities and government agencies in federal civil rights litigation.

In 2018, I started working at a reputable Allentown, Pennsylvania law firm. It was there that I began to focus my practice solely on helping people who have been unfairly treated at work or seriously injured in an accident. This is where my passion for employment and personal injury law really came alive. For nearly 3 years, I dedicated myself to getting justice for hundreds of people who were wrongly injured or wrongly fired. On their behalf, I took the fight to multi-national corporations, big banks, and every insurance company under the sun.

Unlike many lawyers, I have the unique ability to relate to, and empathize with, my clients. I've worked in plenty of toxic work environments and I've helplessly watched my own family members struggle to recover from a serious car accident. It is these lived experiences that motivate me to work hard for my clients every single day. No one should have to put up with illegal behavior at work simply because they "need the job." Nor should someone be driven into bankruptcy because they were seriously injured in an accident that was another person's fault. I've made it my mission to make sure these things don't happen to good, honest, and hardworking people.

If you believe you've been illegally discriminated against or harassed at work, or if you've been seriously injured by someone else's carelessness, let's talk. I offer totally FREE, 1-hour consultations in-person, by video, or by phone - whatever's most convenient for you. Contact me today to see if I can help. I look forward to hearing from you.

attorneys.practice_type: Domestic Law Lawyers in Wexford, PA
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Sadie M. Marak joined the firm in 2020 to focus on domestic and family law, but also has a background as a general practitioner. She has experience handling a wide variety of matters in many of the surrounding counties. Clients value her logical thinking, perseverance and unwavering commitment. Sadie’s empathizing nature allows her to build a strong trusting relationship with clients, ultimately leading to a more comprehensive understanding of each situation.

Sadie attended Washington and Jefferson College wherein she obtained her bachelor’s degree in political science and a minor in sociology. While attending Washington and Jefferson College, Sadie also played Softball and was the captain of the softball team from 2013-2015.

Following her undergraduate education, Sadie attended Duquesne University School of Law wherein she obtained her Juris Doctorate Degree. During law school, Sadie served as a judicial intern for the Honorable Daniel D. Regan of the Allegheny County Court of Common Pleas, participated in the Duquesne Public Defender Clinic and earned a Pro Bono Certificate.

Prior to beginning her career with McMorrow Law, LLC, Sadie was employed as an Associate Attorney at Geary, Loperfito & Generelli, LLC located in Westmoreland County, Pennsylvania wherein she gained experience in family law, criminal law, estate planning, real estate, banking law and municipal law.

When not at the office, Sadie enjoys spending time with her family and traveling. Sadie is committed to developing a trusting relationship with her clients and her goal is always to provide the best representation while calming fears and putting her clients at ease.

attorneys.bio:
Julie M. Marburger earned her Doctor of Jurisprudence from John Marshall Law School. Prior to law school, she graduated from College of Charleston, earning a Bachelor of Arts degree in Historic Preservation and Community Planning & Art History. Ms. Marburger also received a Master of Science in Historic Preservation from the University of Georgia. She is licensed to practice in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania and the State of Georgia.

Ms. Marburger concentrates her practice in all areas of family law. She has years of experience representing clients in custody, divorce and support matters. Ms. Marburger is also skilled at drafting prenuptial and postnuptial agreements, cohabitation agreements, and separation agreements. She also serves clients in resolving issues without litigation through collaborative divorce and mediation.

In 2014, Ms. Marburger received the “Select Lawyer” award for her practice in Family Law based on her “reputation within the community and among colleagues and peers, quality of services provided, experience, educational background and continuing educational endeavors, and utilization of best-practice procedures and techniques.” She has been selected to the Rising Star list, which recognizes excellence in lawyers age 40 and younger, for the years 2016 to 2023. Ms. Marburger is the Vice-Chair of the Amity Township Planning Commission, a member of the Berks County Bar Association, Chair of the Law Day & Entertainment Committees, Co-Chair of the Family Law Section, and serves on the Board for the Endlich Law Club.

Prior to joining Berman Voss, Ms. Marburger was affiliated with a boutique law firm in Wyomissing, serving clients in all areas of family law.

attorneys.name: Carolyn M. Marchesani
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Administration & Probate Lawyers in Pottstown, PA
attorneys.bio:
Carolyn Marchesani has over fifteen years of professional experience providing individuals and families with counsel and strategies for estate planning, probate and estate administration. Ms. Marchesani has concentrated her practice in this area with the goal of ensuring that the client has a plan in place to provide for themselves and their family. This work includes helping to organize information to understand current circumstances, determine desired plans going forward and complete effective execution of this plan by helping clients gain an understanding of the related laws in this area and how these laws may impact them. Estate planning involves coordination of advisors in the area of insurance, tax and financial matters. Lifestyle, family dynamics, roles and responsibilities vary and regularly create a need to review your estate plan.

Ms. Marchesani attended Villanova University School of Law – Graduate Tax Program and completed the Estate Planning Certificate Program, while working as an Associate Attorney for a Chester County based firm. Ms. Marchesani attended Widener University School of Law, in Wilmington, Delaware, where she earned her Juris Doctorate (J.D.) while working full-time as a Paralegal in this same law firm. She was admitted to the bar in 1995. Her undergraduate studies were completed at Fairfield University, Fairfield, CT, where she earned a B.A. in Psychology.

Ms. Marchesani, originally from New Jersey, has been a Chester County resident for over thirty (30) years, and has served on the Downingtown Library Company Board as well as provided volunteer leadership for this organization for many years.

Ms. Marchesani, originally from New Jersey, has been a Chester County resident for over thirty (30) years, and has served on the Downingtown Library Company Board as well as provided volunteer leadership for this organization for many years.

attorneys.name: Alex Marek
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Law Lawyers in Stroudsburg, PA
attorneys.bio:
Alex Marek grew up in a small town in Northern Michigan but has been a resident of Monroe County Pennsylvania for the last ten years. Alex, along with his wife, Kristin, and children moved to Pennsylvania when Kristin accepted a position at St. Luke’s Family Practice in Brodheadsville. Prior to moving to Pennsylvania Alex served as a federal criminal investigator with the United States Postal Inspection Service and as a Federal Air Marshal with the United States Federal Air Marshal Service.

Alex’s educational background consists of a Bachelor of Science degree in Biology from Alma College (Alma, MI), a Master of Science degree in Criminal Justice Administration from Ferris State University (Big Rapids, MI), and a Juris Doctorate degree from Western Michigan University-Thomas M. Cooley Law School (Lansing, MI).

Alex has a broad range of experience. Alex began his law enforcement career in 1999 as a Public Safety Officer at a small municipality in Michigan. His duties entailed police both police patrol and firefighting. Alex also served in the United States Army and received an Honorable Discharge for his military service. Alex has also been employed as a police officer with the City of York (PA) and served as a law clerk for the Honorable Judge Jon Mark at the Monroe County (PA) Court of Common Pleas.

Alex has been a licensed attorney since 2007. Alex first acquired his bar license in the State of Michigan in May of 2007 and later became licensed with the Pennsylvania Supreme Court in 2016. Alex is also registered as a licensed patent attorney with the United States Patent and Trademark Office. Additionally, Alex is a member of the federal bar in the Middle District of Pennsylvania, Eastern District of Pennsylvania, and the United States Supreme Court.

Alex has worked the last several years practicing law as a solo practitioner while serving as a part-time detective with the Monroe County District Attorney’s Office. Alex also coached little league baseball with Stroudsburg Little League along with coaching Football and Baseball at Stroudsburg Highschool.

In June 2021 Alex accepted a full-time detective position with the Monroe County District Attorney’s Office before transitioning to the position of Assistant District Attorney in June 2022 with the Northampton County District Attorney’s Office. In the time employed by Northampton County District Attorney’s Office Alex was promoted from Assistant District Attorney to Deputy District Attorney where he served as Chief of the Appellate Unit until January of 2024 when Alex was unfortunately one of the several attorneys let go by then newly elected District Attorney in a near complete overhaul of the office.

Subsequently, Alex worked part-time at both the Luzerne County District Attorney’s Office as an Assistant District Attorney and the law firm of Newman Williams, P.C. until accepting a full-time role Newman Williams, P.C. where he continues concentrating his legal practice primarily in the field of litigation but also practices in municipal law, zoning, and criminal law.

attorneys.name: Darlene A. Marquette
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Offices of Brian E. Quinn
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
I come from a family of Philadelphia blue collar workers and understand how important a weekly paycheck is. I was the first in my generation to go to college and then law school. I worked my way through both.

I have been evaluating and litigating workers’ compensation cases for most of my 27 year legal career. I worked in the Philadelphia Court of Common Pleas as a law clerk. I later worked for the Pennsylvania Supreme Court. Both of these positions provided significant insight into decisions that shaped the law. I also tried many criminal cases which gave me invaluable trial experience.

I carry these experiences into our workers’ compensation practice and work to maximize an injured worker’s benefits. While I have effectively negotiated workers’ compensation settlements, my vast experience enables me to try a case as well. So if a settlement is not in a client’s best interest, I can fight to get a successful decision from the Judge.

Let me fight for you. I will personally handle your matter. I will always take the time to listen to your questions and understand your concerns.

attorneys.name: Marissa B. Marshall
attorneys.practice_type: Elder Law Issues Lawyers in Bloomsburg, PA
attorneys.bio:
Marissa is a founding member at Kreisher Marshall & Associates, LLC and one of two certified elder law attorneys in Columbia and Montour Counties. She received her certification in 2016 from the National Elder Law Foundation as authorized by the Supreme Court. Marissa specializes in the areas of elder law, estate planning and administration, special needs planning and guardianship. Since 2021, Marissa has been the co-founder and co-chair of Dementia Friendly Susquehanna Valley, a division of Dementia Friendly Pennsylvania which provides education and outreach to those living with dementia and their care partners in the counties of Columbia, Montour, Northumberland and lower Luzerne.

A native of Indiana, Marissa earned her B.A. from Purdue University in 2005 and later earned her Juris Doctorate from Western Michigan University - Cooley Law School in Lansing, MI in 2008. Following law school, Marissa relocated to the Bloomsburg area where she worked as an associate attorney. In 2011, Marissa began focusing her career on elder law, with the assistance of Marianne Kreisher, at the Law Offices of Kreisher & Gregorowicz. In 2016, Marianne and Marissa introduced the concept of life care planning to their clients and community by becoming members of the Life Care Planning Law Firm Association and designating their office as a Life Care Planning Law Firm. They remain the only Life Care Planning Law Firm in the counties of Columbia and Montour. In 2019, Marissa and Marianne purchased Kreisher & Gregorowicz, changed the name to Kreisher Marshall & Associates, LLC, and redirected the entire office's focus to elder law.

Marissa is a member of the Pennsylvania Association of Elder Law Attorneys; National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys; Pennsylvania Bar Association where she serves on the Elder Law Council of the Elder Law Section and co-editor of the Elder Law Section newsletter; Columbia-Montour Bar Association; National Elder Law Foundation; Life Care Planning Law Firm Association and is an accredited attorney with the Department of Veterans Affairs. Marissa is a regular presenter for the Pennsylvania Bar Institute continuing education programs and was a contributing author to Elder Law in Pennsylvania, Ch. 11 - Medical Assistance Marriage Issues (5th ed., PBI Press 2019). She is also active in her community as the Vice-Chair of the Board of Directors for the Community Giving Foundation and donates her time to the Bloomsburg Kiwanis Club and an annual golf tournament organized by the Knights of Columbus in Berwick benefiting Pennsylvania Wounded Warriors, Inc.

attorneys.name: Jordan A. Marzzacco
attorneys.practice_type: Motor Vehicle Accidents Lawyers in Harrisburg, PA
attorneys.bio:
Jordan A. Marzzacco obtained her Bachelor’s Degree from the University of Pittsburgh (cum laude) and her law degree from Widener University School of Law (magna cum laude). While at Widener, Jordan earned membership to the Widener Law Journal review staff and wrote articles published on topics relating to personal injury matters.

Following graduation, Jordan practiced civil litigation defense for a short time before pursuing a career in plaintiff’s personal injury law at Handler, Henning & Rosenberg, where she represented victims of defective drugs and medical products in “mass-tort” claims against pharmaceutical companies and those killed or seriously injured by others in motor vehicle crashes, tractor trailer crashes, slip/trip and falls, dog bites and other cases.

Currently, Jordan continues to represent individual victims injured in motor vehicle crashes, premises liability cases, dog bite cases, construction site accidents and civil rights matters. Jordan also continues to represent those injured or killed by dangerous and defective drugs and products in mass-tort actions.

In 2020, Jordan was recognized by her peers for her excellence in personal injury law by being selected as a “Super Lawyer Rising Star.” Super Lawyers is highly selective and is only awarded to attorneys who show outstanding skill and promise in their respective legal areas. Jordan was also named to the National Trial Lawyers list of “Top 40 under 40” in 2020, another exclusive invitation awarded to highly-qualified trial lawyers practicing civil plaintiff’s law.

Jordan is a member of the Pennsylvania Association for Justice (PAJ) and the American Association for Justice (AAJ).

Jordan also enjoys providing legal services to those in need, regularly volunteering for the Dauphin County Bar Association’s Pro Bono Programs, including Wills for Heroes and the Bethesda Mission Legal Clinic.

attorneys.name: Christopher J. Marzzacco
attorneys.practice_type: Motor Vehicle Accidents Lawyers in Harrisburg, PA
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Marzzacco’s practice is concentrated in automobile, motorcycle and trucking case litigation, including Wrongful Death and Survival actions. Mr. Marzzacco also represents persons seriously injured or killed in premises liability cases, work accidents, and by dangerous or defective products.

Mr. Marzzacco was rated by his peers as “The Best Lawyers in America” from 2017 - 2020 and named in “Super Lawyers” from 2017 - 2020. Mr. Marzzacco has lectured at Continuing Legal Education seminars, presenting on various topics to other lawyers and organizations and has written on a variety of topics relating to personal injury law, automobile law and automobile insurance issues for the Legal Intelligencer and other publications.

Over the years, Mr. Marzzacco has personally made several exceptional recoveries in death and catastrophic cases for his clients including settlements of $2.15 million; $1.85 million; $1.625 million; $1.5 million, $1.015 million and $1 million. Mr. Marzzacco has also been co-counsel in several complex cases that resulted in confidential, multi-million dollar awards and settlements.

From 2001 - 2010, Mr. Marzzacco served on York County’s panel of Arbitrators in general civil litigation cases and from 2011-2012, 2017 and 2018, was appointed Chairman of a panel in Dauphin County. He is a member of several Trial Lawyers’ groups, including the Pennsylvania Association for Justice (PAJ), the American Association for Justice (AAJ), the Philadelphia Trial Lawyers Association (PTLA), and the Dauphin, York and Cumberland County Bar Associations.

Mr. Marzzacco has taught trial advocacy at Widener University School of Law’s Intensive Trial Advocacy Program (ITAP) since 2001 and has coached trial teams for Widener University’s Mock Trial program as well. Since 2011, Mr. Marzzacco has been involved with EndDD.org, traveling across Pennsylvania giving presentations to high school students encouraging them to drive without distraction.

Originally from Carbondale, a small town in Northeastern Pennsylvania, Mr. Marzzacco earned his law degree in 1996 from Widener University School of Law and received his undergraduate degree from Wilkes University in 1993. Chris and his wife Jennifer have lived in the Harrisburg area since 1996.

attorneys.name: Bruce P. Matez APM
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce and Family Law Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Bruce is a lifelong resident of Southern New Jersey and has been practicing family law for 25 years and is a divorced father who has a healthy relationship with his former wife. Early in his career, Bruce recognized the inefficiencies and inadequacies of the Family Court system as a means for helping spouses navigate the emotional, legal and financial issues in their divorces. He was determined to find a better way for people to resolve their differences other than in the traditional adversarial system which tends to rip families apart and create more animosity and ill feelings between divorcing spouses. In 1995, just 6 years into his legal career, Bruce attended a 40 hour Divorce Mediation training and has been mediating divorce and family law cases ever since. In 2011, upon learning about Collaborative Divorce, Bruce attending a training to become a Collaborative Attorney, and was instrumental in bringing Collaborative Divorce to South Jersey. Bruce is extremely proud of his accomplishments and successes as a Mediator, Collaborative Attorney, Arbitrator, Parenting Coordinator, and Litigator. Bruce’s focus and goal is to help his clients reach fair and equitable settlments, avoid the anxiey, stress and financial burden of litigation through the court, and spend less money on attorneys and more on themselves and their families. He takes the time to educate his clients on the law, explain the range of possible resolution of issues, the likely best and worst case scenarios, and works toward an amicable resolution of the issues based upon his client’s informed, rational, and reasonable decision, as well as his/her best interests. Bruce strives toward striking a healthy balance between effective negotiation and strong advocacy. When necessary and appropriate, he uses his knowledge, experience and strong advocacy skills in litigation. When necessary, Bruce is a tenacious advocate and litigator. His ability to effectively communicate with his clients, empathize, listen, provide personal service, analyze issues, and represent their interests with knowlegde and skill, has earned him the respect and admiration of his colleagues, judges, and clients, as well as the gratitude of many of his former clients.

attorneys.name: Troy James Mattes
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Troy J. Mattes, P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Lawyers in Lancaster, PA
attorneys.bio:
Troy James Mattes has been practicing immigration law for over 21 years and has a special interest in immigration law matters. After graduating from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1990, and prior to law school, Mr. Mattes spent three years overseas in Gabon, Africa with the United States Peace Corps. During his time in Africa, Mr. Mattes gained a unique knowledge of life in other countries. This insight contributes to his appreciation for his clients’ special circumstances and the personal attention he gives to each client’s case.

Since 1998, Mr. Mattes has been representing clients in all types of immigration matters before the Immigration Courts including bail/bond matters at the York County Prison in York, Pennsylvania. Further, Mr. Mattes has successfully helped many clients in obtaining lawful permanent resident status and waiver approvals from U.S. Consulates abroad where he enjoys a success rate of over 95% in consular waiver cases.

Mr. Mattes graduated from Widener University School of Law in 1998 and earned a Bachelor of Science Degree in Political Science from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1990. He is a member of the American Immigration Lawyers Association (AILA) and has served as Vice President of the AILA Philadelphia Chapter. Mr. Mattes is also a member of the Pennsylvania and Lancaster Bar Associations. He serves annually as an Arbitrator for the Lancaster Court of Common Pleas. Mr. Mattes is capable in Spanish and fluent in French.

Mr. Mattes is admitted to practice before the United States Citizenship and Immigration Services, and is able to represent clients before the Immigration Court in all 50 States. Mr. Mattes is also admitted to practice in the State Courts of Pennsylvania, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 3rd Circuit and the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania.

attorneys.name: Nicholas W. Mattiacci
attorneys.practice_type: Automobile and Trucking Accidents Lawyers in Cheltenham, PA
attorneys.bio:
Nick serves as Trial Counsel and Director of Business Development with Stampone Law and focuses on a variety of complex civil litigation matters including representation of plaintiffs in connection with catastrophic personal injury, automobile accidents, wrongful death, premises liability, liquor liability, product liability, medical malpractice and construction-related accidents. In addition to being an effective trial lawyer, Nick is a rare professional advocate who has experience working in his community, in corporate America and in Government.

Nick began his career as a litigator with the City of Philadelphia before leaving to mount a campaign for the Pennsylvania House of Representatives, House District 153. As a first time political candidate, despite being outnumbered 4-1 in voter registration, Nick relentlessly advocated his bipartisan message to his district, took part in 7 candidate debates, successfully raised over $250,000 and knocked on more than 13,000 homes before losing by just 1,000 votes. Thereafter, Nick was recruited to an international healthcare corporation where he held two executive positions initially serving as President of one portfolio company, before being tasked with starting a new corporate development division which oversaw business development for a diverse portfolio of 5 companies. Nick thereafter returned to Government serving as an Administration Official for Pennsylvania Governor Tom Corbett and was asked to remain on in his official capacity with incoming Pennsylvania Governor Tom Wolf.

Nick's experience as a litigator, community leader, corporate and Government executive provides him with a unique perspective our clients really relate to.

Background and Education

Nick is a proud graduate of LaSalle College High School and Temple University. Nick received his law degree from Widener University School of Law (DE) in 2006 and is admitted to the Bar in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, the State of New Jersey and the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania. Nick also achieved a master's degree in law, LL.M. in Trial Advocacy, from Temple University Beasley School of Law in 2008. Nick serves as chairman of the McKinley civic association in Abington and is a board member of the LaSalle College High School Alumni Association; the Liguori Academy; The National Italian American Political Action Committee and St. Anthony Society of Philadelphia.

Nick and his wife Amanda, a registered nurse with Holy Redeemer live in Abington with their three children, Luca, Nicky, Angelina and olde English bulldogge Butch!

attorneys.name: Lee F. Mauger
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Pottstown, PA
attorneys.bio:
Lee F. Mauger has been engaged in the private practice of law in Pottstown, Pennsylvania for over 40 years. A Pottstown native and Hill School graduate, Mr. Mauger received his Bachelor of Arts from the University of Pennsylvania in 1978, and his Juris Doctorate in 1981 from the Dickinson School of Law in Carlisle, Pennsylvania. After a brief stint with the Montgomery County Public Defender's Office, Mr. Mauger returned to Pottstown to join the firm founded by his father, L. Stanley Mauger, Esq. With general practice experience in a variety of areas of the law, including business structuring, land use and transactional real estate, over the years, Lee and his father transitioned their focus to estate planning and estate administration, including trust drafting and interpretation. Mr. Mauger has partnered several firms in Pottstown, including Mauger and Major and Mauger and Meter, eventually entering solo practice in 2020 before joining Wolf Baldwin in 2022. Mr. Mauger has counseled hundreds of Pottstown area residents, providing a clear, understandable explanation of the law, and practical advice and solutions to their important personal and financial concerns.

In addition to his professional practice, Mr. Mauger has served on several local community boards, including the Pottstown Library, and was former president of the Pottstown Area Lawyers Association. Mr. Mauger was former Vice-Chairman of the North Coventry Planning Commission, and currently remains in that capacity with the Union Township Planning Commission in Berks County, Pennsylvania, where he resides.

attorneys.name: Mark A. May
attorneys.practice_type: Insurance Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
Mark A. May is a Director at Wilbraham Lawler & Bubas. He is a litigator with 27+ years of experience. He actively represents clients in insurance coverage, insurance defense and other complex commercial litigation matters. Mark has extensive experience in using mediation, appraisal, arbitration, and litigation to obtain and defend against monetary and non-monetary recoveries, settlements, awards, and verdicts for his clients. Mr. May has the unique experience of litigating on behalf of insurance companies and policyholders. He has secured significant dismissals of insurance coverage actions brought against his insurance company clients.

Mark has litigated on behalf of and defended his clients against claims asserting breach of contract, tort, negligence, tortious interference, fraud, unjust enrichment, estoppel, and misappropriation of trade secrets, as well as many other causes of action.

Mark earned his B.A. degree from Pennsylvania State University and his J.D. degree, cum laude, from University of Pennsylvania Law School.

Born in McKeesport, PA, Paul started his legal career with a small law firm in his hometown serving the community, including helping laid-off steelworkers file for bankruptcy when the local steel mills were closing. He has tried or settled hundreds of cases involving injuries as a result of auto accidents, slip and falls and defective products or buildings. Jacob Mazur is a Senior Associate at Rowe Law Offices, P.C., where he focuses his practice exclusively on Family Law. A native of the Lehigh Valley, Jacob brings a practical, results-oriented approach to representing clients across Central and Eastern Pennsylvania.

Born and raised in the Lehigh Valley, Jacob is a proud graduate of Freedom High School in Bethlehem. His journey toward the law began at Kutztown University, where he earned his degree in Criminal Justice with a minor in Paralegal Studies. This early academic focus provided him with a unique, ground-level understanding of the legal system before he even entered law school.

Jacob earned his Juris Doctor from Duquesne University School of Law. While at Duquesne, he distinguished himself through his work with the Family Law Clinic, where he provided essential legal services to disadvantaged individuals. During this time, Jacob gained invaluable courtroom experience, earning the privilege of representing clients in real-world litigation. This clinical background—combined with his work at two law firms handling family law and criminal discovery during law school—shaped his approach to practice: be prepared, be persistent, and always prioritize the client's well-being.

Jacob lives in the Lehigh Valley with his wife, their young child, and their two dogs. Outside of the office, he enjoys spending time with his family and staying involved in the local community.
