attorneys.name: Daniel E. McCabe
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Law Lawyers in West Chester, PA
attorneys.bio:
Daniel E. McCabe is Certified as a specialist in the practice of workers' compensation law by the Pennsylvania Bar Association's Section on Workers' Compensation Law as authorized by the Pennsylvania Supreme Court.

Mr. McCabe was born in West Chester, Pennsylvania, and educated in West Chester until he completed college. He attended West Chester East High School and graduated in 1991.

Mr. McCabe attended West Chester University, as a Speech Communications major and a Political Science minor. He graduated summa cum laude with a Bachelor of Arts in speech communications in 1995. Following his undergraduate work, he attended Villanova University School of Law, where he was active in Moot Court, and earned his Juris Doctor in 1998.

Mr. McCabe was admitted to the bar in 1998, and is licensed to practice law in Pennsylvania. Upon completion of law school he was a clerk for the Honorable Judge Lawrence Wood in the Court of Common Pleas in West Chester. He has also practiced corporate law and collection law in a firm in West Chester, in addition to maintaining his own practice.

In recent years, Mr. McCabe has concentrated his practice solely on workers' compensation law. His first experience with workers' compensation was representing employers and insurance companies. However, since 2003, he has represented injured workers exclusively. His experience on both sides of workers' compensation law allows him to serve his clients with the valuable knowledge of how the insurance companies operate. He is active in the Workers' Compensation section of the Chester County Bar Association.

Mr. McCabe spends his free time as an avid cyclist, even riding the cobblestones of Belgium. He is married with two children. He joined Wolf, Baldwin & Associates, P.C. in 2006 and is proud to be a part of one of the largest workers' compensation departments in the area.

attorneys.name: Thomas J. McClain, Esquire
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
Attorney McClain represents people harmed by auto accidents, truck accidents, slip and falls, workplace accidents, as well as other types of personal injury. With a background in civil rights law, he also represents underserved individuals in cases involving assaults or police brutality. In all of his cases, he recognizes that immense emotional and financial stress a client can face and works to relieve and end that struggle.

Before working at Dugan & Associates Mr. McClain ran a successful solo practice. He understands the pressures and joys of being self-employed. Early in his career Mr. McClain was an insurance defense lawyer and an insurance company lawyer. Today, this experience gives him valuable insights into the opposition that he uses to benefit his clients.

Mr. McClain is a certified mediator and has extensive experience as an arbitrator. He is a former special agent with United States Drug Enforcement Administration where he was a lead investigator on a multi-agency task force that successfully prosecuted a major crack cocaine organization on the streets of Detroit. Mr. McClain is a graduate of Lehigh University and the University of Pittsburgh School of Law and is a member of numerous professional associations.

attorneys.name: Matt M. McClenahen
attorneys.practice_type: DUI/DWI Lawyers in State College, PA
attorneys.bio:
In 2001, McClenahen began working for the busy York County Public Defender's Office, where he quickly gained a reputation as a formidable trial attorney. McClenahen's mentors as a public defender included many experienced, successful defense attorneys and he would not have become the skilled advocate he is today without their help. McClenahen would serve as a public defender for 5 years, acquiring death penalty defense qualification on July 30, 2006, pursuant to Rule 801 of the Pennsylvania Rules of Criminal Procedure.

McClenahen had a total of 36 jury trials as a public defender, with 24 wins, 11 losses and 1 hung-jury.* In non-felony drug trials, McClenahen's record as a public defender was an amazing 20-6-1, which would be impressive for a prosecutor, but is much more remarkable for a defense attorney, given the fact that the deck is usually stacked against criminal defendants.** In felony drug trials, which are generally the most difficult type of case for a defense lawyer to win given the nature of the evidence, McClenahen has still managed to win 6 of 11 trials throughout his career, including a record of 5-0 in cases in which the Commonwealth's case relied on the testimony of a CI.

In 2005, McClenahen worked on a death penalty case as co-counsel, but handled only pre-trial matters, as he was not yet death penalty qualified. In 2006, McClenahen left the York County Public Defender's Office and returned to State College to practice criminal defense, opening McClenahen Law Firm LLC on November 1, 2006.

McClenahen's interests include history, sociology, anthropology, psychology, languages, natural sciences, music, travel, football and soccer.

*A win in a criminal trial does not necessarily mean an all-out acquittal, but a trial result that was better than the prosecutor's plea offer or the likely result had the defendant pled guilty to all charges without the benefit of a plea agreement. Thus, a defendant who was charged with the first-degree felony of aggravated assault, but is convicted of only the second degree misdemeanor or simple assault, won his trial, because he was convicted of a much less serious offense. Had he been convicted of aggravated assault, he would probably have been sent to state prison, while a conviction for simple assault could result in a sentence of probation. However, if the client has only one charge and is convicted, McClenahen still considers this a loss for win-loss record purposes even if the sentence turns out to be more favorable than the sentence offered pursuant to a plea agreement.

**The deck is usually stacked, against criminal defendants because the police very rarely, if ever, file criminal charges against a defendant unless they themselves are convinced beyond a reasonable doubt of a defendant's guilt. Where the evidence is flimsy, a prudent police officer will generally elect not to file charges unless and until he or she can acquire more solid evidence. Felony drug cases are generally the most difficult cases to defend, as they often involve a sale of drugs either directly to an undercover police officer or to a confidential informant, while the police are observing, recording or filming the transaction. With the evidence in most criminal cases being overwhelmingly against the defendant, it takes a very skilled criminal defense attorney to overcome this disadvantage, while a prosecutor of modest ability can often win convictions.

attorneys.name: Marie K. McConnell
attorneys.practice_type: COMMERCIAL REAL ESTATE Lawyers in Allentown, PA
attorneys.bio:
Marie K. McConnell is a shareholder and Chair of the Firm's Corporate, Business & Banking Group. Her practice focuses on commercial transactions, including commercial real estate acquisitions and sales, entity restructures, charter schools, for-profit and nonprofit mergers and acquisitions and organizational issues. She also has significant experience in counseling clients with respect to tax exemptions and tax assessment appeals.

Ms. McConnell merges an undergraduate background in economics and an LL.M. in taxation into her legal practice, resulting in thoughtful, business-oriented solutions that fit each client's goals. She is a trusted advisor to her clients and values the personal relationships she has built over the years. Ms. McConnell is dedicated, driven and highly responsive.

Ms. McConnell brings the same passion with which she serves her clients to the Lehigh Valley community and the Firm itself. She is currently serving as 2022 Past-President of CREW Lehigh Valley, the local 100+ member chapter of a 12,000 member global organization dedicated to transforming the commercial real estate industry by advancing women. Additionally, she is a member of the Firm's Executive Committee as well as its Compensation, Hiring and Retention Committees.

In 2019, Ms. McConnell was honored by Lehigh Valley Business as a Woman of Influence. In addition, her peers have recognized her as a "Super Lawyer - Pennsylvania Rising Star" each year since 2012, a designation awarded to only 2.5% of attorneys in Pennsylvania under 40. She was also recognized by the Greater Lehigh Valley Chamber of Commerce as the inaugural "Future Business Leader of the Lehigh Valley" in 2013.

She is local to the area, having grown up in Allentown.

attorneys.name: R. Brandon McCullough
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
Brandon concentrates his practice primarily in the areas of insurance coverage and bad faith litigation and complex commercial and business litigation. He has represented insurance companies in a wide array of coverage disputes in trial courts and on appeal in both state and federal court. He has litigated and counselled clients on issues involving numerous types of commercial and personal lines insurance policies, including commercial general liability, excess and umbrella liability, directors and officers liability, professional liability, environmental liability, builders' risk, commercial property, auto liability, homeowners insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, specified disease insurance, and long and short term care insurance. Brandon's coverage matters have included disputes over coverage for construction defects, environmental contamination, latent and progressive injuries, auto liability/UIM, and first-party property losses. He also regularly represents insurers in high-exposure bad faith claims, and has represented insurers, brokers and agents in claims for violation of consumer protection laws. In addition, Brandon frequently provides insurance coverage opinions and advice to insurers throughout the claims handling process.

Brandon also has substantial experience representing businesses and individuals in a wide variety of complex litigation matters including cases involving restrictive covenants and trade secrets, breach of commercial contracts, professional liability of accountants and engineers, products liability, civil rights of public-sector employees, property damage and personal injury.

He is an active member of the Insurance Law Committee of DRI - The Voice of the Defense Bar and the Allegheny County Bar Association where he has taken on multiple leadership roles. He also regularly publishes articles and speaks on insurance law and bad faith topics. Brandon is also a graduate of the International Association of Defense Counsel Trial Academy which was held at Stanford Law School. He has been selected as a Pennsylvania Super Lawyer Rising Star continually since 2013.

During law school, Brandon completed judicial internships with the Honorable Joy Flowers Conti of the United States District Court for the Western District of Pennsylvania and the Honorable John A. Zottola of the Court of Common Pleas of Allegheny County, Pennsylvania. He also served as a law clerk for the staff counsel for a major insurance company.

Matt and his wife, Alexandra, reside in Butler, with their 2 children.

attorneys.name: Joseph P. McDonald Jr.
attorneys.firm_name: Joseph P. McDonald Jr., Esq., P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Business And Commercial Law Lawyers in Stroudsburg, PA
attorneys.bio:
Welcome to the Law Offices of Joseph P. McDonald, Jr. I have been a solo practitioner since November 1992, and have been licensed in Pennsylvania since 1986. I work in a multi-county area in eastern Pennsylvania, including Monroe, Pike, Northampton, Lackawanna, and surrounding counties. My practice focuses largely on transactional work, serving small businesses, consumers, and local governmental bodies.

My work over the years has shown my ability and experience in many areas of the law. I represent many small businesses, including family-owned businesses, sole proprietorships, and businesses with a small group of shareholders. In addition, I assist consumers with their residential real estate transactions and in their estate planning and probate needs. I also have a longstanding relationship as counsel for many municipal governmental bodies, assisting them with issues such as wetland laws, planning and development, and sewage facilities planning.

Involvement in the community is very important to me, as demonstrated through the many professional and civic organizations I am involved in. I am a past President of the Monroe County Bar Association, and an Executive Board Member and current 2008 President of the Pocono Mountains Chamber of Commerce. In the past, I have served as the Chairman of the Small Business Development Committee of this organization. I am an active volunteer in many parts of the business community.

My community involvement also includes work as the Vice President of the Stroudsburg Little League. Over the last several years, I have watched my son play and have served as a coach, volunteer, and umpire in this organization. I was also a founding member and Vice President of the Rotary Club of West End, Monroe County. Working as the leader of the Club's essay-based scholarship programs, I have been able to help emphasize the need for good writing and communication skills.

Working with clients is one of my strongest skills. The goal of the first interview with a client is to determine what result you, the client, are trying to achieve. You need to know that you are part of the solution. My function as your lawyer is to offer guidance and come up with the best questions to ask of the opposing party, or what information would be most useful to you. In a setting where the client is part of a new project (such as a new building or product line), my firm emphasizes a team approach, with the lawyer being part of a team that includes accountants, design professionals, and others. The goal is to get the project off the ground, not complicate it.

My firm blends sensitivity to a client's time frame with the fact that legal skill comes from the need to see the big picture and reflect on the proper way to address an issue. In other words, I don't let speed compromise professional insight on how to approach the issue. A great lawyer understands that his value is more than ministerial, more than pushing papers. As a solo practitioner I embrace the idea that I can get work done without the overhead that comes with a larger firm. You can also be assured that you will not get "lost in the shuffle," as you might in a firm of 50 lawyers.

I take the needs of my clients very seriously. In my public appearances on behalf of my clients, my professionalism shows through in the respect I receive from the judges and opposing counsel. If you are in need of a lawyer for your small business or as a consumer anywhere in eastern Pennsylvania, please call us at the Law Offices of Joseph P. McDonald today. We would like to put our professionalism, experience, and dedication to client service to work for you.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Lawyers Cooperative Book Award, Local Government Law, Akron University, 1986

attorneys.name: Courtney Seda McDonnell
attorneys.practice_type: Insurance Defense Lawyers in King of Prussia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Courtney Seda McDonnell is a graduate of The Dickinson School of Law, where she wrote onto the Dickinson Law Review. Ms. McDonnell is also a graduate of Dickinson College, where she was a Latin major and member of Eta Sigma Phi, the national honorary society for Latin majors.

Before attending law school, Ms. McDonnell taught Latin at a prestigious private school and participated overseas in the study of classical language and archeology. While in law school, she clerked for the Honorable Magistrate Judge Charles B. Smith of the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania and clerked at the law firm of Cozen and O'Connor.

After graduating from law school, Ms. McDonnell accepted a position with the firm then known as Silverman Coopersmith Hillman & Frimmer within its litigation department. Thereafter, Ms. McDonnell co-founded McDonnell & Associates and, upon its opening, was instrumental in organizing and establishing the firm.

Ms. McDonnell is one of the firm's owners and is the firm's managing partner. In that capacity, she oversees all business, marketing and staffing operations of the firm. She also actively promotes and recruits women and minorities for the firm. Additionally, Ms. McDonnell has established a successful flex time program for firm attorneys. Currently, thirty-eight percent (38%) of the firm attorneys work on a flex time arrangement. Ms. McDonnell spoke at the 2011 Wal-Mart Super Conference regarding the success of the flex time program for attorneys at McDonnell & Associates.

Ms. McDonnell supervises several client accounts and oversees a team of associates to ensure that the clients' needs and deadlines are being met. The firm has been recognized by Wal-Mart Stores, Inc. for its excellence in achieving quality indicators and consistency in meeting deadlines.

Ms. McDonnell has appeared in federal and state courts in premises liability, professional negligence, trucking cases, false arrest, and civil rights cases. Ms. McDonnell has tried several cases to verdict. She is licensed to practice law in Pennsylvania and New Jersey.

Ms. McDonnell is a member of the National Association of Women Lawyers (NAWL), the Defense Resource Institute, and the American Bar Association.

Ms. McDonnell works as a volunteer for the Support Center for Child Advocates in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Ms. McDonnell was recently recognized by the Frist Judicial District of Pennsylvania for her pro bono work and was enrolled in the First Judicial District 2010 Pro Bono Roll of Honor. Ms. McDonnell served on the host committee for Child Advocates' annual benefit in 2009, 2010, and 2011 and assisted in soliciting donations for the organization.

Awards and Honors

attorneys.name: Michael R. McFarlin
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Wyomissing, PA
attorneys.bio:
After graduation from the Claude Pettit School of Law, located on the campus of Ohio Northern University, and after doing a year-long judicial clerkship for a 3-judge panel in Wicomico County, Maryland, Mike practiced with Brother-brother firm in Allentown, Pennsylvania, where he remained until 1993. He concentrated on family law matters, some criminal matters, and civil litigation.

Attorney McFarlin started his own law firm in 1993 and practiced as a sole practitioner for approximately a decade, including several matters involving federal courts, and courts outside of Pennsylvania, where he practiced pro hac vice, with the permission of the bars of several different states. He spent another decade as an e-discovery attorney for Pepper Hamilton (now Pepper Troutman) in Philadelphia, working on multi-district pharmaceutical litigation.

Joining Rowe Law Offices P.C. in 2024, Attorney McFarlin has returned to his roots of working for a well-known firm focused on representing clients for divorce, custody, support and related matters, estate planning and administration, and real estate issues. Like the firm itself, he is dedicated to excellent, compassionate client service with an emphasis on candid, frank, and straightforward attorney-client communications, focused on client goals.

Attorney McFarlin is admitted to the bar of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania and the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania. His practice is currently concentrated primarily in the area of family law and divorce, custody, support, adoption, and guardianship matters, along with some specialized areas of civil litigation, including partition, involving dividing up jointly owned real estate in a court of equity.

attorneys.name: Raymond McGarry
attorneys.practice_type: Business and Commercial Litigation Lawyers in King Of Prussia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Ray has handled matters in diverse areas of commercial litigation, including real estate, construction, corporate/shareholder disputes, trade secrets and restrictive covenants, environmental, product liability and contract issues. Ray's practice has included trial and appellate work throughout the state of and federal courts of Pennsylvania and New Jersey. In addition, his experience includes commercial arbitrations and mediations, and other forms of alternative dispute resolution.

In the area of construction litigation, he has represented owners, contractors, subcontractors and construction managers in a variety of matters. He has represented such clients as Heery International, in a dispute arising out of a major renovation project at an elementary school, and Conrail Corporation, in a dispute over delays in the construction of a golf course, where Conrail was a major subcontractor.

Ray has represented real estate developers, as well as commercial landlords and tenants in a variety of matters, including commercial landlord/tenant litigation and broker commission issues. In a recent commercial lease dispute, he recovered in excess of $7 million on behalf of a developer/landlord, in litigation involving the breach of a lease by a tenant in a shopping center.

Ray serves as an elected member and the Vice President of the Abington Township Board of School Directors. Among other responsibilities on the board, he serves as chairman of the board's Negotiations Committee, which has primary responsibility for negotiating contracts with the district's union employees, including the teachers union.

attorneys.name: Terence Sean McGraw
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Blue Bell, PA
attorneys.bio:
As a result of passing the first specialty certification exam of its kind given in Pennsylvania, Terry was recently certified as a specialist in the practice of workers' compensation law by the Pennsylvania Bar Association's Section on Workers' Compensation Law as authorized by the Pennsylvania Supreme Court.

Rated "Superb" by Avvo.com and selected annually as a Super Lawyer since 2008, Terry is an experienced workers' compensation, social security, and employee disability benefit lawyer, Terry has handled cases throughout Pennsylvania. A leader in the field of injury and disability law, he routinely gives presentations and teaches other lawyers, injured workers, insurance professionals and medical professionals about these constantly changing areas of law. Terry has helped thousands of clients with workers' compensation, social security (SSDI and SSI), and disability insurance claims.

Terry is a 1986 graduate of Villanova Law School. While studying at Villanova, he was selected to the Moot Court Board. As a Moot Court Board member, he helped run the school's oral argument competition and argued in national competition. He was the member of a team that reached the semi-finals at the John Marshall School of Law International Privacy Law Moot Court Competition.

Terry has been in private practice since 1986. He has focused his practice on representing injured and disabled workers in workers compensation, social security disability, supplemental security income, short term disability, long term disability and unemployment compensation claims throughout the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania.

In 1994, he formed Monte & McGraw with his partner and longtime friend Alfred Monte. In 2007, he went into solo practice. In 2010, he formed a new firm, Warren & McGraw, with his legal mentor, Jon Warren.

Terry is excited about the combination of Jon's 30 years of experience handling complex personal injury claims, and his 25 years of experience handling benefit claims for the injured and disabled. The combination of their experience allows Jon & Terry to offer their injured and disabled clients the full breadth of legal services those clients need under one roof, personally handled by experienced lawyers.

In addition to being an active speaker about the practice areas he concentrates in, Terry is a sustaining member of the National Organization of Social Security Representatives, and a member of the Pennsylvania Bar Association and its Workers' Compensation Section, the Pennsylvania Association for Justice, the Montgomery County Bar Association and its Workers Compensation, Employment Law and Medical Legal Committees.

Currently on hiatus from singing, Terry was a member of the Saint Rose of Lima choir for over 15 years. He earned A's in judged vocal & choral competitions in high school and was invited to sing in the New York State All-State Chorus. He served as the President of Lower Gwynedd Little League for three years and coached youth soccer, basketball and baseball. He is an active member of the Ancient Order of Hibernians (AOH). He serves as the Chairman of Standing Committee of the AOH Montgomery County Board (a position that makes use of his legal skills) and is a member of the Isle of Erin Major Degree Team, responsible for leading the team in presenting the formal membership ceremonies of the AOH. Recently widowed, he is the father of a college aged son and daughter. The fourth child in a large Irish Catholic family of 6, Terry enjoys regular family gatherings with his raucous "crew" and particularly enjoys cooking the traditional holiday meals served at those gatherings.

attorneys.name: Mary Kate McGrath
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Defense Lawyers in Berwyn, PA
attorneys.bio:
MARY KATE is a Philadelphia native with over 20 years of experience in handling complex health care and medical malpractice litigation, and is a partner at Post & Post LLC. She has successfully represented health care providers from the beginning of litigation through verdict at trial, including physicians, physician assistants, behavioral health providers, physical therapists, nurse practitioners, health care practice groups, health care facilities and health care systems in courts across the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania.

Mary Kate has been published and has lectured extensively both locally and nationally on many topics, including telehealth, HIPAA / privacy law and trends in medical malpractice litigation. She was identified as a Philadelphia Super Lawyers Rising Star from 2010 through 2013.

She received her Bachelor’s degree from Northwestern University. She began law school at Villanova University School of Law, but transferred to Brooklyn Law School to complete her degree when she was cast in a Broadway show during law school. Mary Kate continued to work as a professional actor in theaters across the country, including Broadway, a Broadway National Tour, and in regional theaters. Mary Kate received Barrymore Award nominations for roles performed at the Arden Theater Company and the Walnut Street Theater.

She has been active with community service, volunteering as a pro bono child advocate. Mary Kate is a proud member of the “Mom Choir” at Saint Joseph’s Preparatory School, and has served with her son as a cantor for Our Mother of Consolation Parish in Philadelphia’s Chestnut Hill neighborhood, where she has also taught Sunday Story. She was the Chair of the Steering Committee for the First Annual Harry Potter Weekend in Chestnut Hill. In response to the COVID-19 pandemic, she and her family presented a weekly Disney-themed Zoom sing-along on Sunday evenings with Kids-to-Kids. Mary Kate is currently the Vice Chair of the Board of Directors for Commonwealth Youthchoirs.

attorneys.bio:
Brian E. McKinley has been an attorney with Wilder Mahood McKinley & Oglesby since 2001, becoming partner in June, 2012. Mr. McKinley is a member of the Family Law Section of the American Bar Association, Pennsylvania Bar Association and Allegheny County Bar Association. Mr. McKinley is a Council Member for the Pennsylvania Bar Association Family Law Section. He is also a member of the Public Service Committee and Appellate Practice Committee of the Allegheny County Bar Association. He has served on the Rules Committee and as a Council Member of the Family Law Section of the Allegheny County Bar Association. Mr. McKinley is a former member of the Pittsburgh Matrimonial Inns of Court. He has served as a writer and lecturer for family law continuing legal education seminars and classes, including the Pennsylvania Bar Association Family Law Section Summer Meeting and the Clarion University Legal Conference. Mr. McKinley is a co-author of the Pennsylvania Family Law Practice and Procedure 2012 Supplement.

Mr. McKinley is a graduate of the Family Law Trial Advocacy Institute at the University of Houston School of Law. He graduated from the University of Pittsburgh School of Law in 2000. attorneys.name: Christopher M. McLean
attorneys.practice_type: REAL ESTATE, LAND USE & DEVELOPMENT Lawyers in Allentown, PA
attorneys.bio:
With nearly 20 years' experience as a creative problem solver, Christopher M. McLean is a shareholder in the Firm's Real Estate, Land Use & Development and Corporate, Business & Banking groups. Throughout his career, Mr. McLean has been responsible for the negotiation of complex business, loan and real estate transactions, including a wide variety of transaction documents. He regularly represents clients in front of government agencies and municipal governing bodies in connection with land use and entitlements for real estate projects. He counts businesses of all sizes as his clients, from Fortune 500 retailers and builders to local builders and developers. In addition, he works with personal clients on all aspects of estate planning, including the preparation of wills, trusts, powers of attorney and health care directives (living wills) and administration of estates and trusts.

Mr. McLean takes a practical, common sense approach to the challenges that face his clients, working toward the most efficient outcome without overcomplicating or "overlawyering" the matter. His clients have recognized his practical, insightful solutions and value his in-depth knowledge of the law.

Mr. McLean is a member of the Board of Directors of Ripple Community, Inc. and President the Board of Directors of Ripple's newly formed RCI Village. He is able to translate his real estate and corporate experience to assist the Boards in fulfilling their purpose of providing housing stability. RCI Village's purpose is to provide safe, stable, affordable housing, and support and connections that residents need to achieve long-term housing and life stability.

A native to the Lehigh Valley, Mr. McLean understands the marketplace and unique qualities of doing business here. When not in his hometown of Zionsville, he can likely be found on the beaches of Florida or the Caribbean islands, collecting shells and humming "Margaritaville".

Local Legal Leader, Lehigh Valley Magazine, 2016

attorneys.name: Brooke B. McMorrow Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law/Adoptions Lawyers in Wexford, PA
attorneys.bio:
After working in New York as a criminal defense attorney and as a general practitioner, in 2005, Attorney McMorrow moved to Pittsburgh where she opened up a practice in downtown Pittsburgh. In 2010, Attorney McMorrow relocated her offices to the North Hills in Wexford, Pennsylvania. Attorney McMorrow focuses her practice on family law including divorce, child custody, child support and alimony, adoptions, and collaborative divorce. In addition she helps families with Estate Planning, Estate Probate/Administration, Orphans' Court litigation including will contests and guardianships. She also continues to represent those charged with DUI or other criminal charges in Allegheny and the surrounding counties.

Attorney McMorrow strives to change the stereotypes that people have about attorneys by returning phone calls in a timely manner and above all, listening to the client and providing affordable and knowledgeable legal advice in a comfortable setting. She is licensed to practice law in both Pennsylvania and New York. As a member of the Collaborative Law Association of Southwestern Pennsylvania, Attorney McMorrow is trained in collaborative law.

attorneys.name: Kiku Mehta Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Law Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Kiku Mehta specializes in the growing field of Immigration law as well as the fields of business, real estate, global investment, and development. Before he came to the United States, Mr. Mehta was an immigration lawyer in India where he attended La Shah University in India. He also attended Florida State University and is a member of the Pennsylvania Bar.

Prior to joining Ellenberg Law Group, Mr. Mehta worked as a child advocate for the nonprofit Children’s Services Incorporated (SCI) for over 40 years. Mr. Mehta’s law degree along with his master’s degree in social work made him invaluable in the development of Supervised Independent Living (SIL) for both dependent and delinquent adolescence. Mr. Mehta was essential to the representation of more than 2000 youths in family courts during his 10 years. This involved preparing youths to testify at court, working with birth relatives to explain youth charges, interfacing with probation affairs, advocates, judges, and other court officials.

Additionally, Mr. Mehta is an arbitrator for the Court of Common Pleas in Philadelphia.

Mr. Mehta speaks Hindi, Urdu and Gujarda.

attorneys.name: Susan A. Meredith
attorneys.practice_type: Appellate Law Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Susan A. Meredith has been an associate with Caroselli, Beachler & Coleman, L.L.C. since 1995. Attorney Meredith graduated magna cum laude with a Bachelor of Arts from Dickinson College in 1992. In 1995 she earned her J.D. from Duquesne University School of Law, where she was a member of the Law Review from 1993 through 1995 and served as Associate Recent Decisions Editor from 1994 through 1995. Admitted to practice in Pennsylvania, Georgia, the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Pennsylvania and the 3rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, attorney Meredith is a civil litigation lawyer focusing on appellate law. She has been involved in every aspect of an appeal including post-verdict motions, analyzing and researching law, perfecting appeals, preparing appellate briefs and appendices, post-argument motions and petitions for certification of certiorari. Attorney Meredith is familiar with Pennsylvania appellate forums, having handled cases before Pennsylvania's Commonwealth Court, Superior Court and Supreme Court, and the United States Court of Appeals for the 3rd Circuit.

Beyond attorney Meredith's appellate focus, her practice areas include workers' compensation law, Social Security and personal injury, including auto collision, premises liability, product liability and denials of long-term disability benefits. She is a member of the Allegheny County Bar Association, Allegheny County Women's Bar Association, the Pennsylvania Bar Association, Western Pennsylvania Trial Lawyers Association and the Pennsylvania Association for Justice. Attorney Meredith volunteers with the Allegheny County Protection from Abuse Program, representing victims of domestic violence in obtaining PFA orders, and she is an active volunteer in her children's schools and her church.

attorneys.name: Melissa Merk
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Melissa Merk is an accomplished attorney who worked for many years on complex litigation with two large, global law firms on cases involving pharmaceuticals and medical devices. Her practice with Kline & Specter focuses, similarly, on mass torts concerning product liability cases.

In litigation regarding pharmaceutical anti-psychotic medication, Merk managed some 7,500 cases. She participated as trial counsel in a number of matters as well as conducting and defending hundreds of depositions.

Immediately before joining Kline & Specter, Merk was a partner at Faegre Drinker Biddle & Reath LLP, a law firm with offices across the United States and abroad. She served as a member and later vice chair of the firm’s Products Liability Practice Group.

Merk directed a team of partners, associates and paralegals in litigation as well as coordinating with experts to review cases and present reports, drafting pre-trial and trial motions, and preparing cases for trial. In addition to work on anti-psychotic drug litigation, Merk also managed the firm’s vaginal mesh litigation team.

Prior to that experience, she was an attorney with another global law firm, Reed Smith LLP, where she worked on commercial litigation before transitioning to the firm’s product liability group. In that capacity, she prepared for and participated in numerous mass tort trials involving prescription medications and assisted in managing thousands of mass tort claims.

Before working as a lawyer at Reed Smith, Merk was a law clerk to U.S. District Judge Joseph H. Rodriguez for the District of New Jersey. She was also a law clerk at the Lawrenceville, N.J., firm of Hinkle, Fingles & Prior which provides specialized legal services for seniors and families of children and adults with disabilities.

Merk earned her bachelor’s degree at Rider University and was named a Presidential Scholar each year of her attendance. She attended Rutgers University School of Law, where she was a Dean’s Merit Scholar, lead articles editor for the Rutgers Law Journal, and was a teaching assistant for First Year Research and Writing and the Moot Court program.

Merk is admitted to practice in Pennsylvania, New Jersey and the District of Columbia.

attorneys.name: Lorraine W. Mervan
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
Ms. Mervan joined GGGH&A in September 2006. Attorney Mervan has practiced in the area of family law since 1992. After law school, Ms. Mervan practiced corporate law for three years. Previously, after receiving an M.B.A., Ms. Mervan was employed in internal auditing and employee benefits accounting at Alcoa from 1980 through 1986. During her employment at Alcoa, Ms. Mervan passed the CPA exam and was licensed as a CPA based on industry experience until she began law school in 1986.

While at the University of Pittsburgh School of Law, Attorney Mervan was an instructor of legal writing to first year students. She was on the staff of the University of Pittsburgh Law Review. Attorney Mervan is a member of the Pittsburgh chapter of the Order of the Coif.

Attorney Mervan has been a lecturer from 2002 to 2006 on family law for the annual General Practitioners’ Update sponsored by the Pennsylvania Bar Institute. Her written materials on custody have been included in the coursebook for the Fundamentals of Family Law seminar sponsored by the Pennsylvania Bar Institute, most recently, in 2006. She is a past council member of the Family Law Section of the Allegheny County Bar Association and a past participant in the Matrimonial Inns of Court.

She is a member of the Allegheny County Bar Association and the Pennsylvania Bar Association.

attorneys.name: Jay Metzbower
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in York, PA
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Metzbower takes great pride in his reputation of being different than most attorneys. He is known for his down to earth and straight forward approach that makes it easy for clients to understand complex legal issues. Jay credits this skill to his training and experience serving as a Sheriff’s Deputy for eleven years.

During his time with the Sheriff’s Office, Jay received a Life Saving Award, Governor’s Citation, and the Scott T. Brousseau Community Service Award for charitable work in the community. As an attorney, he has a passion for helping first responders, veterans, and their families. Guided by a strong sense of responsibility to protect those who are most vulnerable, he focuses on Medicaid qualification, asset protection from long-term care and nursing home costs, and complex estate planning. He understands the significant consequences that inadequate estate plans can create for minor children, disabled beneficiaries, and surviving family members, and he works diligently to ensure clients receive plans tailored to their unique needs.

For the last two years, he has been teaching workshops on estate planning and speaking in the community to educate others on the pitfalls of common estate planning mistakes.

Jay has been living in York since 2013, but is originally from Baltimore and remains loyal to the Orioles and Ravens. In his spare time, he enjoys motorcycle riding, hiking, playing York County Oldtimers baseball, and spending time with his two sons, Connor and Reilly.

Jay earned his Juris Doctor, Cum Laude from the University of Baltimore School of Law. He is admitted to the bars of both Pennsylvania and Maryland.

attorneys.name: Neil H. Meyer
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Litigation Lawyers in Media, PA
attorneys.bio:
Having spent over 20 years representing clients in a wide variety of civil litigation areas including bankruptcy, divorce, custody, child support, estate administration and litigation, contracts, personal injury, unemployment compensation, and collections, Neil Meyer concentrates his practice in estate administration, estate planning, estate litigation, and family law matters. After practicing for a few years in Georgia, he moved to southeastern Pennsylvania and practiced in Philadelphia for over twelve years. Now practicing in Media, Delaware County, Pennsylvania, Neil Meyer helps clients fight for their inheritance rights and defend their fiduciary decisions along with guiding them through the probate process and settling estates. He helps clients by drafting wills and other estate planning documents to protect their loved ones and their property and to ensure that their wishes are followed after they pass away.

After earning his B.A. from the University of Pennsylvania, Mr. Meyer used his Russian language skills by working as a civilian for the Department of Defense for several years. He then earned his law degree from Emory University in Atlanta, Georgia , and started practicing in the private sector after he was graduated. Living with his wife and three children in Middletown township, Mr. Meyer is a volunteer with the Selective Service System. In his free time, he tries to improve his budding golf game.

attorneys.name: Eric C. Milby
attorneys.practice_type: Business Divorce (Shareholder, Partner, Member Disputes) Lawyers in Narberth, PA
attorneys.bio:
For over twenty years, Mr. Milby has been helping clients resolve corporate, partnership, real estate, construction, and a wide variety of other commercial and contract disputes. His primary practice area is business litigation. Much of that litigation involves disputes within a business such as shareholder disputes, partnership disputes or membership disputes where one party is claiming “minority oppression” or “freezeout/squeezeout” by a majority of the business owners or violations of the fiduciary duties that business partners owe to the company and each other. These cases are often called “business divorce” cases or “dissolution” cases because the business owners often end up going their separate ways either by settlement, splitting up or partitioning the business, dissolving or closing down the business, or because one party receives a cash payment or buyout to leave the business (Business Divorce). Additionally, much of his practice is devoted to disputes between businesses primarily in construction and real estate issues.

Mr. Milby has had remarkable success in jury trials, bench trials and arbitration matters. Within a week after receiving his license to practice, he tried his first bench trial and has been trying cases ever since. However, in this day and age, with clients preferring to avoid the expense and uncertainty of litigation, more than 90% of all business cases result in negotiated settlements. Thus, Mr. Milby has focused much of his professional development on the art, and science, of successful negotiation. Those skills, backed up by an ever-present willingness to take an adversary all the way through trial and a successful litigation track record, regularly enable him to achieve the best possible result for the client while avoiding the expense and distraction of protracted litigation.

Additional Information

Repeat panelist – Nuts and Bolts of Practicing in the Commerce Case Management Program, Pennsylvania Bar Institute

Organizer and Moderator – Counseling the Corporation, Pennsylvania Bar Institute

Panelist – 50 Ways to Leave Your Lover . . . err, Business Partner, American Bar Association, 2015 Spring Meeting of the Section of Business Law

Martindale-Hubbell Peer Review Ratings were created in 1887 as an objective tool that would attest to a lawyer’s ability and professional ethics, based on the confidential opinions of other lawyers and judges who have worked with the lawyers they are evaluating. The Martindale-Hubbell Peer Review Ratings have remained the most prestigious and widely respected lawyer rating system in the world for over one hundred years.

For more information about how the Ratings process works and how the Ratings are used in our profession, please go to www.martindale.com/ratings.

attorneys.name: Alan S. Miller
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
Alan has more than thirty-eight years of experience in complex litigation and counseling, concentrating in the areas of environmental law, insurance coverage and bad faith, and commercial litigation. He chairs the firm’s Environmental and Energy Law practice and the Insurance Coverage and Bad Faith Litigation practice.

Alan’s environmental law practice has involved counseling, litigation and alternative dispute resolution of matters involving municipal, residual, and hazardous waste permitting and compliance, contribution and cost recovery actions under CERCLA and related state statutes, claims for natural resource damages, contamination from leaking underground storage tanks, air and water pollution regulatory permitting and enforcement actions, oil and gas drilling compliance and transactions, and real estate transactions involving contaminated and recycled industrial sites.

Alan’s insurance law practice involves representing insurance companies in a wide array of coverage disputes, both before litigation and in court, arising out of commercial liability, property, medical professional and personal lines policies, including disputes over coverage for claims involving construction defects, exposure to toxic substances, product defects, major property losses, professional liability, infringement of intellectual property rights and violations of consumer protection laws.

Prior to entering private practice, Alan served as a trial attorney with the Environmental Enforcement Section, United States Department of Justice, and as an Assistant Counsel with the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Resources. He is a frequent lecturer and author of materials for continuing legal education courses in the areas of environmental law and insurance coverage.

attorneys.bio:
Christian focuses his practice in the business transactional, commercial real estate and municipal arenas, which Christian believe are all intertwined providing a broad skill-set to base comprehensive representation. By tailoring his practice to focus on complementary areas of the law, Christian provides competent and confident representation in a wide variety of issues that could arise in any transactional deal. Christian’s practice is also built on the fundamentals of transparency, responsiveness, and integrity – which he provides to every client regardless of matter or size.

Christian’s business transactional practice specializes in mergers and acquisitions, private equity, corporate finance, and general corporate law matters. Christian assists clients through all phases of the M&A process, from planning and structuring, to negotiating and drafting, and through closing and post-closing matters. Christian prides his practice on the ability to offer all-encompassing services for the main street through mid-market business clients. Within the M&A spectrum, Christian also has extensive knowledge and experience with PA Liquor Law transactions, helping clients navigate the sale or purchase of an alcohol related (PLCB licensed) businesses, including restaurants, breweries, and distributors.

Christian’s commercial real estate practice includes negotiating and drafting purchase agreements, land use representation, raising capital for commercial developers and project investment, construction loan review and negotiation, and settlement/title services as a PA licensed title agent. Christian routinely represents developers of residential and commercial development, including new construction and renovations/retro-fits, from initial land acquisition through financing (via traditional lenders and private equity), entitlements, and closing.

Christian’s other main practice area is municipal and local government work. Christian represents both municipalities as well as individuals seeking relief or approvals before municipalities. This includes townships in their general governance as well as zoning hearing boards and planning commissions related to specific zoning and land development matters.

Christian grew up in York County, attending Dallastown High School and Dickinson College for undergraduate studies. After attending law school in Ohio, Christian returned home to go into practice with his father and uncle. Christian likes to spend his free time with his family, including wife Kasey, son Brady, daughter Emma and three dogs, often going for walks on his family’s farm. Christian’s other hobbies include running, golfing, pickleball, and anything active. Christian remains active with his college alumni organization as well as various other York-based charitable causes.

By tailoring his practice to focus on complementary areas of the law, Christian provides competent and confident representation in a wide variety of issues that could arise in any transactional deal. Christian’s practice is also built on the fundamentals of transparency, responsiveness, and integrity – which he provides to every client regardless of matter or size.

Christian’s business transactional practice specializes in mergers and acquisitions, private equity, corporate finance, and general corporate law matters. Christian assists clients through all phases of the M&A process, from planning and structuring, to negotiating and drafting, and through closing and post-closing matters. Christian prides his practice on the ability to offer all-encompassing services for the main street through mid-market business clients. Within the M&A spectrum, Christian also has extensive knowledge and experience with PA Liquor Law transactions, helping clients navigate the sale or purchase of an alcohol related (PLCB licensed) businesses, including restaurants, breweries, and distributors.

Christian’s commercial real estate practice includes negotiating and drafting purchase agreements, land use representation, raising capital for commercial developers and project investment, construction loan review and negotiation, and settlement/title services as a PA licensed title agent. Christian routinely represents developers of residential and commercial development, including new construction and renovations/retro-fits, from initial land acquisition through financing (via traditional lenders and private equity), entitlements, and closing.

Christian’s other main practice area is municipal and local government work. Christian represents both municipalities as well as individuals seeking relief or approvals before municipalities. This includes townships in their general governance as well as zoning hearing boards and planning commissions related to specific zoning and land development matters.

Christian grew up in York County, attending Dallastown High School and Dickinson College for undergraduate studies. After attending law school in Ohio, Christian returned home to go into practice with his father and uncle. Christian likes to spend his free time with his family, including wife Kasey, son Brady, daughter Emma and three dogs, often going for walks on his family’s farm. Christian’s other hobbies include running, golfing, pickleball, and anything active. Christian remains active with his college alumni organization as well as various other York-based charitable causes.

attorneys.name: John D. Miller Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Real Estate Lawyers in York, PA
attorneys.bio:
A native of York County, John has practiced law in south central Pennsylvania for more than three decades. His business and real estate practice includes representation of small and medium-sized businesses, family farms and real estate developers in all types of matters.

John is also a licensed title insurance agent and has extensive experience drafting and negotiating real estate documents and securing financing for real estate acquisitions. He has counseled clients on the acquisition and development of numerous agricultural, industrial and residential properties, including through tax-free like-kind exchanges. He has also represented clients securing various types of financing, including lines of credit, mortgages, asset-backed financings and revolving credit facilities, and has litigated a variety of complex real estate and commercial claims before state courts.

John also advises clients on business formation, estate planning and wealth transfer, counseling them on all stages of their business, from initial choice of entity to capitalization to planning for business succession. Through his years of experience, he has also gained a unique knowledge and understanding of multi-generational estate planning for agribusiness.

Maintaining an active municipal law practice, John serves as solicitor of Springfield Township, East Hopewell Township, and Dover Borough Zoning Hearing Board, all in York County. In that capacity he has gained particularly strong knowledge of municipal and land use law. He regularly represents businesses and developers before a variety of local and state administrative agencies.

attorneys.practice_type: Real estate Lawyers in Wexford, PA
attorneys.bio:
Katherine Miller is admitted to the Supreme Court of Pennsylvania. She received her Bachelor’s degree in Intelligence and National Security Studies from Coastal Carolina University, where she was a member of the Honors Program and Phi Sigma Pi Honor Fraternity. Katherine attended law school at Duquesne University, during which time she served as a judicial clerk to two Allegheny County judges. Following her admission to the PA State Bar, she began practicing law at a mid-size firm, primarily focusing on insurance defense litigation including general liability matters, personal injury, products liability, and subrogation.

Katherine took a two year hiatus from the practice of law after having twin daughters in 2021. She recently returned to the field and is now focusing on real estate matters including seller’s disclosure claims, transactional matters relating to the sale and purchase of real estate, landlord/tenant disputes, homeowners and condominium associations, tax sale related issues, and general civil litigation.

attorneys.name: Sara Miller
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Camp Hill, PA
attorneys.bio:
Sara joined Moore Ingram Johnson & Steele in 2024 as an Associate Attorney in the Camp Hill, PA Office.

Sara was born in Jacksonville, Florida, and was raised in Enola, Pennsylvania. She graduated from Millersville University in 2017 with a Bachelor of Arts with a double major in Sociology and Psychology and a minor in Government. Sara then attended Widener Commonwealth School of Law where she graduated from in 2020.

During her time at Widener Commonwealth School of Law, Sara held several different jobs and internships. This includes working in the Cumberland County and Adams County District Attorney’s Office, work with the Pennsylvania Association of Realtors assisting on zoning projects, and experience in the private sector involving tax collection and business law.

Prior to joining Moore Ingram Johnson & Steele, Sara served as a judicial law clerk for the Honorable Shawn C. Wagner at the Adams County Court of Common Pleas. She then became an assistant district attorney in the Adams County District Attorney’s Office where she was the lead prosecutor for crimes of domestic violence, sexual assault, and elder abuse cases. During her time as a prosecutor, Sara achieved numerous felony convictions, ranging from homicide cases down to DUI cases.

In her free time, Sara enjoys spending time with her family and friends, snuggling her two dogs, and riding her rescue horse Violet.

attorneys.name: Tobias L. Millrood
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Tobi L. Millrood, a partner, joined the firm to chair its Mass Tort Department. Millrood is a national leader in the trial bar and has 25 years of complex litigation experience, including in court-appointed leadership positions, and has won a number of major jury verdicts in complex litigation. His focus is on pharmaceutical, medical device and complex personal injury litigation.

Millrood is past president of the world's largest trial bar, the American Association for Justice (AAJ), where he completed his term in July 2021 and currently serves as Immediate Past President. As a result of his leadership within AAJ, Millrood has received numerous awards including Distinguished Service, Heavy Lifting and the prestigious President's Award in 2015.

In addition, Millrood has won many accolades and enjoys a national reputation in the field of mass torts. He has been named among the best attorneys in Pennsylvania by Super Lawyers every year since 2009, including for 2022.

Among his numerous highlights in the field of prescription drug and medical device litigation is his perseverance and success against Wyeth, Pfizer and numerous other Fortune 100 companies in the landmark Hormone Therapy litigation. In 2002, Millrood was the first in the nation to file a Hormone Therapy lawsuit and he dedicated the next twelve years to the litigation, serving as Plaintiffs' Lead Liaison Counsel for the matter in Philadelphia Common Pleas Court, presiding over thousands of cases.

He also served on the plaintiffs' executive committee In Re Prempro Products Liability, and was chair of the AAJ Hormone Therapy Litigation Group. Millrood tried four hormone therapy cases, winning jury verdicts in all four, including those of $72.6 million and $34.3 million.

He also played a major contributing role in critical appellate victories in the litigation, ranging from the state courts of Pennsylvania and Minnesota, to the U.S. Eighth Circuit. He also served in numerous court-appointed leadership positions in other pharmaceutical and medical device cases, including co-Lead counsel in In re Zofran (Ondansetron) Products Liability Litigation MDL 2657, and as co-lead counsel in In re Zimmer Nexgen Knee Products Liability Litigation, MDL 2272.

Millrood was named a co-lead counsel in Pennsylvania opioid litigation, Del. Cty. vs Purdue Pharma, et al. Working in combination with leaders both locally and nationwide, Millrood served on a leadership team that produced a settlement that can bring more than $1 billion to Pennsylvania municipalities and communities devastated by the opioid epidemic.

In addition, he has served in other court-appointed leadership positions, including the Plaintiffs' Steering Committees of In re Stryker Rejuvenate Hip Stem and ABG Modular Hip Litigation, Bergen County, N.J., and In re Consolidated Fresenius Cases in Superior Court in Massachusetts, where in both he was also appointed as Discovery Chair.

Millrood is often called upon within mass tort litigation for his strategic planning and discovery architecture. He is a frequent speaker at various seminars on the topics of Mass Tort Litigation, Expert Witnesses, Direct and Cross-Examination, Closing and Rebuttal at Trial, the Ethics of Settling Mass Tort Cases, Trial Strategies and Electronic Discovery.

Millrood has testified before the Federal Civil Rules Committee on proposed rule changes and has authored numerous comments to the Rules Committee and Subcommitee on MDL litigation. He is an invited lecturer at University of Pennsylvania Carey Law School and an invited trial team coach at the Tulane Law School. Earlier in his career, Millrood garnered several notable achievements and verdicts, including serving as co-counsel in a $22 million medical malpractice verdict, among the largest in state history at that time. Millrood is a member of the Pennsylvania Association for Justice Board of Governors and the Philadelphia Trial Lawyers Board of Directors. He is admitted to practice in Pennsylvania, New Jersey, the federal District of New Jersey, the U.S. Eastern District of Pennsylvania, the Court of Federal Claims and the U.S. Third Circuit.

Millrood earned his bachelor's degree from Tulane University and his law degree from the University of Tulsa College of Law.

attorneys.name: Kenneth Millman
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Pottsville, PA
attorneys.bio:
For almost a quarter of a century, Ken has been an advocate for those who have been victimized by the wrongful conduct of others. This has instilled in him the empathy to understand the problems that they are forced to face and the experience to utilize the legal system to help them obtain maximum compensation for their loss. Whether he is standing up to unsympathetic insurance carriers in settlement negotiations or filing lawsuits in court, Ken has successfully fought for his clients' rights and recovered tens of millions of dollars for them.

Most lawyers have little idea how tough it is to succeed in the courtroom. Like all of the other lawyers at Fanelli, Evans & Patel, Ken does. Before going into the private practice of law, Ken served as a law clerk to the Honorable John T.J. Kelly, Jr. of the Superior Court of Pennsylvania. After completing his clerkship with Judge Kelly, Ken was an Assistant District Attorney in Berks County where he served as the lead attorney representing the Commonwealth in hundreds of felony hearings and trials.

It was this experience in his formative years as a trial attorney that led Ken to concentrate his practice on personal injury litigation. Currently, Ken devotes almost 100 percent of his law practice to this type of litigation which includes but is not limited to automobile, motorcycle and trucking accidents, medical malpractice claims, wrongful death claims, and premises liability actions. Ken has also helped more than 75 survivors of sexual abuse bring claims against their perpetrators and those who enabled the perpetrators. For more than 15 years, Ken fought for both men and women who had been sexually abused by priests, overcoming many obstacles such as the statute of limitations to secure recoveries for them. Persistence, dedication and hard work are a few of the traits that helped Ken achieve results for these very deserving clients.

Ken has significant experience in both jury and non-jury trials where he has successfully obtained verdicts for his clients. For example, Ken tried a wrongful death case in the Berks County Court of Common Pleas which resulted in a verdict in excess of $46 million. Ken has also had success trying cases in Schuylkill County and Lehigh County. Ken is also a strong proponent of Alternative Dispute Resolution when it will benefit his clients. He has successfully represented clients in both arbitrations and mediations and serves as an arbitrator in Berks County.

In addition to devoting countless hours to representing his clients, Ken is very active in the Berks County legal Community. He is a former chair of the Berks County Bar Association's Civil Rules Committee. Ken was also appointed by the judges in Berks County to serve as a discovery master. Ken has been volunteering his time to help the judges resolve discovery disputes in civil cases since the inception of the discovery master program in 2015. He is also a former member of the executive board of the William Strong Chapter of the American Inns of Court. In addition to continuing to serve on the rules committee, Ken is a member of Endlich Law Club. He serves on numerous other committees and frequently presents seminars on various legal topics to other lawyers.

Ken graduated from Franklin & Marshall College in 1991 where he played both football and baseball. He continued his education at the Widener University School of Law and graduated cum laude in 1994. In law school, Ken distinguished himself as the winner of the American Juris Prudence Award and was the recipient of several other academic honors.

Ken is very involved in the local community. He and his wife raised their two sons in Exeter Township. An avid sports enthusiast, Ken coached youth sports in both the City of Reading and Exeter Township for more than 15 years. From 2011 through 2017, Ken was a member of the Exeter Community Library Board of Trustees and served as its President for three of those years. Ken's roots in Berks County run deep.

attorneys.name: Mark E. Milsop
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
Born in Pittsburgh, PA in 1967, Mark E. Milsop is a 1989 graduate of Pennsylvania State University, where he earned his bachelor's degree in economics with a minor in speech communication. He then attended Duquesne University School of Law in 1992, where he earned his Juris Doctor and graduated with honors. During law school, Mr. Milsop was a member of the Law Review and Appellate Moot Court Society. He also interned with the Honorable Ralph J. Cappy of the Pennsylvania Supreme Court. Attorney Milsop knew early on that he wanted to be a courtroom attorney. He wanted to do work that was important, helpful and that makes a difference in people's lives. Mr. Milsop believes the courtroom is a place where he can stand up for people.

Attorney Milsop joined Berger and Green, P.C. in 2007, where he proudly represents injured accident victims in personal injury claims including: car accidents, burn injuries, dog bites, slip and fall incidents, and wrongful death claims. Attorney Milsop has 21 years of experience. He believes in building trust with his clients, letting them know up front what the strengths and weaknesses of their case are, and how he plans to handle them. He understands that a serious injury can have a devastating impact on his client's life. This compels attorney Milsop to work hard to make a recovery for his clients.

Attorney Milsop serves on numerous professional organizations including the Board of Governors of the Western Pennsylvania Trial Lawyers Association (WPTLA), the Local Rules Committee of the Allegheny County Bar Association (ACBA). He is also an elected member of the Academy of Trial Lawyers of Allegheny County (ATLAC), where he was appointed to the membership committee. Mr. Milsop is a former member of the Pennsylvania Association for Justice's Board of Governors and currently serves as Chair of PAJ's Amicus Curiae Committee. He is also a board member and former President of the St. Thomas More Society (Catholic Lawyers). From 2011-2015 Attorney Milsop was named as a Pennsylvania Super Lawyer. These lawyers represent the top five percent of all lawyers in Pennsylvania in peer recognition and professional achievement.

Attorney Milsop has also written on the law, having served as a co-author of the Pennsylvania Automobile Litigation: Guideline and Forms for the Trial Lawyer, 3rd Edition. He also authors a regular Column -"By The Rules"- for WPTLA's quarterly publication.

Mr. Milsop is licensed to practice in all Pennsylvania Courts as well as the United States District Court for the Western District of Pennsylvania and the United States Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit.

Outside of the courtroom, Mr. Milsop likes to stay active in the legal community, writing on the law and advocating for laws that protect the rights of injured accident victims.

Mr. Milsop is proud to serve personal injury victims as an attorney with Berger and Green. He believes that it is important to focus on the fact that his clients have been victims of the carelessness of others. Attorney Milsop feels it is his role to see that his clients are treated fairly by the civil justice system.

Mark E. Milsop

attorneys.name: Trudy Marietta Mintz
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Office of Trudy A. Marietta Mintz
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Camp Hill, PA
attorneys.bio:
Trudy Marietta Mintz is an attorney licensed in Pennsylvania and Maryland. Having attended the University of Baltimore for both her undergraduate and law degree, she was a proud recipient of the Early Entry Jurisprudence scholarship and graduated with high honors. Ms. Marietta Mintz has been a practicing attorney since 2007.

Ms. Marietta Mintz focuses her practice on Family Law including the areas of Grandparents’ Rights, Fathers’ Rights, and other complex situations. She is aware that every family has their unique challenges and is committed to the long-term success of child custody and divorce arrangements. Her goal is to leave each client with a workable plan that will carry the family into a more positive future with the best interest of the child protected.

Ms. Marietta Mintz also practices Criminal Law and prides herself on obtaining just results for her clients. Especially in the area of DUI, she is keenly aware of the impact on the lives of her clients following an arrest. Any arrest is stressful and she works to reduce that stress while providing a vigorous defense for her client.

Ms. Marietta Mintz prides herself on developing a personal relationship with her clients. She fully realizes that they are coming to her at some of the most difficult times of their lives and is honored to become a trusted counselor to them.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Reading, PA
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Paul S. Missan completed his undergraduate diploma at Temple University in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania and received his law degree at Villanova University School of Law.

Upon graduation from Law School, Attorney Missan established a reputation as a tough Prosecutor in the Bronx District Attorney's Office in New York City.

For six years Mr. Missan prosecuted all forms of crimes including narcotic cases, homicide, assaults, theft, drunk driving, etc. After working in the Narcotics Bureau in the Bronx District Attorney's Office, Attorney Missan was recruited to bring his aggressive no-nonsense court skills to the District Attorney's Office in Reading in Berks County, Pennsylvania, where he successfully prosecuted rape, murder, and other crimes as Chief of Child Abuse Unit in the Berks County District Attorney's Office.

Since 1997 Mr. Missan has been available to help those being investigated or charged in criminal matters in Berks County.

attorneys.name: Hannah J. Molitoris
attorneys.practice_type: Brain Injuries Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Hannah J. Molitoris is an attorney at the Philadelphia office with a passion for fighting for her clients. Prior to joining Morgan & Morgan, Ms. Molitoris worked as a public defender representing hundreds of clients in Philadelphia Municipal Court and the Court of Common Pleas.

Ms. Molitoris graduated cum laude from Susquehanna University in 2012 with a Bachelor's degree in Political Science and Communications. She was a member of the Order of Omega Leadership Honor Society, Lambda Pi Eta Political Science Honor Society, and received Departmental Honors in Political Science.

In 2016, she received her Juris Doctor from the Thomas R. Kline School of Law at Drexel University. During law school, Ms. Molitoris was a member of the Student Bar Association, mock trial team, moot court team, and participated in the criminal law clinic. She volunteered with the Philadelphia Lawyers for Social Equity and M.E.N.T.O.R. program.

While at Kline Law, Ms. Molitoris won several academic awards including Dean's List and three CALI Excellence for the Future Awards for best student performances in Appellate Advocacy, Improvisation for Lawyers, and Advanced Trial Advocacy: Criminal Law. She also received the Kline and Specter Award for Trial Advocacy.

Ms. Molitoris competed nationally in both mock trial and moot court competitions. As a member of the mock trial team, she was a regional champion in the Texas Young Lawyers National Trial Competition and a quarterfinalist in the Buffalo Niagara Trial Competition.

Currently, Ms. Molitoris is an adjunct professor at the Kline School of Law. When Ms. Molitoris is not prepping for trial, she enjoys spending time with her fiancé and her dog Lincoln.

Ms. Molitoris is admitted to practice law in Pennsylvania and New Jersey.

attorneys.name: Edward A. Monsky
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Scranton, PA
attorneys.bio:
Joining Munley Law Personal Injury Attorneys in 2020, Ed Monsky brings over 35 years of experience representing people and businesses in motor vehicle accidents, premises liability, products liability, professional liability, and workers’ compensation claims throughout Northeastern Pennsylvania. Currently, he focuses on pre-litigation and workers’ compensation cases.

At the beginning of his illustrious legal career, Ed served as a law clerk for the Honorable Forrest Schaeffer of the Berks County Court of Common Pleas. Since then, he has participated in 25 jury trials and hundreds of arbitration/ administrative hearings throughout Northeast and Central Pennsylvania and federal courts. Additionally, Ed has expertise in Social Security disability claims, preparing wills, powers of attorney, and living wills, and representing clients who serve as the personal representative of estates.

Originally from Scranton, Pennsylvania, Ed earned a B.A. from Haverford College, his M.A. from the University of Pennsylvania, and his J.D. from Washington University School of Law. Ed is an active community member and has served as President of Lackawanna Pro Bono, an organization that provides legal services in civil matters to indigent clients, and a board member of the Lackawanna Bar Association.

attorneys.name: Jeffrey D. Monzo
attorneys.practice_type: Personal injury Lawyers in Greensburg, PA
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Jeffrey D. Monzo concentrates his practice in the areas of Criminal Litigation, Personal Injury Litigation, and Family Law.

Mr. Monzo has over 25 years of experience in litigation and has represented clients in matters including driving under the influence, vehicular homicide, murder, and wrongful death. A former assistant public defender, he has participated in some of the most widely publicized trials in Western Pennsylvania. Mr. Monzo has represented Personal Injury clients who have received settlements of over 1 million dollars.

Mr. Monzo currently serves as the Solicitor for the Westmoreland County Coroner's Office, a position he has held since 2002.

Mr. Monzo was voted by his peers as a "Rising Star" in both 2005 and 2006 by Super Lawyers, a recognition given to those under the age of 40 who exhibit legal excellence. Since 2008, and every year thereafter, he has been named to the Best Lawyers in America for excellence in Criminal litigation. In 2013, he was selected as a member of the Westmoreland Academy of Trial Lawyers for his excellence in Criminal and Civil litigation. Since 2014, Mr. Monzo has been named one of the top 100 DUI Attorneys in Pennsylvania and one of the Best Attorneys in Pittsburgh.

Mr. Monzo is the former president of the board of Lawyers Abstract, a real estate title company. He has also served as president of the board of the Mental Health Association of Westmoreland County and as president of the board of the Maxwell Athletic Association.

Mr. Monzo is a member of the Westmoreland Academy of Trial Lawyers, the Westmoreland Bar Association, the Pennsylvania Bar Association, and the Ned J. Nakles Inns of Court.

He previously served as an adjunct faculty member at Seton Hill University, where he taught Labor Law and Business Law. He also lectured at Seton Hill University on legal issues for students preparing to take the Certified Public Accounting exam.

Mr. Monzo received his B.A. from Dickinson College in 1989 and his J.D. from Ohio Northern University in 1992, where he was the Lead Articles Editor of the Law Review.

Mr. Monzo and his wife, Lisa, have two children.

attorneys.name: Francis Moritz
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Bala Cynwyd, PA
attorneys.bio:
Francis “Fritz” Moritz received his Doctor of Jurisprudence from Seton Hall University School of Law. He received his Bachelor of Arts from La Salle University. While in law school, he was a visiting student at Louisiana State University School of Law. In addition, he served as a law clerk for the Judges of Workers’ Compensation.

Mr. Moritz defends employers, insurance carriers, and third-party administrators in Pennsylvania and New Jersey workers’ compensation claims. His clients include national corporations and small, locally owned businesses, in the hospitality, commercial transportation and trucking, manufacturing, and retail industries, among others.

Since being admitted to the bar, Fritz has practiced in the area of workers’ compensation. Prior to joining Berman Voss, Fritz worked for multiple regional law firms. He also founded and managed The Moritz Law Group, where he defended employers and insurance carriers in workers’ compensation claims.

Over his legal career, Fritz has handled countless cases at the trial court level and successfully argued appeals before the Workers’ Compensation Appeal Board and the Commonwealth Court of Pennsylvania. Fritz was selected as a Pennsylvania Super Lawyer in 2012 and again in 2013. Prior to that, he was selected as a Pennsylvania Super Lawyer Rising Star.

attorneys.bio:
Michael C. Morrone has been a member of the Pennsylvania Bar since 1995. Mike joined the firm of Campana, Campana & Lovecchio, a predecessor firm to the current firm, that same year.

Mike’s practice is divided between criminal defense work and domestic relations. Mike as developed an outstanding reputation in the domestic relations field having had considerable success in both child custody cases as well as divorce actions. Mike established the domestic relations practice when he became an associate. He continues to expand the practice and covers clients throughout central Pennsylvania in domestic relations disputes.

Mike credits much of his success in the domestic relations courtrooms with his experience as a criminal defense attorney. He has practiced criminal defense work for over 20 years. Mike has appeared throughout the courts in central Pennsylvania representing clients in cases ranging from underage drinking, drug related offenses and serious felonies.

Mike is a member of the Federal Criminal Defense Criminal Justice Act Panel for the Middle District of Pennsylvania.
