attorneys.name: John F. Mullen
attorneys.practice_type: Data Privacy & Network Security Lawyers in Devon, PA
attorneys.bio:
John is regarded as an authority on privacy and data security issues by the majority of the largest insurers in the U.S.

As a natural outgrowth of his earlier career in medical data computer systems (as well as substantial experience in mass tort), John developed, and continues to help the insurance industry develop, the cyber market. He devotes a significant portion of his practice to evaluating data privacy risks, regulations, responses and resolutions. He manages first- and third-party risks arising in the world of privacy and data security for insureds, brokers, risk managers, underwriters, product specialists and professional claims personnel.

John serves as a data breach coach/advisor, providing consultation services to insureds (both pre- and post-breach events) addressing data breach events, including computer forensics, notifications, call centers, public relations, crisis communications, fraud consultation, credit monitoring and identity restoration.

In his previous career, John worked in New York City for a leading provider of computer-based data information processing systems and associated services to the healthcare industry in North America and Europe. After reviewing the client's existing data collection and flow, he proposed, sold and helped implement healthcare data processing system solutions that, even then, included cloud computing options. His early interest in healthcare-related technology and data processing was the starting point for his career focus in privacy and data security.

An enthusiastic speaker, John is frequently invited by organizations and brokers to discuss risks related to privacy and data security, breaches, cyber liability and network risks.

Beyond privacy and data security, John handles a variety of complex, high-value liability issues involving mass/toxic/environmental and pollution-related torts. He has decades of national experience litigating and resolving high-exposure mass tort matters on behalf of insureds and insurers in issues involving food contamination, repetitive stress disorders, isocyanides, metal working fluids, formaldehyde, benzene, mold, pharmaceuticals and others.

He is frequently retained in matters where the original/underlying defense counsel is challenged to the point that the insurance company requires outside assistance to reposition the disputes and relative positions of the parties. In such cases, John reorients the cases, the parties and the litigation into a much more favorable position with regard to the insured and the insurer.

attorneys.name: Sergio C. Muniz Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Eagleville, PA
attorneys.bio:
Sergio C. Muñiz, Jr., is an associate in the Melbourne, Florida office. He is a 1994 graduate of the United States Air Force Academy and a 2000 graduate of The University of Texas School of Law. He is admitted to the Texas and Florida Bars, and admitted to practice in a number of Federal Courts. Mr. Muñiz has served as an Air Force JAG Officer, focusing on government contracts and contractor disputes. He has experience in a wide variety of matters including insurance coverage, surety and fidelity litigation, government contract litigation under the Contract Disputes Act, real estate title defense and litigation, insurance defense and other commercial litigation matters. Mr. Muñiz has also experience representing creditors in bankruptcy court proceedings.

Mr. Muñiz has focused his practice representing insurance companies in insurance coverage litigation and representing sureties in construction payment and performance bond litigation involving both small and large projects, public and private contracts. As a derivative of surety and fidelity litigation, he also has experience in construction litigation. He also has an extensive background in federal government claims and the litigation of disputes before various agencies dealing with contract appeals. In addition to pursuing contractor claims and appeals in the U.S. Court of Federal Claims and Agency Board of Contract Appeals, he can also defend contractors against government claims.

He is admitted to the Texas and Florida Bars, and admitted to practice in a number of Federal Courts. Mr. Muñiz has served as an Air Force JAG Officer, focusing on government contracts and contractor disputes. He has experience in a wide variety of matters including insurance coverage, surety and fidelity litigation, government contract litigation under the Contract Disputes Act, real estate title defense and litigation, insurance defense and other commercial litigation matters. Mr. Muñiz has also experience representing creditors in bankruptcy court proceedings.

Mr. Muñiz has focused his practice representing insurance companies in insurance coverage litigation and representing sureties in construction payment and performance bond litigation involving both small and large projects, public and private contracts. As a derivative of surety and fidelity litigation, he also has experience in construction litigation. He also has an extensive background in federal government claims and the litigation of disputes before various agencies dealing with contract appeals. In addition to pursuing contractor claims and appeals in the U.S. Court of Federal Claims and Agency Board of Contract Appeals, he can also defend contractors against government claims.

attorneys.name: Daniel W. Munley
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Scranton, PA
attorneys.bio:
Daniel W. Munley is an award-winning personal injury lawyer and a champion of plaintiffs’ rights. For decades, Dan has tirelessly fought to win millions for injured victims of tragic accidents and their families. While Dan handles a range of complex personal injury cases, he is widely regarded as a national leader in traumatic brain injury and tractor-trailer accident litigation. Through hard work and unrelenting commitment to his clients, he has won numerous multimillion-dollar verdicts and settlements. Just recently, Dan strategically negotiated a record-setting $26 million settlement for a truck accident victim.

A seasoned truck accident lawyer, Daniel served as Chairperson of the American Association for Justice’s Trucking Litigation Group from 2011-2012, and currently serves on the executive board for that group. In 2020, he received the Robert W. Munley Champion of Justice Award (previously the Chairman’s Award) from the American Association for Justice Trucking Litigation Group. He has been certified by the Association of Interstate Trucking Lawyers of America, and board-certified in Truck Accident Law and Civil Trial Practice by the National Board of Trial Advocacy.

Daniel has been named among the Top 100 Trial Lawyers in Pennsylvania, the Trucking Trial Lawyers Top Ten, and has been listed in the Best Lawyers in America and Pennsylvania Super Lawyers. He was selected “Lawyer of the Year: Product Liability– Plaintiffs” for the Allentown Metro Area in 2020 by Best Lawyers. That same year, he was one of only two lawyers in the region named to the Lawdragon 500 Leading Plaintiffs’ Lawyers. He has earned an AV-Preeminent rating and a Platinum-Level Client Champion designation from Martindale-Hubbell.

In addition to his major tractor-trailer crash victories, Dan regularly presents cutting-edge truck accident trial techniques at conferences around the country.

attorneys.bio:
Caroline Munley is a top-rated personal injury lawyer and a fierce guardian of victims’ rights. As Munley Law Personal Injury Attorneys’s managing partner, Caroline has won millions of dollars for car accident, commercial truck crash, and workplace injury victims.

She is widely recognized as an impassioned advocate and tenacious courtroom lawyer, and has been named a Pennsylvania Super Lawyer since 2022. Since 2018, Caroline has been listed among the Best Lawyers in America for Personal Injury Litigation-Plaintiffs and Workers’ Compensation Law-Claimants for Northeastern Pennsylvania. She was also honored to be named to the lists of Top 25 Women Trial Lawyers in PA, and Multi-Million Dollar Advocates. She was named as one of the Top 25 Medical Malpractice Trial Lawyers in Pennsylvania by the Medical Malpractice Trial Lawyers Association.

Caroline is certified as a specialist in the practice of workers’ compensation law by the Pennsylvania Bar Association’s Section on Workers’ Compensation Law as authorized by the Pennsylvania Supreme Court.

Caroline’s father, the late Robert W. Munley, instilled her commitment to fighting for justice for all and inspired Caroline to become a lawyer. In addition to her major car and truck accident case victories, Caroline works tirelessly to better the local communities of northeast Pennsylvania. She serves as the chair of the Board of Trustees for the Everhart Museum in Scranton, Pennsylvania, and is an active board member for the Women’s Resource Center of Northeastern Pennsylvania.

attorneys.name: Marion K. Munley
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Scranton, PA
attorneys.bio:
Marion Munley is a champion of the civil justice system and the rights of victims—particularly those injured in trucking crashes and by products in the marketplace. She is known for her compassionate approach to representing the catastrophically injured and her tireless devotion to her clients and their families. Marion treats each client like a member of her family. Through her advocacy, she has won many multimillion dollar recoveries for her clients including one of the largest trucking accident settlements in history.

Widely recognized as one of the state’s most prominent and widely respected truck accident lawyers, Marion is Triple Board Certified by the National Board of Trial Advocacy in Civil Trial, Civil Practice, and Truck Law. Marion has earned an AV-Preeminent designation from Martindale-Hubbell, the industry’s highest ethical and client satisfaction rating.

A leader in the legal community, Marion is an active member of the American Association for Justice (AAJ) and is currently the AAJ Secretary. She was the first woman to become Chair of the AAJ Trucking Litigation Group in 2018 and is a past chair of the AAJ Women Trial Lawyers Caucus. Marion has also served as President of the Melvin M. Belli Society. Marion is the second woman in Pennsylvania to become Board Certified as a Civil Trial Advocate by the National Board of Trial Advocacy. Among her other professional affiliations are the American Board of Trial Advocates, the International Society of Barristers, and the Summit Council, an exclusive group of today’s top civil justice attorneys committed to the highest levels of trial advocacy, to obtaining justice for individuals and families who have been hurt by corporate wrongdoing, and to the protection of the civil justice system.

During her career, Marion has received some of the highest honors a lawyer can receive. Listed in The Best Lawyers in America® since 2012, Marion has been named the 2024 “Lawyer of the Year” for Product Liability Litigation – Plaintiffs in Northeastern Pennsylvania. Marion has also been named to the Top 10 Pennsylvania Super Lawyers list for 2023 and has been listed in Pennsylvania Super Lawyers for the last 18 years. She has been consistently recognized as one of the “Top 50 Women Lawyers in Pennsylvania” in Super Lawyers Magazine. A graduate of Temple University School of Law, Marion received her undergraduate degree from the University of Scranton.

attorneys.name: Craig Murphey
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury - General Lawyers in Erie, PA
attorneys.bio:
Craig Murphey has been a trial lawyer for over 25 years. Before joining our team, Craig was a partner in one of Erie's largest law firms, where he concentrated his practice on defending personal injury cases - especially car, truck and motorcycle accident lawsuits involving deaths or catastrophic injuries.

Over the years, Craig has also represented and advised insurance carriers in numerous types of claims involving automobile, homeowner's, or commercial general liability policies. He has also handled many cases that have shaped Pennsylvania auto insurance law, especially in the arena of uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage.

Craig also has much experience with insurance bad faith cases. He has represented and counseled both insurance companies and policyholders in bad faith claims, ever since the Pennsylvania bad faith claim handling statute was enacted in 1990.

With Purchase George & Murphey, P.C., Craig will use his education and experience to help accident victims, policyholders and other insureds in all types of personal injury, property damage, bad faith and other insurance claims. In addition, he will protect the interests of those suffering from injury or medical mistakes and represent companies and individuals in a wide variety of business disputes.

Craig has been honored by his peers and clients as an outstanding lawyer and leader. He is currently the President of the Erie County Bar Association. He was formerly President of the Pennsylvania Defense Institute, an organization comprised of leading insurance defense lawyers and insurance claim executives.

He has been selected for inclusion in The Best Lawyers in America© every year since 2012 and as a Pennsylvania Super Lawyer every year since 2011. The Pennsylvania Super Lawyers designation is awarded to only the top 5% of all Pennsylvania attorneys following a selection process that includes peer nominations, an evaluation of professional achievement, and independent research of the candidates. Craig has been recognized by The Best Lawyers in America© as the 2017 Pittsburgh region "Lawyer of the Year" for Personal Injury-Defense. This is quite an honor -- Best Lawyers© honors only one lawyer in each practice area and region as "Lawyer of the Year."

attorneys.bio:
Over 25 years representing developers, land owners, telecommunications companies and other applicants in every phase of obtaining project approvals from Municipal, County, State and Federal agencies.

My public sector expertise developed strong relationships with elected and appointed officials, and brings a practical approach to cut through “red tape” and think “outside the box” to solve complicated issues to obtain project approvals.

Peer Talk/Review:

Land Use litigation before Pennsylvania agencies and courts.

Development of shopping centers, office and industrial buildings, retail stores, restaurants, mixed-use developments and hospitals.

Development of every form of residential subdivision from single family, town house, multi-family, apartment and mixed-use developments.

attorneys.name: Patrick W. Murray Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Attorney Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
PATRICK W. MURRAY - PITTSBURGH INJURY ATTORNEY

Attorney Patrick W. Murray is one of the founding partners of the law firm of SMT Legal. He received his B.A. in 2000 from Point Park University and his J.D. in 2003 from Duquesne University. While attending Duquesne University School of Law, he served as Associate Comment Editor of the Law Review and represented the University in trial and A.D.R. competitions. Also while attending Duquesne University School of Law, Mr. Murray worked for Dickie, McCamey & Chilcote, P.C. and continued to work with the firm after receiving his degree. In 2006, Attorney Murray joined Klett, Rooney, Lieber and Schorling, P.C. before that firm merged to form Buchanan, Ingersoll & Rooney, P.C. Super Lawyers Magazine has also named Mr. Murray a Pennsylvania Super Lawyer Rising Star.

Attorney Murray initially concentrated his practice in the area of civil litigation defense for transportation companies which included major trucking and railroad companies. Mr. Murray expanded his practice to include a variety of areas within civil defense including, but not limited to: premises liability, motor vehicle liability, employment law, family law, workers' compensation, real estate disputes and transactions, and medical and nursing home litigation.

Attorney Murray is a member of the Allegheny County Bar Association and American Bar Association. Additionally, Mr. Murray is a Member of the Million Dollar Advocates Forum for Top Trial Lawyers in America as well as a President's Club Member of the Western Pennsylvania Trial Lawyers Association. He has been admitted to practice before the Supreme Court of Pennsylvania, United States Third Circuit Court of Appeals, United States District Court for the Western District of Pennsylvania and United States District Court for the Middle District of Pennsylvania. In addition to Pennsylvania, Attorney Murray has also practiced law in Ohio. Attorney Murray has successfully assisted his clients in the negotiation of settlements in cases involving millions of dollars in dispute, has secured dismissals for a number of clients and represented clients in appellate matters arguing before the Third Circuit Court of Appeals and Pennsylvania Appellate Courts.

Representing injured people, Mr. Murray has secured favorable jury and non-jury verdicts on behalf of clients to compensate them for their injuries and out of pocket expenses. Additionally, Mr. Murray has successfully assisted his clients in the negotiation of settlements in cases involving severe and catastrophic injuries. However, Mr. Murray's experience goes beyond representation of injured people and also includes representation of Estates in Wrongful Death and Survival actions.

Beyond his civil litigation accomplishments, attorney Murray has represented clients through real estate transactions and closings, child custody disputes and has even been successful in assisting non-parental clients and fathers obtain primary custody. In addition to being an attorney with real estate experience, Mr. Murray is also a founding member of 24/7 Settlement Services, LLC which provides both residential and commercial real estate closing services in the area.

Attorney Murray is also an adjunct professor at Duquesne University School of Law, is Blackboard Certified and has been involved with teaching at several local universities. He lives in the north Hills area of Pittsburgh with his wife and two children.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
Since joining Gentile, Horoho & Avalli in 2005, Rebecca Myers has focused her practice exclusively on family law. In addition to practicing in all aspects of domestic relations litigation, Ms. Myers has completed training as a parent coordinator and is competing training in mediation.

Attorney Myers' interest in family law is long standing and she devoted much of her studies in law school at the University of Pittsburgh to this area of practice. Additionally, her undergraduate training in psychology has proven helpful in assisting her clients through the difficult, often emotionally draining family court system. In addition to her family law litigation practice, Ms. Myers is also a certified mediator in divorce and family conflicts by the Association for Conflict Resolution.

She is trained in mediation and collaborative law and chairs the firm’s collaborative law group. Additionally, Ms. Myers is a member of the Collaborative Law Association of Southwestern Pennsylvania, where she serves as membership chair. She is also a member of the Collaborative Law section of the Allegheny County Bar Association.

Upon graduation from law school, she was awarded the American Association of Matrimonial Lawyers award for excellence in the area of family law. Additionally, Attorney Myers was named a Super Lawyer Rising Star in 2010, 2013 and 2014.

She is a member of the Allegheny County Bar Association and the Pennsylvania Bar Association. Ms. Myers is a member of the Family Law Section and the Young Lawyers Divisions of the local and state bar associations.

Mr. Myers is a founding shareholder of MyersLafferty Law Offices. After graduating summa cum laude from Clarion University in 1980, he attended the University of Pennsylvania School of Law, one of America's preeminent Ivy League law schools. At Penn, he helped found the Law School's Journal of Comparative Business and Capital Market Law. attorneys.name: Brian Patrick Bronson
attorneys.practice_type: Long-Term Disability Lawyers in Greensburg, PA
attorneys.bio:
Brian Patrick Bronson is an associate of the firm and concentrates his practice in the areas of Social Security Disability, ERISA, Disability Insurance (Long-Term and Short-Term Disability Claims), Veterans disability, and criminal defense.

Mr. Bronson is a lifelong resident of Unity Township and currently resides in East High Acres with his wife, Liznelia, his two sons, Bradan Padraic and Brody Quinn, and a daughter, Brooklyn. Brian’s wife Liz, is a graduate of Duquesne University with degrees in Biochemistry and Nursing. She is currently employed as a Registered Nurse with the Veteran’s Administration and works at the VA hospital located in Oakland at University Drive. Brian is a member of the National Rifle Association and is an avid hunter and outdoorsman.

Brian is the son of two educator parents, who both served long and distinguished careers with the Greater Latrobe School District and the Westmoreland Intermediate Unit #7. He is a graduate of Greater Latrobe High School and was twice selected as an All-Conference Football Player, with a First Team All-Quad South Selection in 1994. Mr. Bronson also served as the President of the Pennsylvania Junior Classical League from 1993-1994. He was a member of the Westmoreland Youth Symphony, where he was a violinist and was selected for the All-District Orchestra on two separate occasions. Mr. Bronson also received the honor of being selected to play in a televised Side-by-Side concert with the Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra under the direction of the renowned Lorin Maazel.

Mr. Bronson received his B.S. from Bucknell University in Lewisburg, Pennsylvania in 1999, where he majored in Business Administration, and his law degree from the Duquesne University School of Law (Cum Laude) in 2002. Mr. Bronson is admitted to practice in Pennsylvania, the Federal District Court for the Western District of Pennsylvania, and the U.S. Third Circuit Court of Appeals.

While at Bucknell University, Mr. Bronson was a three-time letter winner on the Varsity Football Team participating in the NCAA-Division 1-AA Patriot League. He was twice selected as the Player of the Game for his performances against Cornell University and Towson University. In 1998, Mr. Bronson received the George Rieu Award given to the most outstanding linebacker or defensive lineman. Mr. Bronson was also a member of the Sigma Chi Fraternity-Kappa Chapter where he served as the Sargeant of Arms, or Kustos.

While at Duquesne Law School, Mr. Bronson earned the C.A.L.I. Award in the subject of Criminal Law. He also served as a member of the Duquesne Law Review where he authored 2 published articles: The California Open Primary Act Unconstitutionally Burdens Political Parties’ Associational Rights: California Democratic Party v. Jones, 39 Duq. Law. Rev. 845 (Summer 2001); and Pennsylvania’s Common Law Right to Privacy Inadequately Protects the Rights of Individual Workers’ Compensation Claimant from the Harassment Caused by Video Surveillance. 40 Duq. Law. Rev. 523 (Spring 2002).

Mr. Bronson is a member of the Westmoreland County and Pennsylvania Bar Associations, the National Organization of Social Security Claimants’ Representatives (NOSSCR), and the Ned J. Nakles American Inn of Court. Mr. Bronson has attended the American Conference Institute’s National Forum on Litigating Disability Insurance Claims and the annual NOSSCR national conventions. Mr. Bronson also serves on the board of directors of Laurel Legal Services, Inc., an organization that provides free civil representation to low-income citizens. Mr. Bronson is also a part of Operation Standby, which assists the JAG Corps in providing representation to Armed Services personnel.

Brian has been selected as a Rising Star by the PA SuperLawyers magazine in 2010, 2011, and 2012.

attorneys.name: Joyce Novotny
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Greensburg, PA
attorneys.bio:
Joyce Novotny-Prettiman is an associate at the firm. Joyce is a member of the American, Pennsylvania and Westmoreland Bar Associations. After serving as the president of the Westmoreland Bar Association for one year, she currently acts as immediate past president of that organization. She also participates in the following committees of the Westmoreland Bar Association: Civil Litigation and Lawyers Assistance Committee (chair). She is also a member of the Ned J. Nakles American Inn of Court and serves as the immediate past president for the Inn. She has been elected to the Westmoreland Academy of Trial Lawyers and is a member of the Pennsylvania Association for Justice and the Western Pennsylvania Trial Lawyers Association. She is also a member of the Million Dollar Advocates Forum. In regard to alternative dispute resolution matters, she has had mediation training and has been trained in the collaborative law process.

Ms. Novotny-Prettiman earned her B.A. in 1997 from Seton Hill College (summa cum laude) and her law degree from Duquesne University in 2000. She began practicing with the firm after her admission to the practice of law and is currently active in the areas of plaintiff personal injury litigation, long-term disability and general civil litigation.

Ms. Novotny-Prettiman was plaintiff's counsel in the case of Gallagher v. GEICO decided by the Pennsylvania Supreme Court in January 2019 which invalidates the "household exclusion" regularly used by auto insurance carriers to deny underinsured motorist benefits.

Joyce has a unique legal background. She was a legal secretary before obtaining her paralegal certification from St. Vincent College in 1989, and worked in the capacity of legal assistant until her admission into law school. While attending law school, Ms. Novotny-Prettiman worked as a law clerk at QuatriniRafferty.

She is also active in the community and volunteers as a member of the parish council and as a lector at St. Benedict Church. She is a member of the board of directors for Laurel Faith in Action which is devoted to helping residents in the communities of Latrobe, Derry, and Ligonier who are over 60 remain independent in their own homes, with dignity (www.laurelfia.org). She was a volunteer for CASA of Westmoreland from 2010 through 2020 which is an agency that works to give children a voice in the court system when circumstances have placed that child in protective services. She has also been appointed to the Westmoreland County Parks and Recreation Citizens Advisory Board.

A lifelong resident of Unity Township, Joyce currently resides in the Latrobe-Greensburg area with her husband, Daniel. She enjoys spending her free time with her family and friends and loves to practice yoga and to go for a jog to enjoy the outdoors. Summer is her favorite season and she has enjoyed jet skiing and boating for years which pastime grows from the many Sundays her father took her and her sister for boating adventures.

attorneys.name: Feranmi Olugbenga
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Feranmi Olugbenga-Jebutu joined Wilbraham, Lawler, & Buba as an associate attorney in 2025.

In 2018, Ms. Olugbenga-Jebutu graduated from Drexel University with a Bachelor of Science in Psychology and earned a certificate of Intermediate Proficiency in Korean. At Drexel, she was a member of the Pennoni Honors College and received the A.J. Drexel Scholarship.

In 2023, Ms. Olugbenga-Jebutu graduated from Temple University, Beasley School of Law, where she was the recipient of the Beasley Scholarship. While at Temple, she served as a Legal Research and Writing Teaching Assistant for Temple’s International Law students at both Temple’s Main and Shanghai campuses. Furthermore, she was actively involved in student organizations serving as Vice President, Secretary and Treasurer for Temple’s First-Generation Owls, as well as Treasurer of Temple’s International Law Society. Additionally, she interned at Philadelphia Legal Assistance (PLA), assisting indigent homeowners at risk of losing their homes.

In her last year of law school, Ms. Olugbenga-Jebutu was selected as a Temple Global Scholar for Japan. While studying abroad in Japan, Ms. Olugbenga-Jebutu met with both international and domestic attorneys and visited the Japanese Supreme Court, where she engaged in discussion with the Justices.

In her spare time, Ms. Olugbenga-Jebutu enjoys reading, volunteering, watching foreign films and traveling.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Beasley Scholarship

A.J. Drexel Scholarship

attorneys.name: Harry A. Dorian Jr. (1953
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Bensalem, PA
attorneys.bio:
Harry A. Dorian, Jr. has been practicing law since 1978. He is a graduate of Ohio Northern University School of Law, where he was co-editor of the Ohio Northern University Law Review. In 1975, he graduated with honors from Penn State University with a BA degree in English. He grew up in Montgomery County, graduating from Lower Merion High School in 1971. He was awarded the rank of Eagle Scout in 1970.

Mr. Dorian is a senior managing partner of the firm of Dorian, Goldstein, Wisniewski & Orchinik, P.C. where, for the past 35 years, he has concentrated his practice in the areas of medical malpractice, nursing home negligence, motor vehicle accidents, product liability and other cases involving serious injury or death.

For more than twenty years, he has consistently received the highest possible peer-review rating available ("AV Preeminent") from Martindale-Hubbell for maintaining the highest standards of professional ethics and legal ability. This rating is based upon an extensive peer-review survey of practicing attorneys and judges.

Also, he was recently again named "Pennsylvania Super Lawyer" by Philadelphia Magazine and Law and Politics, based upon a confidential survey of over 39,000 attorneys in Pennsylvania. Only 4% of attorneys in Pennsylvania are awarded the status of a "Pennsylvania Super Lawyer". He has also consistently obtained a rating of "Superb" by Avvo (receiving a perfect 10.0 score), and The National Association of Trial Lawyers has named him one of the "Top 100 Trial Lawyers in Pennsylvania".

He has obtained numerous multi-million dollar recoveries in various types of negligence cases, such as motor vehicle accidents, slip and falls, medical malpractice, nursing home neglect/abuse, dog attacks, premises defects and product liability.

Mr. Dorian has also been appointed a Special Judge Pro Tempore and Settlement Master by the Philadelphia Court of Common Pleas in its Civil Case Management Program. He is also a frequent Arbitrator for the Bucks County Court of Common Pleas.

Mr. Dorian has given lectures to physicians and surgeons on issues related to patient safety and medical malpractice, and he has taught other attorneys at legal seminars involving various areas of the law. Recently, he spoke to hundreds of dentists and dental professionals about oral cancer and dental malpractice at Continuing Dental Education seminars at the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor, and the Temple University School of Dentistry in Philadelphia.

Mr. Dorian has tried numerous cases in both state and federal court in Pennsylvania. He has argued appeals before the Pennsylvania Supreme Court, Pennsylvania Superior Court and the Commonwealth Court of Pennsylvania. He is a long-time member of the American Association for Justice, Pennsylvania Association for Justice, Pennsylvania Bar Association, Bucks County Bar Association, Philadelphia Bar Association and the Philadelphia Trial Lawyers Association, as well as a certified member of the "Million Dollar Advocates Forum". He is also an AARP-approved attorney with the AARP Legal Services Network.

Harry and the law firm also donate a significant amount of time and funds providing legal services to disadvantaged clients who cannot afford an attorney.

Harry's hobbies include fishing, tennis and hoping that the Phillies win the World Series again in his lifetime.

Highest rating (AV Preeminent) for more than 30 years by Martindale-Hubbell.

Named "Pennsylvania Super Lawyer" by Philadelphia Magazine for more than 10 years.

Rated "Superb" by AVVO with a perfect 10/10 score.

Named one of the "Top 100 Trial Lawyers" in Pennsylvania, National Association of Trial Lawyers.

Certified Member, Million Dollar Advocates Forum.

Appointed Special Judge Pro Tempore, Philadelphia Court of Common Pleas.

Appointed Settlement Master, Philadelphia Court of Common Pleas.

Arbitrator, Bucks County Court of Common Pleas.

Eagle Scout Award recipient.

attorneys.bio:
Mark A. Wisniewski was a member of the law firm of Dorian, Goldstein, Wisniewski & Orchinik for over 25 years. He passed away unexpectedly on November 10, 2007 at the young age of 52. Mark had been a managing partner of the firm since 1987. His practice focused mainly in the areas of estates & wills. Throughout his career, Mark donated a substantial amount of his time and expertise to providing free legal services to disadvantaged clients. Following his death, the firm received hundreds of cards and letters from Mark’s clients expressing their appreciation and gratitude for Mark’s help and friendship.

Mark grew up in Montgomery County, Pennsylvania. He graduated from Sacred Heart Parochial School of Swedesburg, Upper Merion Senior High School (Class of 1972), Penn State University (Class of 1976) and Villanova University School of Law (1979). He received the Eagle Scout award in 1970. Mark and his family lived in King of Prussia, where Mark loved working with children and coaching various youth sports in Upper Merion.

Mark was also actively involved with many charitable organizations, and committed a great deal of his time to the Sacred Heart Church of Swedesburg, the Parish Holy Name Society and the Polish Festival Committee. He also was a dedicated Eucharistic Minister at the Sacred Heart Parish Church and at the Basilica of Saints Peters and Paul in Philadelphia. He was a strong advocate for, and provided free services to, Mother Theresa and her Little Sisters of the Poor in Norristown.

Mark was an avid outdoorsman, skilled fisherman and accomplished tennis player. He was very devoted to his wife, Laureen, and their three children: Andrew, Megan and Kate.

After Mark’s passing, many of Mark’s friends and family members commented that Mark was “larger than life”. He will always be deeply missed, but fondly remembered, by all of us here at Dorian Goldstein, as well as by the many clients, friends and family members whose lives he touched.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Eagle Scout Award, 1970 - Present

attorneys.name: Matthew C. Potts
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Easton, PA
attorneys.bio:
Matthew C. Potts joined Steven N. Goudsouzian, LLC in March of 2014. Matthew C. Potts is of counsel to the firm. Matthew C. Potts brings a wealth of experience to the firm especially in the area of criminal defense.

Matthew C. Potts was the founder of the Law Offices of Matthew C. Potts, LLC, a law firm located in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania that specialized in criminal and civil litigation. Mr. Potts is a lifelong resident of the Lehigh Valley. A graduate of Liberty High School and Lehigh University, Mr. Potts obtained his law degree from the Villanova University School of Law. Upon completing law school, Mr. Potts served as Judicial Law Clerk to the Honorable William F. Moran, Administrative Judge for the Northampton County Court of Common Pleas.

Since completing his clerkship in 2001, Mr. Potts maintained an active litigation practice focusing on criminal defense, civil litigation and family law. With over 25 jury trials and countless non-jury trials, Mr. Potts has been one of the most active courtroom practitioners in the Lehigh Valley. Mr. Potts has tried matters ranging from Driving Under the Influence to Criminal Homicide, and he is one of the select few Lehigh Valley lawyers certified under the Pennsylvania Rules of Criminal Procedure to try death penalty cases. Mr. Potts has also handled the appeals of criminal clients in the Superior and Supreme Courts of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania.

In addition to his successful criminal practice, Mr. Potts maintains a significant civil litigation practice handling matters involving contract disputes, personal injury, custody disputes, protection from abuse and municipal law. Mr. Potts has tried countless civil cases and appeared in the Pennsylvania Superior and Commonwealth Court on civil appeals.

Mr. Potts is a member of the Pennsylvania Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, Pennsylvania Bar Association, Northampton County Bar Association and Lehigh County Bar Association. In addition to his private practice he has served as an Assistant Solicitor for the City of Bethlehem and an adjunct professor at the Northampton Community College.

attorneys.name: Feranmi Olugbenga
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Feranmi Olugbenga-Jebutu joined Wilbraham, Lawler, & Buba as an associate attorney in 2025.

In 2018, Ms. Olugbenga-Jebutu graduated from Drexel University with a Bachelor of Science in Psychology and earned a certificate of Intermediate Proficiency in Korean. At Drexel, she was a member of the Pennoni Honors College and received the A.J. Drexel Scholarship.

In 2023, Ms. Olugbenga-Jebutu graduated from Temple University, Beasley School of Law, where she was the recipient of the Beasley Scholarship. While at Temple, she served as a Legal Research and Writing Teaching Assistant for Temple’s International Law students at both Temple’s Main and Shanghai campuses. Furthermore, she was actively involved in student organizations serving as Vice President, Secretary and Treasurer for Temple’s First-Generation Owls, as well as Treasurer of Temple’s International Law Society. Additionally, she interned at Philadelphia Legal Assistance (PLA), assisting indigent homeowners at risk of losing their homes.

In her last year of law school, Ms. Olugbenga-Jebutu was selected as a Temple Global Scholar for Japan. While studying abroad in Japan, Ms. Olugbenga-Jebutu met with both international and domestic attorneys and visited the Japanese Supreme Court, where she engaged in discussion with the Justices.

In her spare time, Ms. Olugbenga-Jebutu enjoys reading, volunteering, watching foreign films and traveling.

attorneys.name: Joyce Novotny
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Greensburg, PA
attorneys.bio:
Joyce Novotny-Prettiman is an associate at the firm. Joyce is a member of the American, Pennsylvania and Westmoreland Bar Associations. After serving as the president of the Westmoreland Bar Association for one year, she currently acts as immediate past president of that organization. She also participates in the following committees of the Westmoreland Bar Association: Civil Litigation and Lawyers Assistance Committee (chair). She is also a member of the Ned J. Nakles American Inn of Court and serves as the immediate past president for the Inn. She has been elected to the Westmoreland Academy of Trial Lawyers and is a member of the Pennsylvania Association for Justice and the Western Pennsylvania Trial Lawyers Association. She is also a member of the Million Dollar Advocates Forum. In regard to alternative dispute resolution matters, she has had mediation training and has been trained in the collaborative law process.

Ms. Novotny-Prettiman earned her B.A. in 1997 from Seton Hill College (summa cum laude) and her law degree from Duquesne University in 2000. She began practicing with the firm after her admission to the practice of law and is currently active in the areas of plaintiff personal injury litigation, long-term disability and general civil litigation.

Ms. Novotny-Prettiman was plaintiff's counsel in the case of Gallagher v. GEICO decided by the Pennsylvania Supreme Court in January 2019 which invalidates the "household exclusion" regularly used by auto insurance carriers to deny underinsured motorist benefits.

Joyce has a unique legal background. She was a legal secretary before obtaining her paralegal certification from St. Vincent College in 1989, and worked in the capacity of legal assistant until her admission into law school. While attending law school, Ms. Novotny-Prettiman worked as a law clerk at QuatriniRafferty.

She is also active in the community and volunteers as a member of the parish council and as a lector at St. Benedict Church. She is a member of the board of directors for Laurel Faith in Action which is devoted to helping residents in the communities of Latrobe, Derry, and Ligonier who are over 60 remain independent in their own homes, with dignity (www.laurelfia.org). She was a volunteer for CASA of Westmoreland from 2010 through 2020 which is an agency that works to give children a voice in the court system when circumstances have placed that child in protective services. She has also been appointed to the Westmoreland County Parks and Recreation Citizens Advisory Board.

A lifelong resident of Unity Township, Joyce currently resides in the Latrobe-Greensburg area with her husband, Daniel. She enjoys spending her free time with her family and friends and loves to practice yoga and to go for a jog to enjoy the outdoors. Summer is her favorite season and she has enjoyed jet skiing and boating for years which pastime grows from the many Sundays her father took her and her sister for boating adventures.

attorneys.name: Harry A. Dorian Jr. (1953
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Bensalem, PA
attorneys.bio:
Harry A. Dorian, Jr. has been practicing law since 1978. He is a graduate of Ohio Northern University School of Law, where he was co-editor of the Ohio Northern University Law Review. In 1975, he graduated with honors from Penn State University with a BA degree in English. He grew up in Montgomery County, graduating from Lower Merion High School in 1971. He was awarded the rank of Eagle Scout in 1970.

Mr. Dorian is a senior managing partner of the firm of Dorian, Goldstein, Wisniewski & Orchinik, P.C. where, for the past 35 years, he has concentrated his practice in the areas of medical malpractice, nursing home negligence, motor vehicle accidents, product liability and other cases involving serious injury or death.

For more than twenty years, he has consistently received the highest possible peer-review rating available ("AV Preeminent") from Martindale-Hubbell for maintaining the highest standards of professional ethics and legal ability. This rating is based upon an extensive peer-review survey of practicing attorneys and judges.

Also, he was recently again named "Pennsylvania Super Lawyer" by Philadelphia Magazine and Law and Politics, based upon a confidential survey of over 39,000 attorneys in Pennsylvania. Only 4% of attorneys in Pennsylvania are awarded the status of a "Pennsylvania Super Lawyer". He has also consistently obtained a rating of "Superb" by Avvo (receiving a perfect 10.0 score), and The National Association of Trial Lawyers has named him one of the "Top 100 Trial Lawyers in Pennsylvania".

He has obtained numerous multi-million dollar recoveries in various types of negligence cases, such as motor vehicle accidents, slip and falls, medical malpractice, nursing home neglect/abuse, dog attacks, premises defects and product liability.

Mr. Dorian has also been appointed a Special Judge Pro Tempore and Settlement Master by the Philadelphia Court of Common Pleas in its Civil Case Management Program. He is also a frequent Arbitrator for the Bucks County Court of Common Pleas.

Mr. Dorian has given lectures to physicians and surgeons on issues related to patient safety and medical malpractice, and he has taught other attorneys at legal seminars involving various areas of the law. Recently, he spoke to hundreds of dentists and dental professionals about oral cancer and dental malpractice at Continuing Dental Education seminars at the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor, and the Temple University School of Dentistry in Philadelphia.

Mr. Dorian has tried numerous cases in both state and federal court in Pennsylvania. He has argued appeals before the Pennsylvania Supreme Court, Pennsylvania Superior Court and the Commonwealth Court of Pennsylvania. He is a long-time member of the American Association for Justice, Pennsylvania Association for Justice, Pennsylvania Bar Association, Bucks County Bar Association, Philadelphia Bar Association and the Philadelphia Trial Lawyers Association, as well as a certified member of the "Million Dollar Advocates Forum". He is also an AARP-approved attorney with the AARP Legal Services Network.

Harry and the law firm also donate a significant amount of time and funds providing legal services to disadvantaged clients who cannot afford an attorney.

Harry's hobbies include fishing, tennis and hoping that the Phillies win the World Series again in his lifetime.

Recently, he spoke to hundreds of dentists and dental professionals about oral cancer and dental malpractice at Continuing Dental Education seminars at the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor, and the Temple University School of Dentistry in Philadelphia.

Mr. Dorian has tried numerous cases in both state and federal court in Pennsylvania. He has argued appeals before the Pennsylvania Supreme Court, Pennsylvania Superior Court and the Commonwealth Court of Pennsylvania. He is a long-time member of the American Association for Justice, Pennsylvania Association for Justice, Pennsylvania Bar Association, Bucks County Bar Association, Philadelphia Bar Association and the Philadelphia Trial Lawyers Association, as well as a certified member of the "Million Dollar Advocates Forum". He is also an AARP-approved attorney with the AARP Legal Services Network.

Harry and the law firm also donate a significant amount of time and funds providing legal services to disadvantaged clients who cannot afford an attorney.

Harry's hobbies include fishing, tennis and hoping that the Phillies win the World Series again in his lifetime.

attorneys.name: Mark A. Wisniewski (1954
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Bensalem, PA
attorneys.bio:
Mark A. Wisniewski was a member of the law firm of Dorian, Goldstein, Wisniewski & Orchinik for over 25 years. He passed away unexpectedly on November 10, 2007 at the young age of 52. Mark had been a managing partner of the firm since 1987. His practice focused mainly in the areas of estates & wills. Throughout his career, Mark donated a substantial amount of his time and expertise to providing free legal services to disadvantaged clients. Following his death, the firm received hundreds of cards and letters from Mark’s clients expressing their appreciation and gratitude for Mark’s help and friendship.

Mark grew up in Montgomery County, Pennsylvania. He graduated from Sacred Heart Parochial School of Swedesburg, Upper Merion Senior High School (Class of 1972), Penn State University (Class of 1976) and Villanova University School of Law (1979). He received the Eagle Scout award in 1970. Mark and his family lived in King of Prussia, where Mark loved working with children and coaching various youth sports in Upper Merion.

Mark was also actively involved with many charitable organizations, and committed a great deal of his time to the Sacred Heart Church of Swedesburg, the Parish Holy Name Society and the Polish Festival Committee. He also was a dedicated Eucharistic Minister at the Sacred Heart Parish Church and at the Basilica of Saints Peters and Paul in Philadelphia. He was a strong advocate for, and provided free services to, Mother Theresa and her Little Sisters of the Poor in Norristown.

Mark was an avid outdoorsman, skilled fisherman and accomplished tennis player. He was very devoted to his wife, Laureen, and their three children: Andrew, Megan and Kate.

After Mark’s passing, many of Mark’s friends and family members commented that Mark was “larger than life”. He will always be deeply missed, but fondly remembered, by all of us here at Dorian Goldstein, as well as by the many clients, friends and family members whose lives he touched.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Eagle Scout Award, 1970 - Present

attorneys.name: Matthew C. Potts
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Easton, PA
attorneys.bio:
Matthew C. Potts joined Steven N. Goudsouzian, LLC in March of 2014. Matthew C. Potts is of counsel to the firm. Matthew C. Potts brings a wealth of experience to the firm especially in the area of criminal defense.

Matthew C. Potts was the founder of the Law Offices of Matthew C. Potts, LLC, a law firm located in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania that specialized in criminal and civil litigation. Mr. Potts is a lifelong resident of the Lehigh Valley. A graduate of Liberty High School and Lehigh University, Mr. Potts obtained his law degree from the Villanova University School of Law. Upon completing law school, Mr. Potts served as Judicial Law Clerk to the Honorable William F. Moran, Administrative Judge for the Northampton County Court of Common Pleas.

Since completing his clerkship in 2001, Mr. Potts maintained an active litigation practice focusing on criminal defense, civil litigation and family law. With over 25 jury trials and countless non-jury trials, Mr. Potts has been one of the most active courtroom practitioners in the Lehigh Valley. Mr. Potts has tried matters ranging from Driving Under the Influence to Criminal Homicide, and he is one of the select few Lehigh Valley lawyers certified under the Pennsylvania Rules of Criminal Procedure to try death penalty cases. Mr. Potts has also handled the appeals of criminal clients in the Superior and Supreme Courts of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania.

In addition to his successful criminal practice, Mr. Potts maintains a significant civil litigation practice handling matters involving contract disputes, personal injury, custody disputes, protection from abuse and municipal law. Mr. Potts has tried countless civil cases and appeared in the Pennsylvania Superior and Commonwealth Court on civil appeals.

Mr. Potts is a member of the Pennsylvania Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, Pennsylvania Bar Association, Northampton County Bar Association and Lehigh County Bar Association. In addition to his private practice he has served as an Assistant Solicitor for the City of Bethlehem and an adjunct professor at the Northampton Community College.

Jeffrey L. Naftulin retired in 2016 and practiced law in Pennsylvania from 1970-2015. He successfully represented people who were seriously injured as a result of injuries caused by: drunk drivers; power companies; manufacturers; tractor trailer operators; motorists (including uninsured motorists); companies and persons who created hazardous working conditions; hazardous constructions sites; and hit & run drivers.

attorneys.name: William H. Nam
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Litigation Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Billy focuses on what is best for his client and offers advice based on his history as a risk management consultant. He is a part of the Complex Litigation team where he handles commercial transactions, real estate litigation, and regulatory disputes. He is a storyteller in the courtroom and loves to see cases through to trial.

Billy earned his Bachelor of Business Administration with honors from Temple University in 2018 and received a dual degree in Human Resource Management and Risk Management and Insurance. In his final year, his team participated in the annual Gamma Iota Sigma Case Competition where his team won best overall presentation, and he earned the best individual presenter award. He worked at a Marsh and McLennan Agency as an Underwriting Consultant before entering law school. He earned his law degree from Temple University Beasley School of Law as an evening student while working full-time during the day. He served as the Student Bar Association President during his last year.

Billy spent his last two years of law school clerking for the Honorable Edward C. Wright in the First Judicial District of Pennsylvania. His clerkship gave him firsthand experience watching hundreds of Landlord-Tenant Appeals, L&I Code Violation Appeals, and PennDOT Appeals per month. This experience has helped him learn the rules of Pennsylvania appellate procedure and is a major reason why he loves to be in court. Billy is admitted to practice in Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and Maryland.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injuries Lawyers in Fairview, PA
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Alan Natalie has been practicing in as a solo-practice attorney and serving as Assistant Public Defender in Erie County, Pennsylvania, since 1989. In his solo practice, he focuses in the areas of:

• Civil litigation

• Criminal defense

• Estate law, including litigation, planning and administration

In addition to his law practice, Attorney Natalie serves as managing partner of 21st Century Erie Development Partnership, LLC, responsible for the historical restoration, redevelopment, and management of commercial property in downtown Erie. He is also an adjunct instructor of legal studies for Gannon University. He also takes an active role in community affairs through extensive volunteer positions for numerous civic and professional organizations in Erie County.

Over the course of his distinguished career, he has assumed leadership positions in the Erie County Bar Association, including Board of Directors Member, Young Lawyers Division Chair, and Civil Practice Section Chair.

Attorney Natalie is the son of a high-ranking police officer for the City of Erie, where he learned the respect for rule of law. His upbringing has led to personal philosophy that everyone deserves to be treated with dignity and respect, while afforded the legal rights provided by our Constitution. This often means zealously representing clients and serving the cause of justice in cases which may not be politically popular in the community.

He has been married for twenty-one years to wife, Suzanne, and is the father of three children, Angelina, Melania, and Giovanni.

attorneys.name: Lance J. Nelson
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in West Chester, PA
attorneys.bio:
Lance Nelson, chair of MacElree Harvey, Ltd.'s family law practice, has over 25 years of experience representing clients in family law matters such as divorce, marital agreements, adoption, custody, and support. For his business clients, Lance advises on a variety of legal issues, including contract disputes, construction issues, corporate control issues and other aspects of day-to-day business disputes.

Since joining MacElree Harvey in 1992, Lance was named a shareholder in 1998 and served as the Managing Partner from 2001 to 2011.

Notable Representations

Successfully represented in a non-jury trial a non-profit organization to resolve certain corporate governance issues that were raised by a dissident group of members.

Counseled a father with a significant interest in a family-owned business. Worked with client and client's spouse's counsel to resolve issues related to the value of the family-owned business, the division of the marital property, an equally shared custody arrangement and ongoing support obligations without resorting to any court intervention.

Worked with a mother whose husband owned a substantial business. Through many court hearings in the litigation process, successfully resolved for this mother all of the issues related to the value of the husband's business, a custody schedule, appropriate support payments and the division of the marital property.

Counseled children who own significant portions of multigeneration family-owned business through the prenuptial process. Helped young man navigate an already stressful pre-wedding situation and address the consequences of his ownership in a multi-million dollar family business without injecting more stress with his fiance.

Represented a professional service firm through the arbitration process when a former owner left taking many clients with him. Through the arbitration, successfully secured for the majority owner enforcement of certain financial and other obligations of the departing shareholder.

After a multi-day non-jury trial, successfully secured a substantial judgment for a custom builder that included not only sums that were due under the contract, but lost profits.

attorneys.bio:
Matthew Ness is a dedicated criminal defense attorney and DUI lawyer serving clients in Pittsburgh and across Western Pennsylvania. He is passionate about protecting the constitutional rights of individuals accused of crimes, emphasizing the freedoms guaranteed under both the U.S. Constitution and Pennsylvania’s Bill of Rights. Ness believes that every client deserves a fair trial and just treatment, and he brings this commitment to every case he handles.

With a strong background as a public defender in Allegheny County, Ness has extensive trial experience with complex felony cases, including attempted homicide, rape, child sexual abuse, robbery, drug possession, and firearms charges. He combines his deep understanding of criminal law with compassionate, client-focused guidance, ensuring that clients are informed and empowered throughout the legal process.

Matthew Ness joined Worgul, Sarna & Ness, Criminal Defense Attorneys, LLC to provide clients with individualized attention and a supportive environment while vigorously defending their rights. He handles a wide range of criminal matters, including DUI, drug charges, and other criminal defense cases, representing clients throughout Allegheny, Beaver, Butler, Westmoreland, Washington, Fayette counties, and surrounding regions.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Mt. Lebanon, PA
attorneys.bio:
Ailis S. Nerad, Esquire, is a Junior Associate focusing on Family Law, where she helps clients through all stages of family law matters, including divorce, custody, and support. Before joining the firm as a junior associate, Attorney Nerad spent two years clerking with the firm, gaining valuable experience working alongside the team and supporting clients through some of life’s most personal challenges.

Attorney Nerad loves working in family law because it’s all about people—their stories, their struggles, and their hopes for the future. Every case is different, but at the heart of it all is helping someone find clarity and stability during what can be a really emotional time. Attorney Nerad does what she can to make a real difference for families and help them move forward with confidence and peace of mind.

When Attorney Nerad is not advocating for her clients, she enjoys spending quality time with her friends and family. An avid lover of the outdoors, she often spends her weekends hiking local trails with her puppy and exploring new destinations. She also enjoys experimenting with new recipes in the kitchen and cultivating her garden. In her free time, Attorney Nerad can often be found reading, staying active, and finding balance through a variety of recreational activities that keep her energized both personally and professionally.

attorneys.name: Darth M. Newman
attorneys.firm_name: Law Offices of Darth M. Newman LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
Darth is a skilled trial attorney with more than a decade of litigation experience in complex commercial and plaintiff's side whistleblower cases. He has tried shareholder disputes, fraud, insider dealing, and fiduciary duty matters worth millions of dollars. He has also represented whistleblowers from across the country helping to shed light on all manner of fraud against the government from dangerous healthcare systems, devices, and doctors to government contracting and loan fraud.

Darth's trial experience includes a federal jury trial, a Delaware Chancery Court trial, and a range of other state court trials and arbitrations. He has briefed and argued motions and appeals in various federal and state courts and helped secure an en banc Federal Circuit decision striking down a portion of the Lanham Act as unconstitutional; that decision was later unanimously affirmed by the United States Supreme Court. Darth is also a skilled negotiator with a lengthy record of resolving otherwise intractable disputes short of trial.

An active member of the Allegheny County Bar Association, Darth is the current Chair of the Professional Ethics Committee and Member of the Federal Court Section. Nationally, he is a member of Taxpayers Against Fraud, a public interest non-profit organization dedicated to fighting fraud against the government. Darth was a soccer referee long before he was a lawyer. He has officiated around the country, is still a referee and referee coach/mentor, and now serves as the Western Pennsylvania State Youth Referee Administrator and an ex-officio member of the Pennsylvania West Soccer Association Youth Board.

Before opening his own firm, Darth worked at national and regional firms and helped start two litigation boutiques.

He has briefed and argued motions and appeals in various federal and state courts and helped secure an en banc Federal Circuit decision striking down a portion of the Lanham Act as unconstitutional; that decision was later unanimously affirmed by the United States Supreme Court. Darth is also a skilled negotiator with a lengthy record of resolving otherwise intractable disputes short of trial.

An active member of the Allegheny County Bar Association, Darth is the current Chair of the Professional Ethics Committee and Member of the Federal Court Section. Nationally, he is a member of Taxpayers Against Fraud, a public interest non-profit organization dedicated to fighting fraud against the government. Darth was a soccer referee long before he was a lawyer. He has officiated around the country, is still a referee and referee coach/mentor, and now serves as the Western Pennsylvania State Youth Referee Administrator and an ex-officio member of the Pennsylvania West Soccer Association Youth Board.

Before opening his own firm, Darth worked at national and regional firms and helped start two litigation boutiques.

attorneys.name: Carmen Nocera
attorneys.practice_type: Medical malpractice Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
Carmen J. Nocera is an associate attorney at Harry S. Cohen and Associates, where he focuses his practice on representing victims of medical malpractice. Mr. Nocera has spent his career representing injury victims in personal injury and workers’ compensation matters throughout the Commonwealth and takes great pride in obtaining justice for his clients.

Mr. Nocera is a 2015 graduate of Slippery Rock University, where he received a degree in Safety Management and was a member of the university’s baseball team. Prior to law school, Mr. Nocera worked as an environmental health and safety consultant in the construction industry.

Mr. Nocera earned his law degree from the University of Pittsburgh School of Law in 2019. During law school, Mr. Nocera was an accomplished member of the Mock Trial Team, as well as Chair of the Moot Court Board.

Since 2023, Carmen has been voted by his peers as a Pennsylvania Super Lawyers Rising Star, an honor reserved to the top 2.5% of attorneys in Pennsylvania who are under the age of 40 or who have been practicing for less than 10 years. Mr. Nocera was also selected for membership to the National Trial Lawyers Top 40 Under 40.

In May of 2025, Mr. Nocera was co-counsel on a case that secured a $5.25 million verdict in Allegheny County in a case involving the wrongful death of a woman whose lung was perforated during a diagnostic bronchoscopy, a condition that went undiagnosed and untreated.

Mr. Nocera is an active member of the Pittsburgh legal community. He is on the Board of Governors of both the Western Pennsylvania Trial Lawyers Association (WPTLA) and the Pennsylvania Association for Justice (PAJ). In addition, Mr. Nocera coaches mock trial at the University of Pittsburgh School of Law.

Mr. Nocera resides in the city of Pittsburgh and enjoys golfing, cooking, and spending time with his dog, Oliver.

attorneys.name: Alex B. Norman
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Alex B. Norman is a trial lawyer representing individuals who have suffered brain and spinal cord injuries in car and commercial truck crashes. Driving a motor vehicle on the road is a privilege. When someone abuses that privilege, they have to be held to account for all of the harm that they cause.

Alex's personal history inspires his passion for seeking full justice for the people. Born and raised in Berks County, Pennsylvania, he is a graduate of Temple University and Temple University James E. Beasley School of Law. Following law school, Alex worked for insurance defense firms for more than a decade. He represented insurance companies, insurance policy holders, and Fortune 500 companies in personal injury cases in Pennsylvania and New Jersey. He saw first hand how insurance companies treat injured people. Prior to joining Morgan & Morgan he worked at a boutique trial litigation firm in Center City representing folks who suffered catastrophic injuries from reckless drivers, defective products, unsafe properties, and inadequate security.

Alex is invested in the community. He volunteers with local youth organizations which allows him to hone his communication skills and inspire youngsters to have grit and self-determination. He is also an active member of the Greater Philadelphia YMCA, NJ Development Board. He supports the Brain Injury Association of American and the state branches in Pennsylvania and New Jersey.

attorneys.name: Joyce Novotny
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Greensburg, PA
attorneys.bio:
Joyce Novotny-Prettiman is an associate at the firm. Joyce is a member of the American, Pennsylvania and Westmoreland Bar Associations. After serving as the president of the Westmoreland Bar Association for one year, she currently acts as immediate past president of that organization. She also participates in the following committees of the Westmoreland Bar Association: Civil Litigation and Lawyers Assistance Committee (chair). She is also a member of the Ned J. Nakles American Inn of Court and serves as the immediate past president for the Inn. She has been elected to the Westmoreland Academy of Trial Lawyers and is a member of the Pennsylvania Association for Justice and the Western Pennsylvania Trial Lawyers Association. She is also a member of the Million Dollar Advocates Forum. In regard to alternative dispute resolution matters, she has had mediation training and has been trained in the collaborative law process.

Ms. Novotny-Prettiman earned her B.A. in 1997 from Seton Hill College (summa cum laude) and her law degree from Duquesne University in 2000. She began practicing with the firm after her admission to the practice of law and is currently active in the areas of plaintiff personal injury litigation, long-term disability and general civil litigation.

Ms. Novotny-Prettiman was plaintiff's counsel in the case of Gallagher v. GEICO decided by the Pennsylvania Supreme Court in January 2019 which invalidates the "household exclusion" regularly used by auto insurance carriers to deny underinsured motorist benefits.

Joyce has a unique legal background. She was a legal secretary before obtaining her paralegal certification from St. Vincent College in 1989, and worked in the capacity of legal assistant until her admission into law school. While attending law school, Ms. Novotny-Prettiman worked as a law clerk at QuatriniRafferty.

She is also active in the community and volunteers as a member of the parish council and as a lector at St. Benedict Church. She is a member of the board of directors for Laurel Faith in Action which is devoted to helping residents in the communities of Latrobe, Derry, and Ligonier who are over 60 remain independent in their own homes, with dignity (www.laurelfia.org). She was a volunteer for CASA of Westmoreland from 2010 through 2020 which is an agency that works to give children a voice in the court system when circumstances have placed that child in protective services. She has also been appointed to the Westmoreland County Parks and Recreation Citizens Advisory Board.

A lifelong resident of Unity Township, Joyce currently resides in the Latrobe-Greensburg area with her husband, Daniel. She enjoys spending her free time with her family and friends and loves to practice yoga and to go for a jog to enjoy the outdoors. Summer is her favorite season and she has enjoyed jet skiing and boating for years which pastime grows from the many Sundays her father took her and her sister for boating adventures.

attorneys.name: Kevin P. O'Brien
attorneys.practice_type: Automobile and Trucking Accidents Lawyers in Cheltenham, PA
attorneys.bio:
Kevin is a partner at Stampone O’Brien Dilsheimer Holloway where he focuses his practice on catastrophic personal injury and wrongful death claims. Kevin is an active trial lawyer and is routinely sought out by colleagues as trial approaches to become involved as lead trial counsel.

Kevin’s practice has involved all different types of catastrophic injury cases including product liability, trucking injury cases, medical malpractice, workplace injury, premises liability, civil rights, and institutional physical and sexual abuse cases. He is one of the leading attorneys in the Country on behalf of infants who have died from asphyxia and suffocation in the “Infant Inclined Sleeping Products” and individuals who have suffered scalding and burn injuries from defective pressure cookers, both of which have been recalled by the CPSC.

Kevin has secured some of the largest verdicts and settlements in Pennsylvania and New Jersey history, including a $55 million verdict for a pedestrian who suffered bilateral leg amputations after being struck by a truck—believed to be the largest verdict ever in Essex County, New Jersey. His results also include multiple eight-figure settlements and verdicts, including recoveries of $40 million, $33 million, $20 million, $18.5 million, and numerous other seven- and eight-figure outcomes across product liability, trucking, construction, and wrongful death cases. attorneys.name: Michael J. O'Neill
attorneys.practice_type: National Trial Practice Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Mr. O'Neill is a litigator whose diversified civil practice includes commercial disputes as well as employment and tort litigation matters. Mr. O'Neill's practice is national in focus. He has successfully litigated many complex seven- and eight-figure disputes on behalf of national and international manufacturers and employers in a wide variety of commercial, product liability, toxic tort and employment disputes in both state and federal courts all over the country. Most recently, his practice has focused on defending catastrophic injury product liability and trucking cases, as well as advising clients concerning risk management and litigation issues. He has handled catastrophic product liability and transportation claims all over the United States, including Alabama, Arizona, California, Georgia, Illinois, Indiana, Kansas, Kentucky, Maryland, Nevada, New Jersey, New York, Oregon, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Texas, Utah, Virginia, Washington and West Virginia.

Mr. O'Neill is admitted to practice and has litigated in New York, New Jersey and Pennsylvania, and before the U.S. District Courts for the Eastern, Middle and Western Districts of Pennsylvania, the Northern District of Texas and the District of New Jersey. He is a member of the Defense Research Institute and is active in the Institute's Aerospace, Construction, Product Liability and Trucking Law Committees as well as its Young Lawyers Committee.

Mr. O'Neill also has a long history of practical aviation experience beginning with his attaining his civilian aviation license (fixed-wing, single engine) in 1988. During college Mr. O'Neill enlisted in the Pennsylvania National Guard and attended Basic Training and Advanced Individual Training at Ft. Rucker, Georgia where he was an honor graduate. Prior to completion of his undergraduate degree, Mr. O'Neill graduated from U.S. Army Officer Candidate School with honors and was commissioned as a 2nd Lieutenant. Mr. O'Neill was among the very few Army National Guard officers from across the country to be selected to attend U.S. Army Aviation and Warfighting Center at Ft. Rucker, Alabama where he graduated in 1995 with honors. Mr. O'Neill successfully completed Aircraft Qualification Courses for the UH-1, OH-6, OH-58 and AH-1 helicopters and holds a civilian commercial rotary-wing license with an instrument rating.

Mr. O'Neill attained his undergraduate degree from the University of Scranton. After graduating from the U.S. Army Aviation and Warfighting Center in 1995, he attended Villanova University School of Law in Villanova, Pennsylvania where he received his J.D. in 1998.

Since 2005, Mr. O'Neill has held an adjunct position teaching trial advocacy at his alma mater, Villanova University School of Law. Mr. O'Neill has also served as a member of the Temple American Inn of Court. Currently, he is a member of the Young Friends Committee of Lankenau Hospital and the Young Friends of the Philadelphia Antique Show.

Attorney Fatih Oguz is licensed to practice in Pennsylvania and in Turkey. Mr. Oguz received his Bachelor of Laws degree from Istanbul University Faculty of Law. After being admitted to practice law in Pennsylvania in 2021, he has started his law practice in Karen Ann Ulmer, P.C. focusing on Family Law, Estates and Property Law.

Mr. Oguz is fluent both in English and Turkish languages.

attorneys.name: Douglas J. Olcott
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Pittsburgh, PA
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Doug Olcott focuses his practice on Personal Injury, Work Accidents, Medical Malpractice, Hepatitis C Exposure, Legal Malpractice and Social Security Disability in Pennsylvania and New Jersey. He has been selected by Pennsylvania Super Lawyers as one of the top 5% of lawyers in Pennsylvania since 2012. Since 2014, he has been listed as one of the Top 50 Super Lawyers in Pittsburgh and one of the Top 100 Super Lawyers in Pennsylvania. He is a lifetime member of both the Million Dollar Advocates Forum and the Multi-Million Dollar Advocate Forum, a select group of attorneys who have won a plaintiff verdict or settlement of over at least two million dollars.

In 2013, a 2.2 Million Dollar total settlement was reached for an 81-year-old man who was killed, and his 53-year-old son who suffered a closed head injury, as the result of a serious car collision. In addition, he settled a 1.3 Million Dollar product liability case for a Pulaski man who fell 40 feet while working on a cellular tower in October of 2013.

In 2012, Doug made headlines after winning a jury trial in Beaver County where a man was awarded 2.8 Million Dollars in damages and delay damages for injuries he sustained in a 2003 car accident. That verdict was one of the largest in Beaver County's history for a plaintiff injured in a car accident.

A magna cum laude graduate of Seton Hall University School of Law, Doug has been licensed to practice since 1990. He is licensed to practice law in both Pennsylvania and New Jersey. While practicing law in New Jersey he was a Certified Civil Trial Attorney by the Supreme Court of New Jersey. After practicing law in New Jersey for seventeen years, Doug moved to New Castle to join Dallas W. Hartman, PC., where he has handled hundreds of cases over the last five years. He is a member of the Pennsylvania Association for Justice, Pennsylvania Bar Association, Western Pennsylvania Trial Lawyers Association and Lawrence County Bar Association.

attorneys.name: Nathan Orians
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Philadelphia, PA
attorneys.bio:
Witnessing the abuse of children at a juvenile detention center convinced Nathan Orians to switch his career from social work to one in which he could help not only children but improve the system - the law.

The first-hand observation of child abuse by Orians, who also holds a master's degree in social work, while an employee at the Delaware County Juvenile Detention Center convinced him to blow the whistle on what Fox News later called "shocking revelations" of what occurred at the facility.

The disclosure prompted an investigation into the detention center by the public defender and state legislators, with Fox News noting a judge subsequently ordered its closure. Pennsylvania Attorney General Josh Shapiro was investigating the matter further.

"The systemic abuses I witnessed and repeatedly attempted to stop forced me to reconsider my entire career path and go to law school," Orians said in an interview with Fox News about the detention center. "The people in charge purposely place children into a dangerous facility and they turned a blind eye or even covered up abuse that was ongoing for years."

Now, as an attorney, Orians concentrates in child sexual and physical abuse cases, while also handling catastrophic personal injury litigation. For two years prior, Orians worked as a law clerk at the firm, focusing primarily on sexual abuse, catastrophic injury, Title IX violations and medical malpractice cases.

In his tenure as a social worker, Orians held a number of positions, including as a clinical case manager at the juvenile detention center, counseling individuals, couples and families in therapy sessions at Bard College, performing psychodynamic/trauma assessments as a case manager intern, and wrote grants for programs helping at-risk youths stay in school at the R.E.A.L. Skills Network in Poughkeepsie, N.Y.

Orians earned his bachelor's degree at Vassar College and his master's degree at Smith College School for Social work.

He earned his law degree at the Thomas R. Kline School of Law, where he graduated cum laude, was associate editor and a board member of the Law Review, was awarded best student honors for Trial Advocacy and in Depositions, won the American Law Institute CLE Scholarship & Leadership Award, and numerous other academic awards.

Orians was also awarded Pro Bono Honors at the law school, partly for his work helping expose the abuse at the juvenile detention center.
